[signaltometricsconnector] Add error_mode configuration to handle OTTL evaluation errors (#46005)

Fixes
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/45746

This change adds an error_mode configuration option to the
signaltometrics connector to control how OTTL evaluation errors are
handled. Previously, a single bad record would cause the entire batch to
fail and be dropped.

Changes:
- Add error_mode field to Config with three modes: propagate, ignore,
silent
- propagate (default): Returns error, entire batch fails (backward
compatible)
- ignore: Logs error, skips bad record, continues processing valid
records
- silent: Skips bad record silently, continues processing valid records
- Update aggregator to handle errors based on configured error_mode
- Add comprehensive tests for all three error modes
- Update README with error handling documentation

[chore][hostmetricsreceiver] Fix example config: uptime scraper renamed to system (#46149)

#### Description

The hostmetricsreceiver `uptime` scraper was renamed to system awhile
ago, see #36123 . However, the sample config was never updated to match
this, if the users uses `uptime` in their config the collector will not
run as the `uptime` scraper is no longer present, this scraper has been
renamed to system.

#### Using uptime

##### Config

```yaml
extensions:
  zpages:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:55679

receivers:
  hostmetrics:
    collection_interval: 1m
    scrapers:
      ...
      uptime:

exporters:
  debug:
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889

service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [hostmetrics]
      exporters: [prometheus, debug]

  extensions: [zpages]
```

##### Output

```bash
opentelemetry-collector-contrib main  ✗ make run otelcontribcol
cd ./cmd/otelcontribcol && GO111MODULE=on go run --race . --config ../../local/config.yaml
Error: failed to get config: cannot unmarshal the configuration: decoding failed due to the following error(s):

'receivers' error reading configuration for "hostmetrics": '' invalid scraper key: uptime
exit status 1
make: *** [Makefile:359: run] Error 1
```

#### Fix

Use `system` instead of uptime, this is only an issue with the
[example-config.yaml](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/receiver/hostmetricsreceiver/example_config.yaml?plain=1#L18)
for hostmetrics, this work just renames `uptime` to `system`.

### Release Notes

###
[`v4.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v4.4.0)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/compare/v4.3.0...v4.4.0)

- Micro-optimize `Map` for integer keys
[#​185](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/185)
- Add `Map.RangeRelaxed` method for faster map iteration
[#​187](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/187)
- Add `Map.DeleteMatching` method for batch entry deletion
[#​186](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/186)

Read-heavy operations on `Map` with integer keys are now 24-29% faster
due to a more efficient hash function, as well as a number of
micro-optimizations.

`RangeRelaxed` is a much faster (\~11x), lock-free alternative to
`Range`. The downside is that the same key may be visited by
`RangeRelaxed` more than once if it is concurrently deleted and
re-inserted during the iteration. `RangeRelaxed` should be preferred
over `Range` in all cases when weaker consistency is acceptable.

```go
m := xsync.NewMap[string, int]()
m.Store("alice", 10)
m.Store("bob", 20)
m.Store("carol", 30)
m.Store("dave", 40)

// Iterate map entries and calculate sum of all values.
sum := 0
m.RangeRelaxed(func(key string, value int) bool {
	sum += value
	return true // continue iteration
})
```

`DeleteMatching` deletes all entries for which the delete return value
of the input function is true. If the cancel return value is true, the
iteration stops immediately. The function returns the number of deleted
entries. The call locks a hash table bucket for the duration of
evaluating the function for all entries in the bucket and performing
deletions. It performs up to 20% faster than `Range` + `Delete`, yet if
the percentage of the entries to-be-deleted is low, `RangeRelaxed` +
`Delete` combination should be more efficient.

```go
// Delete entries with value greater than 25.
deleted := m.DeleteMatching(func(key string, value int) (delete, cancel bool) {
	return value > 25, false
})
```

###
[`v4.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v4.3.0)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/compare/v4.2.0...v4.3.0)

- Add iterator function `Map.All`
[#​181](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/181)
- Make shrink resize lock-free on target buckets
[#​180](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/180)

`All` is similar to `Range`, but returns an `iter.Seq2`, so is
compatible with Go 1.23+ iterators. All of the same caveats and behavior
from `Range` apply to `All`.

```golang
m := xsync.NewMap[string, int]()
for i := range 100 {
  m.Store(strconv.Itoa(i), i)
}

// Will print all of the map entries
for key, val := range m.All() {
  fmt.Printf("m[%q] = %q\n")
}
```

Kudos to [@​llxisdsh](https://redirect.github.com/llxisdsh) and
[@​moskyb](https://redirect.github.com/moskyb) for making this
release happen.

###
[`v4.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v4.2.0)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/compare/v4.1.0...v4.2.0)

- Cooperative parallel rehashing in `Map`
[#​178](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/178)
- Use `runtime.cheaprand` instead of `fastrand`
[#​177](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/177)

Introduces cooperative rehashing for `xsync.Map` this means that
goroutines that execute write operations, such as `Compute` or `Store`,
may participate in table rehashing when the hash table grows or shrinks.
From now on, table rehashing never spawns additional goroutines.

This behavior is always enabled, so the `WithSerialResize` function is
now marked as deprecated and acts as a no-op.

###
[`v4.1.0`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v4.1.0)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/compare/v4.0.0...v4.1.0)

- New data structure: `UMPSCQueue`
[#​168](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/168)
- Speed up `LoadAndDelete` and `Delete` in case of non-existing `Map`
key
[#​167](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/167)
- Parallel `Map` resize
[#​170](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/170)

`UMPSCQueue` is meant to serve as a replacement for a channel. However,
crucially, it has infinite capacity. This is a very bad idea in many
cases as it means that it never exhibits backpressure. In other words,
if nothing is consuming elements from the queue, it will eventually
consume all available memory and crash the process. However, there are
also cases where this is desired behavior as it means the queue will
dynamically allocate more memory to store temporary bursts, allowing
producers to never block while the consumer catches up.

From now on, `Map` spawns additional goroutines to speed up resizing the
hash table. This can be disabled when creating a `Map` with the new
`WithSerialResize` setting:

```go
m := xsync.NewMap[int, int](xsync.WithSerialResize())
// resize will take place on the current goroutine only
for i := 0; i < 10000; i++ {
	m.Store(i, i)
}
```

Thanks [@​PapaCharlie](https://redirect.github.com/PapaCharlie)
and [@​llxisdsh](https://redirect.github.com/llxisdsh) for the
contributions!

###
[`v4.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v4.0.0)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/compare/v3.5.1...v4.0.0)

- Minimal Golang version is now 1.24.
- All non-generic data structures are now removed. Generic versions
should be used instead - they use the old names, but type aliases are
present to simplify v3-to-v4 code migration.
- `MapOf`'s hasher API is gone. The default and only hash function is
now based on `maphash.Comparable`.
- `Map`'s `Compute` API now supports no-op (cancel) compute operation.

Thanks [@​PapaCharlie](https://redirect.github.com/PapaCharlie)
for making this release happen

##### Migration notes

- The old `*Of` types are kept as type aliases for the renamed data
structures to simplify the migration, e.g. `MapOf` is an alias for
`Map`.
- `NewMapOfPresized` function is gone. `NewMap` combined with
`WithPresize` should be used instead.
- `Map.Compute` method now expects `valueFn` to return a `ComputeOp`
value instead of a boolean flag. That's to support compute operation
cancellation, so that the call does nothing.
- `Map.LoadOrTryCompute` method is renamed to `LoadOrCompute`. The old
`LoadOrCompute` method is removed as it was redundant.

[chore] Fix mdatagen generator issues with oracle cloud RDP (#46006)

## Description

The Oracle Cloud Resource Detection Processor (RDP) relies on the
`mdatagen` tool to generate code and config files from a source
`metadata.yaml` file. This is part of how this RDP initially came to
life.

At some point in the past few months, something changed with this
process, and `mdatagen` experiences errors when attempting to regenerate
the files for the Oracle Cloud Resource Detection Processor. This in
turn is blocking efforts to:

1. Add a new `realm` attribute to the RDP:
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/45890
2. Update the CODEOWNERS file to add myself as a code owner. 

Rather than fixing the underlying issues as "ride along" issues
unrelated to the above 2 items, I'm breaking this out into a separate
chore PR for clarity.

### Fix 1: Removing `parent` declaration

With the previous `parent: resourcedetectionprocessor` declaration that
used to work in `metadata.yaml`, I was now getting this error when I
tried to run `mdatagen metadata.yaml`:

```
status must be empty for subcomponents
````

Just as @paulojmdias discovered in [a similar
PR](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/44424)

...it was now required to remove that parent declaration, and also to
change the format of the `type` from:

```
type: resourcedetectionprocessor/oraclecloud
```

...to:

```
type: oracleclouddetector
```

This matches many of the other detectors like Azure, DigitalOcean,
Dynatrace, etc. I've followed suit by making similar changes in this PR,
and now `mdatagen` cleanly generates files.

### Fix 2: `NewFactory` code generation error

After making the above changes I was getting this error:

```
Error: ./generated_component_test.go:16:24: undefined: NewFactory 
```

in a newly-generated test file:
`processor/resourcedetectionprocessor/internal/oraclecloud/generated_component_test.go`

I got some help from @paulojmdias on Slack who gave me this fix:

> Please copy this
[file](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/processor/resourcedetectionprocessor/internal/azure/metadata.go)
to oraclecloud folder (and ofc rename the package name) there and run
make generate fmt lint test, and push the changes.

Once I did that, the compilation error went away.  

I also copied the convention used by many other RDPs, including azure,
to include this in the `metadata.yaml`:

```
tests:
  skip_lifecycle: true

[processor/redaction] Add HMAC support for GDPR compliance (#45715)

#### Description

This PR adds HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) hash
functions (`hmac-sha256` and `hmac-sha512`) to the redaction processor,
enabling GDPR-compliant pseudonymization of sensitive data such as IP
addresses in telemetry data.

**Problem:**
The current redaction processor supports simple hash functions (MD5,
SHA1, SHA3), which are vulnerable to rainbow table attacks for
low-entropy data like IP addresses. IPv4 has only ~4.3 billion possible
values (2^32), making it feasible to pre-compute all possible hashes and
reverse them. This violates GDPR Article 4(5) requirements for true
pseudonymization.

**Solution:**
HMAC addresses this security gap by requiring a secret key, making it
practically impossible to reverse-engineer original values without the
key while maintaining consistency (same input + same key = same output)
required for pattern analysis.

**Changes:**

- **config.go**: Added `HMACSHA256` and `HMACSHA512` hash function
types, `HMACKey` configuration field
- **processor.go**: Implemented HMAC hashing logic with `hashStringHMAC`
helper function
- **processor_test.go**: Added 4 comprehensive test cases for HMAC
functionality
- **README.md**: Added comprehensive HMAC documentation including
security considerations and key management

**Usage Example:**

```yaml
processors:
  redaction:
    allow_all_keys: true
    blocked_values:
      - "(?:[0-9]{1,3}\\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}"  # IPv4 addresses
    hash_function: hmac-sha256  # or hmac-sha512
    hmac_key: "${env:REDACTION_SECRET_KEY}"
    summary: silent
```

```bash
# Key generation
export REDACTION_SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
```

#### Link to tracking issue

N/A - This is a new feature addition for GDPR compliance. No existing
issue tracking this enhancement.

#### Testing

Added 4 comprehensive unit tests covering:
- HMAC-SHA256 basic functionality
- HMAC-SHA512 basic functionality
- Hash consistency (same input + same key = same output)
- Different keys produce different hashes

All new tests and existing tests pass successfully:
```bash
=== RUN   TestRedactSummaryDebugHashHMACSHA256
--- PASS: TestRedactSummaryDebugHashHMACSHA256 (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestRedactSummaryDebugHashHMACSHA512
--- PASS: TestRedactSummaryDebugHashHMACSHA512 (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestHMACConsistency
--- PASS: TestHMACConsistency (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestHMACDifferentKeys
--- PASS: TestHMACDifferentKeys (0.00s)
PASS
ok  	github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/processor/redactionprocessor	0.255s
```

**Manual testing:**
- Built and verified binary includes HMAC functions
- Tested HMAC-SHA256 and HMAC-SHA512 with sample configurations
- Verified consistent output with same key
- Verified different output with different keys

#### Documentation

Updated `processor/redactionprocessor/README.md` with:
- Complete HMAC section explaining security advantages over simple hash
functions
- Configuration examples for both `hmac-sha256` and `hmac-sha512`
- Key generation and management best practices
- GDPR Article 4(5) compliance explanation
- Security recommendations for production use
- Performance impact notes

**Key Benefits:**
- ✅ Rainbow table resistant (pre-computed hash tables are useless
without the key)
- ✅ GDPR compliant (meets pseudonymization requirements per Article
4(5))
- ✅ Backward compatible (existing configurations continue to work)
- ✅ Consistent output (same input with same key = same hash, enabling
analytics)
- ✅ Minimal performance overhead (~2x slower than MD5, negligible in
most deployments)

**Security Considerations:**
- HMAC-SHA256 recommended for most use cases
- Keys should be at least 256 bits (32 bytes)
- Keys must be stored separately from log data (e.g., Kubernetes
Secrets, Vault)
- Regular key rotation recommended per security policy

**References:**

- [RFC 2104: HMAC](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2104)
- [GDPR Article 4(5):
Pseudonymisation](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/)
- [NIST FIPS 198-1: HMAC
Standard](https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/detail/fips/198/1/final)

Add `service.instance.id` resource attribute to the MongoDB receiver
following the pattern established in the PostgreSQL receiver PR #45345.

- `service.instance.id` is a deterministic UUID v5 derived from
`serverAddress:serverPort`.

As discussed, and requested initially by @lmolkova, I'm also moving the
`database` resource attribute to a metric attribute. This makes more
sense modeling wise, and also removes the database from the set of
identifying resource attributes, meaning there will only be one resource
per database server.

The motivation for adding `service.instance.id` is to fix OTLP interop
with Prometheus, which depends on the identifying OTel [service
attribute semantic
conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/service/)
triplet (`service.namespace`, `service.name`, `service.instance.id`) to
successfully convert OTLP resource attributes (as per the [OTLP Metric
Points to Prometheus
spec](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/compatibility/prometheus_and_openmetrics/#resource-attributes-1)).

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass (`make test`)
- [x] Linting passes (`make lint`)
- [x] Added dedicated test for `generateInstanceID` function verifying
determinism, uniqueness, and UUID v5 format
- [x] Updated integration test expected files

[extension/sumologic] feature gate has been replaced with an configuration parameter (#46103)

This PR migrates the `updateCollectorMetadata` functionality from a
feature gate to a configuration parameter in the Sumo Logic extension,
addressing user experience issues with the previous implementation.

  **What changed:**
- Removed the `extension.sumologic.updateCollectorMetadata` feature gate
- Added a new `update_metadata` configuration parameter to the extension
config
  - Set the default value to `true` to enable the feature by default
- Updated tests and documentation to reflect the new configuration
approach

  **Why this change:**
Previously, users had to enable collector metadata updates using a
command-line feature gate:
  ```bash
otelcol-sumo --config={configPath}
--feature-gates=extension.sumologic.updateCollectorMetadata

This was not intuitive and difficult for users to discover. By moving
this to a configuration parameter, users can now easily control this
behavior via their YAML configuration:

  extensions:
    sumologic:
      update_metadata: true  # default: true

This improves usability while maintaining backward compatibility by
enabling the feature by default (matching the behavior in the Sumo Logic
distribution).

  Link to tracking issue

  Fixes #46102

  Testing

- Verified existing unit tests pass with the new configuration parameter
- Updated extension_test.go and factory_test.go to use the new
config-based approach
- Tested that metadata updates are enabled by default when
update_metadata is not explicitly set
- Tested that setting update_metadata: false properly disables metadata
updates

  Documentation

- Updated extension/sumologicextension/README.md to document the new
update_metadata configuration parameter (line 81-83)
- Added changelog entry in
.chloggen/sumologicextension-update-metadata-config.yaml with migration
guidance
- The changelog includes example configuration showing how to use the
new parameter

[extension/oauth2clientauth] Use request context, and expose Token method (#45917)

#### Description

This PR exposes a `Token` method on the extension so the Kafka
components can use it as a means of obtaining an oauth2 access token.
See
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/41873

While working on that change, I found that HTTP and gRPC request context
is not honoured: cancelling a request's context would not cancel the
token refresh, nor would the token refresh propagate trace context. This
is essentially due to https://github.com/golang/oauth2/issues/262. I
have fixed these issues by implementing variations on the HTTP and gRPC
auth code that pass through request context.

[receiver/hostmetrics] reduce excessive float64 precision in scrapers (#46153)

## Summary

Hostmetrics scrapers compute ratios and unit conversions using raw
`float64` division, producing 15-17 decimal digits when the inputs only
support 7-10 significant digits. The extra digits are IEEE 754
arithmetic noise that hurts downstream compression.

This PR adds a `precision` package and applies it to the memory, disk,
and filesystem scrapers on all platforms. All inputs are `uint64`,
matching gopsutil's stat types directly. When the denominator is zero,
`RatioUint64` falls through to native Go division (`NaN`/`+Inf`) to
preserve pre-existing behavior.

`RatioUint64` is for utilization ratios; it derives significant digits
from `floor(log10(max(numerator, denominator))) + 1`. `Scale(numerator
uint64, unit time.Duration)` handles unit conversions, deriving the
denominator from `time.Second/unit` and rounding via `math.Round(result
* mul) / mul` to avoid binary float artifacts like `12345/1000 =
12.345000000000001`.

**Memory** uses `RatioUint64` for all utilization data points. No casts
needed since gopsutil fields are already `uint64`.

**Disk** uses `Scale` with `time.Millisecond` on Linux/others, and
`time.Nanosecond` / `time.Nanosecond*100` on Windows.

**Filesystem** uses `RatioUint64` with `Used/(Used+Free)`, matching
gopsutil's `UsedPercent` formula. On Unix this excludes root-reserved
blocks, where `Used+Free < Total`.

## Why CPU scrapers are excluded

gopsutil converts raw jiffies to seconds by dividing by `ClocksPerSec`
(typically 100) before the scraper sees them, and `cpu.TimesStat` only
exposes `float64` seconds. This shrinks operand magnitudes so much that
a 1-CPU/10s-interval machine gets only 1 significant digit, rounding 3%
utilization to 0.0. The problem affects all platforms. A follow-up issue
will track this.

## Testing

```bash
cd receiver/hostmetricsreceiver
go test ./internal/precision/...
go test ./internal/scraper/memoryscraper/...
go test ./internal/scraper/diskscraper/...
go test ./internal/scraper/filesystemscraper/...
```

## Benchmarks

`RatioUint64` adds ~13 ns per call due to `Log10`+`Pow`+`Round`. `Scale`
adds ~0.13 ns (just `Round`). Both zero-alloc. At scrape intervals of
10-60 seconds this is negligible.

```
BenchmarkRatioUint64-14                   88009604        13.47 ns/op     0 B/op   0 allocs/op
BenchmarkRatioUint64_RawDivision-14       1000000000       0.53 ns/op     0 B/op   0 allocs/op
BenchmarkScale-14                         1000000000       0.64 ns/op     0 B/op   0 allocs/op
BenchmarkScale_RawDivision-14             1000000000       0.51 ns/op     0 B/op   0 allocs/op
```

```bash
go test ./internal/precision/... -bench=. -benchmem
```

Closes
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46141

###
[`v0.43.0`](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/releases/tag/v0.43.0):
0.43.0

##### Breaking Changes 🛠

- Add support for go 1.26 by
[@​giortzisg](https://redirect.github.com/giortzisg) in
[#​1193](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1193)
  - bump minimum supported go version to 1.24
- change type signature of attributes for Logs and Metrics. by
[@​giortzisg](https://redirect.github.com/giortzisg) in
[#​1205](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1205)
- users are not supposed to modify Attributes directly on the Log/Metric
itself, but this is still is a breaking change on the type.
- Send uint64 overflowing attributes as numbers. by
[@​giortzisg](https://redirect.github.com/giortzisg) in
[#​1198](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1198)
- The SDK was converting overflowing uint64 attributes to strings for
slog and logrus integrations. To eliminate double types for these
attributes, the SDK now sends the overflowing attribute as is, and lets
the server handle the overflow appropriately.
- It is expected that overflowing unsigned integers would now get

#### Description
This PR enables dynamic metric configuration at runtime. This means that
collector configuration files can now define a set of attributes for a
metric that they would like to aggregate data by. This can be done on a
per-metric basis for any metric attribute defined at a [requirement
level](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/pull/13913)
of `recommended` or below.

[14281](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/pull/14281).

[receiver/elasticsearchreceiver] Fix IPv6 endpoint formatting (#46090)

Use net.JoinHostPort for proper IPv6 address handling in integration
tests.

#### Description

This PR fixes IPv6 endpoint formatting in the `elasticsearchreceiver`
integration tests. The issue occurred because IPv6 addresses were not
being properly bracketed when constructing HTTP endpoints, causing test
failures in environments where Docker assigns IPv6 addresses.

The fix uses Go's standard `net.JoinHostPort` function, which
automatically handles IPv6 address formatting by enclosing them in
square brackets (e.g., `[::1]:9200`) while leaving IPv4 addresses
unchanged (e.g., `127.0.0.1:9200`).

[extension/basicauth] Add username_file and password_file config options (#46227)

Add a shared credentials file library
(`extension/internal/credentialsfile`) that provides a `ValueResolver`
interface for resolving secrets from inline config values or watched
files. The library uses fsnotify to watch for file changes, enabling
live credential rotation without collector restarts.

Wire the library into basicauthextension's `client_auth` config with two
new fields: `username_file` and `password_file`. When set, file-based
values take precedence over their inline counterparts. Credentials are
read dynamically on each request via the `ValueResolver`, so file
changes are reflected immediately for both HTTP and gRPC clients.

ignore option

[processor/resourcedetection] Add OIDC issuer and token path checks for EKS detection (#45885)

EKS changed the `gitVersion` format in Kubernetes 1.35 (platform version
eks.3), removing the `-eks-` identifier that the detector relied on.
This adds multiple fallback detection methods before the `gitVersion`
check:

1. IRSA token path - `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` contains
"eks.amazonaws.com"
2. Pod Identity token path - `AWS_CONTAINER_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN_FILE`
contains "eks-pod-identity"
3. OIDC issuer - API server `/.well-known/openid-configuration` issuer
contains "oidc.eks."
4. Fallback: `gitVersion` contains "-eks-" (existing check)

Each positive signal is reasonably conclusive. Errors in earlier checks
gracefully fall through to subsequent checks.

Fixes #45866

    events:

        enabled: true
      db.server.query_sample:
        enabled: true

[processor/resourcedetection] Add `tags_from_imds` config option to EC2 detector to control instance tag retrieval method (#46175)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

This PR adds support for fetching EC2 instance tags via the Instance
Metadata Service (IMDS), controlled by the new `tags_from_imds`
configuration option in the EC2 resource detector.

Since `InstanceMetadataTags` is not enabled by default on EC2 instances,
a feature gate defaulting to IMDS would silently break tag retrieval for
most users. A config option is a better fit as it requires explicit
opt-in.

When `tags_from_imds` is set to `false` (default), tags are fetched via
the EC2 DescribeTags API (the existing behavior), which requires the
`ec2:DescribeTags` IAM permission.
When `tags_from_imds` is set to `true`, tags are fetched via IMDS (no
IAM permissions are needed), but `InstanceMetadataTags` must be enabled
on the instance.

[extension/azure_encoding] Add processing for Azure Traces (AppAvailabilityResults, AppDependencies and AppRequests) (#45802)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
This PR adds to `azure_encoding` extension ability to parse Traces from
several Azure Resources that are related to Azure Application Insights:
* AppAvailabilityResults
* AppDependencies 
* AppRequests

Other Categories in `microsoft.insights/components` Resource type
doesn't have some fields, like Id (SpanId) or looks more like Logs or
Metrics (like AppMetrics/AppEvents/AppTraces/etc.) and couldn't be
transformed to Traces. They should be added later to Logs/Metrics
parsers in this extension.

For parsing Azure Trace records was chosen the same approach that was
used in this extension for Resource parsing, so it should support all
types of export formats, as well as provide good flexibility for adding
new Categories in code later.

fix(pkg/stanza): strip illegal XML 1.0 characters before parsing (#46436)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

Sysmon Operational events can embed control characters (e.g. U+0001) in
fields such as FileVersion. Go's encoding/xml rejects these as illegal
XML 1.0 characters, causing the receiver to log an error for every
affected event.

Add sanitizeXMLBytes() to remove code points outside the XML 1.0 legal
range before unmarshalling, so malformed events are processed rather
than dropped.

Assisted-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6

ottl: improve Len() unsupported type error diagnostics (#46476)

#### Description

Enhances error diagnostics in the `Len()` OTTL function by including the
runtime type when an unsupported target type is encountered.

Previously, unsupported types returned a generic error message:

`errors.New(typeError)`

This change replaces it with:

`fmt.Errorf("Len: unsupported target type %T. %s", val, typeError)`

This improves debugging clarity for OTTL users without modifying
execution logic, control flow, or return values for valid inputs.

---

#### Link to tracking issue

N/A — small diagnostic improvement aligned with ongoing OTTL type‑system
stabilization and compilation optimization efforts.

All tests pass successfully.

No documentation changes required.

[`v3.10.0`](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/releases/tag/v3.10.0):
3.10.0 / 2026-02-24

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/compare/v3.9.1...v3.10.0)

Prometheus now offers a distroless Docker image variant alongside the
default
busybox image. The distroless variant provides enhanced security with a
minimal
base image, uses UID/GID 65532 (nonroot) instead of nobody, and removes
the
VOLUME declaration. Both variants are available with `-busybox` and
`-distroless`
tag suffixes (e.g., `prom/prometheus:latest-busybox`,
`prom/prometheus:latest-distroless`).
The busybox image remains the default with no suffix for backwards
compatibility
(e.g., `prom/prometheus:latest` points to the busybox variant).

For users migrating existing **named** volumes from the busybox image to
the distroless variant, the ownership can be adjusted with:

```
docker run --rm -v prometheus-data:/prometheus alpine chown -R 65532:65532 /prometheus
```

Then, the container can be started with the old volume with:

```
docker run -v prometheus-data:/prometheus prom/prometheus:latest-distroless
```

User migrating from bind mounts might need to ajust permissions too,
depending on their setup.

This release is the last to support [Go 1.24].
The next release will require at least [Go 1.25].

##### Added

- Support testing of [Go 1.26].
([#​7902](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7902))

##### Fixed

- Update `Baggage` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation` and `Parse`
and `New` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage` to comply with W3C
Baggage specification limits.
`New` and `Parse` now return partial baggage along with an error when
limits are exceeded.
Errors from baggage extraction are reported to the global error handler.
([#​7880](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7880))

[Go 1.26]: https://go.dev/doc/go1.26

[extension/filestorage] compaction: Fix nil pointer panic when reopen fails (#46490)

#### Description

When `Compact()` fails to reopen the bbolt database (e.g. because the
storage directory was removed), it sets `c.db` to `nil`. The
`on_rebound` compaction loop then crashes the collector process with a
nil pointer dereference (`SIGSEGV`) on the next `shouldCompact()` call,
which invokes `c.db.View()`.

This PR fixes two bugs in `client.go`:

1. **Nil pointer crash:** `Compact()` used `c.db, openErr =
bbolt.Open(...)`, which overwrites `c.db` with `nil` on failure. Changed
to use a local variable and only assign to `c.db` on success. The old
(closed) `*bbolt.DB` returns `bbolt.ErrDatabaseNotOpen` on all
operations instead of panicking, so the compaction loop and callers
degrade gracefully.

2. **Dead code in error handling:** `errors.As(err, &pathErr)` checked
`err` (which holds the result of the earlier `bbolt.Compact` call —
always `nil` at that point) instead of `moveErr`. Fixed to
`errors.As(moveErr, &pathErr)`.

#### Link to tracking issue

Fixes #46489

#### Testing

`TestCompactReopenFailureReturnsErrors`: verifies that after a failed
reopen, `Get()` returns an error (not a panic) and `Close()` is safe to
call.

[connector/spanmetricsconnector] Support extrapolated span metrics using the new `ot.th` tracestate key (#45557)

## Description

This PR adds support for W3C tracestate-based adjusted count in the span
metrics connector, enabling accurate extrapolated metrics for sampled
traces. The implementation extracts sampling information from the
`ot.th` (OpenTelemetry threshold) field in the W3C tracestate header to
compute stochastic-rounded adjusted counts.

### Key Features

- **Stochastic rounding for fractional adjusted counts** - Uses
integer-only operations for efficiency
- **Single-entry cache** - Optimizes consecutive identical tracestates
(common in trace batches)
- **Mixed-mode support** - Handles services where some spans have
tracestate and others don't
- **New `sampling.method` attribute** - Distinguishes between adjusted
and non-adjusted metrics. This attribute is enabled by a config option
`enable_metrics_sampling_method` (default `false`)
- **Histogram support** - Observes multiple events at once based on
adjusted count
- **Zero-allocation optimizations** - Hand-written W3C tracestate parser
replaces regex

### Implementation Details

The implementation includes:

1. **`adjusted_count.go`** - Core logic with
`GetStochasticAdjustedCount()` function and `AdjustedCountCache`
2. **Connector integration** - Seamlessly integrates into the existing
span metrics pipeline
3. **W3C tracestate parsing optimizations** - Zero-allocation parser for
common cases
4. **Comprehensive testing** - Unit tests and benchmarks covering
various scenarios

When a span contains a valid `ot.th` field in its tracestate, the
connector:
- Extracts the threshold value (sampling probability)
- Computes adjusted count as `1.0 / threshold`
- Applies stochastic rounding to maintain statistical accuracy. (This is
combined with previous step as stochastic int div to avoid floating
point operations).
- Generates metrics with the appropriate count value

For services in mixed mode (some spans with tracestate, some without),
separate metric series are generated with the `sampling.method`
attribute to distinguish them.

## Performance Impact

Benchmarks were run to assess the performance overhead of W3C tracestate
processing and adjusted count calculations.

**Test Environment:**
- CPU: Apple M1 Max
- Go: darwin/arm64
- Benchmark time: 3s per test

### Connector ConsumeTraces Performance (3-span batch)

| Scenario | Time (ns/op) | Memory (B/op) | Allocs/op | Overhead |
|----------|--------------|---------------|-----------|----------|
| Baseline (original) | 3,870 | 2,114 | 57 | - |
| No tracestate | 3,871 | 2,114 | 57 | +0.0% |
| With tracestate (th:8, 50% sampling) | 3,957 | 2,114 | 57 | +2.2% |
| With tracestate (th:c, 25% sampling) | 3,937 | 2,114 | 57 | +1.7% |
| With tracestate (th:1, 6% sampling) | 3,950 | 2,115 | 57 | +2.0% |
| No th field in tracestate | 3,982 | 2,114 | 57 | +2.9% |
| Complex tracestate | 4,095 | 2,146 | 58 | +5.8% |

### Large Trace Performance

| Spans | Scenario | Time (ns/op) | Memory (B/op) | Allocs/op | Overhead
|

|-------|----------|--------------|---------------|-----------|----------|
| 10 | No tracestate | 11,745 | 7,144 | 190 | - |
| 10 | With tracestate (th:8) | 11,823 | 7,144 | 190 | +0.7% |

[receiver/awsecscontainermetrics] Add ephemeral storage metrics from ECS Task Metadata Endpoint V4 (#46414)

## Summary

* Add support for `EphemeralStorageMetrics` from the ECS Task Metadata
Endpoint V4, which provides ephemeral storage utilization monitoring for
AWS Fargate tasks
([announcement](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2022/11/aws-fargate-monitoring-storage-utilization/))
* Emits two new **task-level only** gauge metrics:
`ecs.task.ephemeral_storage.utilized` and
`ecs.task.ephemeral_storage.reserved` (in MiB)
* Ephemeral storage is shared across all containers in a Fargate task,
so these metrics are only emitted at the task level, not per-container

## Breaking Change

The unit string for the following **existing** metrics has been
corrected from `"Megabytes"` to `"MiB"`:
- `ecs.task.memory.utilized` / `container.memory.utilized`
- `ecs.task.memory.reserved` / `container.memory.reserved`

The underlying values were already computed in MiB (divided by
`1024*1024`), but the label was incorrect.
Users relying on the exact unit string in metric filters or dashboards
will need to update accordingly.

## Details

The ECS Task Metadata Endpoint V4 response includes an
`EphemeralStorageMetrics` field (available on Fargate Linux platform
version 1.4.0+):

```json
{
  "EphemeralStorageMetrics": {
    "Utilized": 500,
    "Reserved": 21000
  }
}
```

### New metrics

| Metric Name | Unit | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ecs.task.ephemeral_storage.utilized` | MiB | Gauge | Ephemeral
storage currently used by the task |
| `ecs.task.ephemeral_storage.reserved` | MiB | Gauge | Ephemeral
storage reserved (configured) for the task |

### Files changed

| `internal/aws/ecsutil/metadata.go` | Add `EphemeralStorageMetrics`
struct and field to `TaskMetadata` |
| `receiver/.../ecs_metrics.go` | Add 2 new fields to `ECSMetrics` |
| `receiver/.../constant.go` | Rename `unitMegaBytes` to `unitMiB`,
correct value from `"Megabytes"` to `"MiB"` |
| `receiver/.../accumulator.go` | Populate ephemeral storage from task
metadata |
| `receiver/.../translator.go` | Emit 2 new gauges (task-level only,
guarded by `prefix == taskPrefix`) |

`TestConvertToOTMetricsTaskLevel` with assertions for metric names,
units, and values |

[exporter/googlecloudstorage] Refactor reuse_if_exists to check bucket existence (#45971)

## Description

**BREAKING CHANGE**: Refactored the `reuse_if_exists` configuration
option to match its semantic meaning and enable usage with bucket-level
permissions only.

## Motivation

Previously, even with `reuse_if_exists=true`, the exporter would attempt
bucket creation (requiring project-level `storage.buckets.create`
permission) and only fall back to reusing if a conflict occurred. This
failed when the service account lacked project-level bucket creation
permissions but had bucket-level permissions.

## Changes

### Behavior Changes
- **`reuse_if_exists=true`**: 
- Now checks if bucket exists using `bucket.Attrs()` (requires
`storage.buckets.get` on the specific bucket)
  - If bucket exists: uses it
  - If bucket doesn't exist: fails with error
  - No attempt to create bucket
- **`reuse_if_exists=false`**: 
  - Attempts to create bucket (unchanged)
  - Fails if bucket already exists (unchanged)

### Code Changes
- Refactored bucket creation logic in `Start()` method
- Removed `use_existing` flag (functionality now in refactored
`reuse_if_exists`)
- Removed unused `isBucketConflictError()` function
- Updated tests to cover new behavior
- Updated documentation and examples
- Updated changelog to reflect breaking change

## Backward Compatibility

**This is a breaking change** for users currently using
`reuse_if_exists=true` who rely on bucket creation. Users in this
scenario should either:
1. Set `reuse_if_exists=false` to create buckets (requires project-level
permissions)
2. Create buckets externally and set `reuse_if_exists=true` (works with
bucket-level permissions)

## Testing

- All existing tests pass
- Added test case:
`bucket_does_not_exist_with_reuse_if_exists=true_should_fail`
- Linting passes
- Mock storage emulator updated to handle `bucket.Attrs()` calls

RFC](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/rfcs/semconv-feature-gates.md).

  - `http.host` -> `server.address`
  - `http.server_name` -> `server.address`
  
Migration path:

Enable `<component>.EmitV1NetworkConventions` to start emitting both old
and new keys (dual-emit transition)
Once user pipelines and backends are updated, also enable
`<component>.DontEmitV0NetworkConventions` to stop emitting the
deprecated v1.12.0 keys.

perf(kafkaexporter): Use metric.WithAttributeSet (#46664)

#### Description

Replace `metric.WithAttributes()` with `metric.WithAttributeSet()`
across all 6 franz-go hook methods (12 call sites). `WithAttributes`
allocates and sorts a new `attribute.Set` on every call; building the
set once and reusing the option eliminates redundant work on hot paths.

Where multiple metrics share the same attributes (OnBrokerThrottle,
OnBrokerE2E, OnProduceBatchWritten, OnProduceRecordUnbuffered), the
attribute set is built once and the `metric.WithAttributeSet` option is
reused across all metric calls.

[exporter/kafkaexporter] Reuse pdata wrapper in resource-partitioned Logs and Metrics paths (#46724)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

While looking at the `partitionData` code for logs and metrics, I
noticed that when `partition_*_by_resource_attributes` is enabled, we
allocate a fresh `plog.NewLogs()` / `pmetric.NewMetrics()` wrapper on
every loop iteration just to `CopyTo` into it and hand it off. Since
`exportData` consumes each yielded value synchronously, the wrapper from
the previous iteration is never touched again, so we can safely boost it
outside the loop and let `CopyTo` overwrite the same target each time.

I ran some benchmarks, and the numbers look good, especially for logs
where the proto nesting is deeper.

[extension/azure_encoding] add encoding.format field to azure encoding extension (#46412)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

This PR adds `encoding.format` field for `azureencodingextension`. All
logs processed by this extension are automatically tagged with an
`encoding.format` attribute at the scope level to identify the source
format. This allows you to easily filter and route logs based on their
Azure service and log type.

The pattern used is `azure.<format_name>` at the log family level.

Examples:

- Application Gateway Access:
`encoding.format:"azure.application_gateway"`
- App Service HTTP: `encoding.format:"azure.appservice"`
- Front Door WAF: `encoding.format:"azure.frontdoor"`

##### Format values

The following format values are supported in the
`azureencodingextension` to identify different Azure log types:


| Azure log family | Format value | Description | 
| -- | -- | -- | 
| Activity | azure.activity | Azure activity logs (administrative,
alert, policy, recommendation, security, etc.) |
| Application Gateway | azure.application_gateway | Application Gateway
logs (access, performance, firewall) |
| App Service | azure.appservice | App Service logs (app, audit, HTTP,
platform, etc.) |
| CDN | azure.cdn | Azure CDN access logs | 
| Data Factory | azure.datafactory | Data Factory logs (activity,
pipeline, trigger runs) |
| Front Door | azure.frontdoor | Front Door logs (access, health
probe, WAF) |
| Function App | azure.function_app | Azure Functions application logs |
| Messaging | azure.messaging | Event Hubs/Service Bus logs
(operational, metrics, audit, etc.) |
| Storage | azure.storage | Storage operation logs (read, write, delete)
|
| Generic | azure.generic | Generic parser applied |

[pkg/xstreamencoding] add unmarshaler adapters (#46754)

#### Description

Introduce adapters for plog.LogsUnmarshaler and
pmetric.MetricsUnmarshaler which, on first call, read the entire stream
into memory and invoke the unmarshaler. Subsequent calls return EOF.

The offset is always the entire stream size in bytes, and if an offset
is provided then that many bytes will discarded first.

We also extract LogsDecoderFactory and MetricsDecoderFactory interfaces
from LogsDecoderExtension and MetricsDecoderExtension in the encoding
package.

[pkg/translator/azurelogs] remove semconv v1.28.0 and v1.34.0 dependencies (#46430)

#### Description

Removes the semconv v1.28.0 and v1.34.0 imports from
`pkg/translator/azurelogs`, migrating fully to v1.38.0.

Three attribute key strings changed between versions, which would break
existing consumers if changed directly. This PR follows the established
dual feature gate pattern (same as `processor/k8sattributesprocessor`)
to allow a gradual migration:

- **`pkg.translator.azurelogs.emitStableLogConventions`** (alpha,
default off): emit new stable attribute names
- **`pkg.translator.azurelogs.dontEmitLegacyLogConventions`** (alpha,
default off): suppress old attribute names

Gate behaviour matrix:

| emitStable | dontEmitLegacy | Result |
|---|---|---|
| false | false | legacy only (default, no change) |
| true | false | both old + new (migration window) |
| true | true | stable only |
| false | true | error at startup |

**Attribute migrations (guarded by gates):**
- `code.function` → `code.function.name` (AppServiceAppLogs `Method`
field)
- `code.filepath` → `code.file.path` (AppServiceAppLogs `Source` field)
- `event.name` on Resource → `lr.SetEventName("az.resource.log")` on
each LogRecord (the legacy placement was semantically incorrect)

**Import-only cleanup (no key string change, no gate needed):**
- `az.service_request_id` was removed from semconv in v1.36.0 without a
replacement. Hardcoded as a local const with a TODO comment.

[receiver/kafkareceiver] Avoid map allocation in contextWithHeaders when no headers (#46759)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

`contextWithHeaders` is called on every Kafka message and always
allocates a `map[string][]string` even when there are no headers. Adding
a `len()` method to the `messageHeaders` interface lets us early-return
for headerless messages (skipping the map alloc entirely) and pass a
size hint to `make` for the headers-present path (avoiding map
grow/rehash).

The impact is not really huge, but I think it deserves a review, so I
decided to propose this PR.

[`v1.42.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.42.0):

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/compare/v1.41.0...v1.42.0)

##### Added

- Add `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.40.0` package.
The package contains semantic conventions from the `v1.40.0` version of
the OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions.
See the [migration documentation](./semconv/v1.40.0/MIGRATION.md) for
information on how to upgrade from
`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.39.0`.
([#​7985](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7985))
- Add `Err` and `SetErr` on `Record` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log`
to attach an error and set record exception attributes in
`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log/sdk`.
([#​7924](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7924))

##### Changed

- `TracerProvider.ForceFlush` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`
joins errors together and continues iteration through SpanProcessors as
opposed to returning the first encountered error without attempting
exports on subsequent SpanProcessors.
([#​7856](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7856))

##### Fixed

- Fix missing `request.GetBody` in
`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp` to
correctly handle HTTP2 GOAWAY frame.
([#​7931](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7931))
- Fix semconv v1.39.0 generated metric helpers skipping required
attributes when extra attributes were empty.
([#​7964](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7964))
- Preserve W3C TraceFlags bitmask (including the random Trace ID flag)
during trace context extraction and injection in
`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation`.
([#​7834](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7834))

##### Removed

- Drop support for \[Go 1.24].
([#​7984](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7984))

signaltometricsconnector: Add `sum.monotonic` property for improved counter handling (#45865)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
So far there has been no way to set the `IsMonotonic` property of
metrics, although the main use-case based on the examples of the README
is to generate counters, which are clearly monotonic.

The incorrect monotonic=false setting causes some problems on my end,
namely that the OTel -> Prometheus conversion is incorrect (`_total`
isn't appended, if monotonic is false), additionally, the `interval`
processor doesn't work with non-monotonic sums.

`MergeCtx` for metadata partitioning and adding config validation so
`topic_from_metadata_key` must be included in `include_metadata_keys`

validation failure cases.

[exporter/kafka] Remove messageHeaders abstraction since Sarama is deprecated (#46815)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

The generic header utility functions (`metadataToHeaders[H]`,
`setMessageHeaders[M,H]`, `setHeaders[M,H]`) in
`internal/kafkaclient/headers.go` were designed to abstract over Sarama
and franz-go types via Go generics. Now that Sarama has been fully
removed, the generics are only ever instantiated with `kgo.RecordHeader`
/ `*kgo.Record`.

I decided to add a changelog file to give some visibility, but this is
not expected to change any user behaviour.

[pkg/ottl/ottlfuncs] Add UTF-8 support to truncate_all function (#45055)

#### Description

The `truncate_all` function cuts strings at arbitrary byte positions,
which could break UTF-8 multi-byte characters and produce invalid utf-8
output.

This PR makes it back up to a valid character boundary when the limit
falls mid-character. If the string isn't valid UTF-8 to begin with, it
just cuts at the byte level like before.

Based on the approach suggested by @jade-guiton-dd in

are respected.

[extension/googlecloudlogentryencoding] Fix incorrect snake_case conversion for numeronyms (e.g. k8s) (#46588)

#### Description:
This PR fixes an issue where the googlecloudlogentryencoding extension
incorrectly converted log field names containing numeronyms
(abbreviations containing numbers, such as "k8s") into snake_case.

#### The Problem:
The previous implementation relied on strcase.ToSnakeWithIgnore, which
treats a digit followed by a lowercase letter as a word boundary.

- Input: labels.authorization.k8s.io/decision
- Previous Output: labels.authorization.k8_s.io/decision (Incorrect
split at 8 and s)
- Expected Output: labels.authorization.k8s.io/decision

#### The Solution:
Introduced a shared.ToSnakeCase helper function that wraps the existing
library call. It uses a regex replacement ((\d)_([a-z]) -> ${1}${2}) to
post-process the string, re-merging digits and subsequent lowercase
letters. This approach preserves standard numeronyms (e.g., k8s, v1beta)
while maintaining snake_case for standard camelCase inputs.

#### Link to tracking Issue:
Fixes #46571

#### Testing:

- Added unit tests in internal/shared to cover edge cases (k8s, v1beta,
standard camelCase).
- Updated log_entry_test.go to verify the fix in the extension logic.
- Updated golden files (activity_expected.yaml) to reflect the correct
output.
- Ran tests locally; all tests passed.

#### Documentation:
- I have updated the changelog (.chloggen directory)

receiver/prometheus: validate target allocator interval to prevent ticker panic (#46857)

#### Description

This PR adds validation for the `interval` field in the Prometheus
receiver target allocator configuration.

Previously, if `interval` was set to `0s` or a negative duration, the
collector would eventually call `time.NewTicker(interval)`. In Go,
`time.NewTicker()` panics when the duration is less than or equal to
zero, which could cause the collector to crash at runtime.

This change adds a validation check in the target allocator
configuration to ensure that `interval` must be a positive duration.
Invalid configurations are now rejected during configuration validation
with a clear error message, preventing runtime panics.

#### Link to tracking issue

Fixes #46842

#### Testing

Unit tests were added in
`receiver/prometheusreceiver/internal/targetallocator/config_test.go` to
validate the new behavior. The following cases are covered:

-   Valid interval (e.g., `30s`) → configuration passes validation
-   Boundary interval (`1ns`) → configuration passes validation
-   Zero interval (`0s`) → validation error returned
-   Negative interval (`-1s`) → validation error returned

All existing tests in the Prometheus receiver target allocator package
were executed:

`go test ./receiver/prometheusreceiver/internal/targetallocator/...`

All tests pass successfully.

#### Documentation

No user-facing documentation changes were required. The change only adds
validation for an invalid configuration value and does not modify any
configuration schema or documented behavior.

processor/tailsampling: stabilize TestDropLargeTraces metric assertions (#46283)

## Description

Fixes #46154

This PR fixes flakiness in `TestDropLargeTraces` within the tail
sampling processor tests.

The test validates that traces exceeding `MaximumTraceSizeBytes` are
dropped and that the correct metrics are emitted. While the sampling
behavior itself is deterministic, metric assertions were intermittently
failing in CI environments.

---

## Root Cause

Metrics in the tail sampling processor are recorded asynchronously via
the OpenTelemetry Metrics SDK.

The test previously performed metric collection synchronously using:

```go
telem.reader.Collect(...)
```

In slower CI environments, metric aggregation had not fully completed at
collection time, leading to intermittent missing datapoints and
assertion failures.

Locally, the test passed consistently due to faster execution timing.

Affected metrics:

- `otelcol_processor_tail_sampling_sampling_trace_dropped_too_early`
- `otelcol_processor_tail_sampling_traces_dropped_too_large`

---

## Fix

Metric collection and assertions are now wrapped in
`require.EventuallyWithT` to account for asynchronous aggregation.

### Key changes

- Retry metric collection for up to **2 seconds**
- Poll interval of **100ms**
- Assertions execute once datapoints stabilize
- Ensures deterministic validation across environments

The retry window aligns with async metric stabilization patterns used in
existing collector tests.

---

## Scope

- **Test-only change**
- No processor logic modified
- No sampling behavior changes
- No production code impact

---

## Testing

Validation performed:

- Repeated local runs (`-count=20`)
- Full module test suite execution
- No regressions observed

All tests pass consistently after stabilization.

---

## Notes

The fix preserves strict metric validation while making the test
resilient to async metric pipeline timing differences between local and
CI environments.

## Description

This PR adds unit tests for the previously untested `logs.go` file in
the `otlpjsonconnector` package, which contains the logs connector that
extracts OTLP log payloads from log record bodies.

### Changes

- New file: `connector/otlpjsonconnector/logs_test.go`

### Tests Added

| Test | What it validates |
|------|-------------------|
| `TestNewLogsConnector` | Constructor creates a properly initialized
connector with logger and consumer |
| `TestLogsConnectorCapabilities` | `Capabilities()` returns
`MutatesData: false` |
| `TestLogsConnectorConsumeLogsWithValidLogPayload` | Valid OTLP JSON
log body is unmarshaled and forwarded to the sink (1 log record) |
| `TestLogsConnectorConsumeLogsWithTracePayload` | Trace payloads in log
bodies are correctly skipped |
| `TestLogsConnectorConsumeLogsWithMetricPayload` | Metric payloads in
log bodies are correctly skipped |

payloads are dropped without error |

This logic had no dedicated unit tests. The existing `connector_test.go`
covers higher-level golden-file based scenarios but does not isolate the
`ConsumeLogs` method or test edge cases like malformed JSON.

[internal/metadataproviders] Fix response body leak and add status check in OpenShift provider (#46922)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

The three HTTP methods in the OpenShift metadata provider
(`OpenShiftClusterVersion`, `Infrastructure`, `K8SClusterVersion`) never
close the response body after making requests. This can leak connections
and file descriptors over time, especially when periodic refresh is
enabled. Eventually, the collector runs out of file descriptors and
cannot make new HTTP calls.

This change adds `defer resp.Body.Close()` to all three methods and also
validates the HTTP status code before trying to decode the response.
Previously, a 403 or 500 from the API would produce a confusing JSON
decode error instead of a clear message about the actual status code.

fix(datadogreceiver): preserve original per-span attribute (#46850)

#### Description

This is to fix an issue with spans like db / sql ones not showing the
override name (i.e. testdb) that would display when doing through the DD
agent directly prior to routing through a shared OTEL collector like
Alloy

Why this works end-to-end:

1. `span.Meta` entries become span attributes in the OTEL conversion
(`newSpan.Attributes().PutStr(k, v)`)
2. `span.Service` (after override) becomes the resource-level
`service.name` via `groupByService` which satisfies OTEL's resource
model
3. The DD exporter's OTelSpanAccessor checks span attributes before
resource attributes, so `span.Meta["service.name"]` (the original
per-span service) takes precedence over the resource-level base service

No config flags needed, no language-specific heuristics, no
groupbyattrs. The original service name roundtrips cleanly through
DD→OTEL→DD. Works for all tracers and all languages.

Currently, we get around this with something like this in the Alloy
config. The Alloy datadog exporter just natively uses primitives here
and that's what led me to this change.
```
	trace_statements {
		context    = "span"
		statements = [
			`set(attributes["server.address"], attributes["http.server_name"]) where attributes["http.server_name"] != nil and attributes["server.address"] == nil`,
			`set(attributes["peer.service"], Concat([attributes["django.db.alias"], "db"], "")) where attributes["django.db.alias"] != nil`,
			`set(attributes["base_service"], attributes["service.name"]) where attributes["django.db.alias"] != nil`,
			`set(attributes["_dd.base_service"], attributes["service.name"]) where attributes["django.db.alias"] != nil`,
			`set(attributes["service.name"], attributes["peer.service"]) where attributes["django.db.alias"] != nil`,
		]
	}

	trace_statements {
		context    = "span"
		statements = [
			// Outbound calls (DB, cache, HTTP client) have server.address set by DD trace libs
			`set(span.kind, SPAN_KIND_CLIENT) where instrumentation_scope.name == "datadog" and span.kind == SPAN_KIND_UNSPECIFIED and attributes["server.address"] != nil`,
			// Inbound request handlers have http.route set by DD trace libs
			`set(span.kind, SPAN_KIND_SERVER) where instrumentation_scope.name == "datadog" and span.kind == SPAN_KIND_UNSPECIFIED and attributes["http.route"] != nil`,
		]
	}
```

## Description
This PR enables re-aggregation for the `flinkmetrics` receiver by
setting `reaggregation_enabled: true` and classifying all attributes
with appropriate `requirement_level` values.

Attributes are classified as `required` where aggregation would produce
meaningless results — `checkpoint` (completed vs failed are distinct
states), `garbage_collector_name` (distinct GC implementations), and
`record` (in/out/dropped are fundamentally different). `operator_name`
is classified as `recommended` as aggregating across operators can still
produce operationally meaningful totals.

[pkg/stanza] Add support for `if` option in `recombine` operator (#46074)

#### Description

The recombine operator inherits the `if` field from `TransformerConfig`,
but its `Process()` and `ProcessBatch()` methods never evaluate it. This
means the `if` field is silently accepted but has no effect, leading
users to believe they are conditionally applying recombine when it
actually applies to all logs unconditionally.

This adds a warning during `Build()` when the `if` field is configured
on a recombine operator, informing the user that it is not supported and
suggesting a `router` operator as an alternative.

#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #46048

#### Testing

Added `TestBuildWarnsOnIfExpr` which verifies that building a recombine
config with `if` set emits exactly one warning with the expected
message. All existing tests continue to pass.

#### Documentation

No documentation changes needed. The warning message itself guides users
toward the correct approach (using a `router` operator).

[receiver/windowseventlogreceiver] Use a map for event_data (#46034)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

Changes the `event_data` format from an array of single-key maps (which
is extremely difficult to work with in OTTL) to a flat map , making
fields directly accessible via OTTL.

**Before:**
```json
{
  "event_data": {
    "data": [
      {"ProcessId": "7924"},
      {"Application": "app.exe"},
      {"": "anonymous_value"}
    ]
  }
}
```

**After:**
```json
{
  "event_data": {
    "ProcessId": "7924",
    "Application": "app.exe",
    "Data1": "anonymous_value"
  }
}
```

- Named `<Data>` elements become direct keys
- Anonymous `<Data>` elements get numbered keys (`Data1`, `Data2`, etc.)
- Fields now directly accessible: `body["event_data"]["ProcessId"]`

For Windows logs, any given log has either named elements or anonymous
elements, which avoids typical key conflicts.

[receiver/otelarrowreceiver] Fix OTLP handlers returning codes.Unknow… (#46210)

## Description

The otelarrow receiver's standard OTLP protocol handlers (the non-Arrow
fallback path for traces, metrics, and logs) return raw Go errors
directly from `Export` methods. When gRPC serializes a plain `error`
without an attached `status.Status`, it [defaults to
`codes.Unknown`](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.59.0/server.go#L1345).
Upstream exporters treat `codes.Unknown` as a permanent (non-retryable)
failure, causing data to be dropped instead of retried.

The core OTLP receiver handles this correctly via
[`errors.GetStatusFromError()`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/receiver/otlpreceiver/internal/errors/errors.go),
which maps:

  - Non-permanent errors → `codes.Unavailable` (retryable, HTTP 503)
  - Permanent errors → `codes.Internal` (HTTP 500)

The otelarrow receiver's Arrow streaming path (`sendOne()` in
`arrow.go`) also already handles this correctly. Only the OTLP unary RPC
fallback handlers were affected.

#### Impact

When a downstream collector's `memory_limiter` processor rejects data,
the plain `ErrDataRefused` error surfaces as `codes.Unknown` through the
otelarrow receiver. The upstream exporter's `shouldRetry()` does not
include `codes.Unknown`, so data is permanently dropped:

error: "not retryable error: Permanent error: rpc error: code = Unknown
desc = data refused due to high memory usage"
      dropped_items: 1

With this fix, the same scenario produces `codes.Unavailable` and the
data is retried with backoff.

#### Link to Tracking Issue


https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46182

#### Changes

- Added `internal/errors/errors.go` with `GetStatusFromError()`
mirroring the core OTLP receiver's logic
- Updated `internal/trace/otlp.go`, `internal/metrics/otlp.go`,
`internal/logs/otlp.go` to convert errors before returning
- Updated all corresponding tests to expect `codes.Unavailable` instead
of `codes.Unknown`
- Added `TestExport_PermanentErrorConsumer` tests for all three signal
types

#### Testing

All existing tests updated and passing. New test coverage added for:
- Plain (non-permanent) consumer errors → `codes.Unavailable`
- Permanent consumer errors → `codes.Internal`
- Existing gRPC status errors (admission2 queue errors) → passed through
unchanged

[internal/aws]: respect NO_PROXY env var in awsutil HTTP client (#46923)

fixes #46892

When no explicit `proxy_address` is configured, `newHTTPClient` in
`internal/aws/awsutil/conn.go` manually reads `HTTPS_PROXY` via
`getProxyAddress` and passes it to `http.ProxyURL`. This unconditionally
routes **all** requests through the proxy, completely ignoring
`NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` environment variables.

This causes TLS failures for users running behind intercepting proxies
(e.g. mitmproxy) who rely on `NO_PROXY` to bypass the proxy for AWS
endpoints:
```
tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

## Fix

Introduced `getProxyFunc` which:
- **Empty `proxy_address` (env-based proxy):** returns
`http.ProxyFromEnvironment`, Go's stdlib function that correctly handles
`HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, and their lowercase variants.
- **Explicit `proxy_address` (config-based proxy):** returns
`http.ProxyURL` as before — no behavior change.

## Tests

Added three tests to `conn_test.go`:
- `TestNoProxyIsRespectedWhenUsingEnvProxy` -- verifies proxy is
bypassed for hosts matching `NO_PROXY`
- `TestProxyIsUsedForNonExcludedHosts` -- verifies proxy is still used
for non-excluded hosts
- `TestExplicitProxyAddressStillWorks` -- verifies backward
compatibility with explicit `proxy_address` config

## Note

`internal/aws/proxy/conn.go` has a similar pattern (its own
`getProxyAddress`/`getProxyURL` with the same `http.ProxyURL` usage).
Happy to fix that in this PR as well.

The old `getProxyAddress` and `getProxyURL` in `awsutil/conn.go` are now
unused by production code (only their existing tests reference them).
Happy to remove them too in this PR if preferred.

[exporter/kafka] Fix topic routing for multi-resource batches with topic_from_attribute (#46873)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

When `topic_from_attribute` is set, `getTopic` returns on the first
resource that has the attribute, silently routing all other resources in
the batch to the same topic. This is incorrect when resources carry
different attribute values.

Fixed `partitionData` for all four signals (metrics, logs, traces,
profiles) to auto-split by resource when `topic_from_attribute` is
configured, so each `getTopic` call sees exactly one resource and
resolves to the correct topic.
The split yields `key=nil` to avoid side effects on Kafka message
partitioning. Single-resource batches (the common case) add only one
boolean check.

Does not seem that this change produces any performance impact, as we

# Description

This PR adds unit tests for the previously untested `metric.go` file in
the `internal/exp/metrics/identity` package, which builds stable metric
identities from resource, scope, and metric metadata.

## Changes

histogram, and exponential histogram metrics |
| `TestMetricHashChangesWhenIdentityChanges` | Metric hashes change when
identity inputs such as scope version, metric name, unit, monotonicity,
or temporality change |

matches the equivalent `OfMetric(OfScope(OfResource(...)))` path |

expected `metric/<hash>` representation |

## Motivation

The metric identity helpers are used by several components that
deduplicate, route, or track metrics by identity. This package
previously had no direct tests, even though correctness here is
important for downstream grouping behavior. This PR adds focused
coverage for the main construction and hashing logic without changing
production code.

#### Description

Adds a new `otelcol.elasticsearch.docs.retried_http_request` metric that
counts the documents retried due to retryable HTTP status
errors(retryOnStatus) at the transport layer.

We already have `otelcol.elasticsearch.docs.retried`, but it explicitly
counts document-level retries. Including request-level retries in this
metric would inflate its value significantly and likely confuse users.
Instead, this change introduces a separate metric.

Fixes
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46215

#### Documentation

Added the new metric to the documentation.

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.

#### Description

The Alibaba ECS metadata provider makes multiple sequential HTTP calls
to its cloud IMDS endpoints during resource detection. Since these calls
are independent of each other, this change runs them in parallel using
`errgroup`, reducing total metadata fetch time from `N *
single_call_latency` to `1 * single_call_latency`

Benchmarks with simulated 2ms IMDS latency show Alibaba ECS going from
~16ms to ~2ms (7 calls).

This was identified during the initial implementation of the detector,
but was postponed to further discussion.

[extension/bearertokenauth] Redact bearer token from authentication error messages (#46271)

## Description

Fixes #46200

### Problem

When a client presents an invalid bearer token to the
`bearertokenauthextension`'s `Authenticate` method, the **full token
value** is included in the returned error message:

```go
return ctx, fmt.Errorf("scheme or token does not match: %s", token)
```

This error propagates to log output, exposing sensitive credentials in
plain text. As reported in #46200, the error output looks like:

```
failed to send logs to : 401 Unauthorized (body: scheme or token does not match: Bearer {"token":""})
```

This is a **credential exposure vulnerability** — any token (valid or
malformed) sent by a client will be written to logs in cleartext when
authentication fails.

### Root Cause

The `Authenticate` method in `bearertokenauth.go` uses `fmt.Errorf` to
construct an error message that includes the raw token value (`%s`,
`token`). While this may have been intended for debugging, it violates
the security principle of never logging credentials, even in error
paths.

### Fix

Replace the token-exposing error message with a generic authentication
failure message that communicates the nature of the error without
leaking secrets:

```go
// Before (vulnerable):
return ctx, fmt.Errorf("scheme or token does not match: %s", token)

// After (secure):
return ctx, errors.New("provided authorization does not match expected scheme or token")
```

The error message remains descriptive enough for operators to understand
the failure cause (scheme mismatch vs. token mismatch) without exposing
the credential itself.

### Design Reasoning

- **No token in error messages**: The most secure approach is to never
include tokens in error messages, even in redacted form. Partial
redaction (e.g., showing first/last N characters) still leaks
information about token format and length, which can aid brute-force
attacks.
- **Minimal change**: This is a single-line fix in the production code,
reducing merge risk.
- **Backward compatibility**: The error string change is non-breaking —
callers should be checking `err != nil`, not parsing error message
content. The `Authenticate` method is part of the `extensionauth.Server`
interface, and the interface contract does not specify error message
format.

### Tradeoffs

- **Debuggability**: Operators lose the ability to see which exact token
was rejected in logs. However, this is the correct tradeoff — tokens
should never appear in logs. If debugging is needed, operators can
enable debug-level logging at the transport layer or inspect the request
directly.
- **Error granularity**: We could split into separate errors for "wrong
scheme" vs. "wrong token" vs. "wrong format". However, from a security
perspective, it is better to not distinguish these cases to avoid oracle
attacks. This aligns with established auth error handling patterns
(e.g., HTTP 401 does not tell you *why* auth failed).

### Testing

Added `TestAuthenticateErrorDoesNotExposeToken` which:
1. Configures a valid token and attempts authentication with an invalid
one
2. **Asserts the error does NOT contain the invalid token** (the
reported vulnerability)
3. **Asserts the error does NOT contain the valid/expected token**
(defense in depth)
4. Asserts the error still communicates authentication failure with
"does not match"

All existing tests pass with zero regressions.

### Changelog

Added `.chloggen/fix-bearer-token-exposure-in-error-logs.yaml` per
contribution guidelines.

[receiver/journald] Fix emitting of historical entries on startup (#46556)

#### Description

When start_at is set to "end" (the default), journalctl is invoked with
--follow but without --lines=0. This causes journalctl to output the
last 10 journal entries before switching to follow mode, resulting in
unexpected historical log entries on every collector startup.

Pass --lines=0 when start_at is "end" to suppress the backlog and only
receive entries that arrive after the receiver starts.

#### Testing

Wrote a small script that sends a single log entry per second to
journald. Build OTel collector with/without the changes in this PR. 10
log entries are reported on startup without this PR. Only log entries
written after starting the OTel collector are reported when applying the
changes of this PR.

#### Description
I noticed that `func_uuidv7_test.go` was incorrectly calling the `uuid`
(v4) factory instead of the intended `uuidV7` factory.

This PR:
- Corrects the factory call to `uuidV7`.
- Adds assertions to verify the UUID version digit (7) at index 14.

index 19.

values.

within the `pkg/ottl` module.

Release 1.79.3

Security

  • server: fix an authorization bypass where malformed :path headers (missing the leading slash) could bypass path-based restricted "deny" rules in interceptors like grpc/authz. Any request with a non-canonical path is now immediately rejected with an Unimplemented error. (#8981)

Release 1.79.2

Bug Fixes

  • stats: Prevent redundant error logging in health/ORCA producers by skipping stats/tracing processing when no stats handler is configured. (grpc/grpc-go#8874)

Release 1.79.1

Bug Fixes

  • grpc: Remove the -dev suffix from the User-Agent header. (grpc/grpc-go#8902)

Release 1.79.0

API Changes

  • mem: Add experimental API SetDefaultBufferPool to change the default buffer pool. (#8806)
    • Special Thanks: @​vanja-p
  • experimental/stats: Update MetricsRecorder to require embedding the new UnimplementedMetricsRecorder (a no-op struct) in all implementations for forward compatibility. (#8780)

Behavior Changes

  • balancer/weightedtarget: Remove handling of Addresses and only handle Endpoints in resolver updates. (#8841)

New Features

  • experimental/stats: Add support for asynchronous gauge metrics through the new AsyncMetricReporter and RegisterAsyncReporter APIs. (#8780)
  • pickfirst: Add support for weighted random shuffling of endpoints, as described in gRFC A113.
    • This is enabled by default, and can be turned off using the environment variable GRPC_EXPERIMENTAL_PF_WEIGHTED_SHUFFLING. (#8864)
  • xds: Implement :authority rewriting, as specified in gRFC A81. (#8779)
  • balancer/randomsubsetting: Implement the random_subsetting LB policy, as specified in gRFC A68. (#8650)
    • Special Thanks: @​marek-szews

Bug Fixes

  • credentials/tls: Fix a bug where the port was not stripped from the authority override before validation. (#8726)
    • Special Thanks: @​Atul1710
  • xds/priority: Fix a bug causing delayed failover to lower-priority clusters when a higher-priority cluster is stuck in CONNECTING state. (#8813)
  • health: Fix a bug where health checks failed for clients using legacy compression options (WithDecompressor or RPCDecompressor). (#8765)
    • Special Thanks: @​sanki92
  • transport: Fix an issue where the HTTP/2 server could skip header size checks when terminating a stream early. (#8769)
    • Special Thanks: @​joybestourous
  • server: Propagate status detail headers, if available, when terminating a stream during request header processing. (#8754)
    • Special Thanks: @​joybestourous

Performance Improvements

  • credentials/alts: Optimize read buffer alignment to reduce copies. (#8791)
  • mem: Optimize pooling and creation of buffer objects. (#8784)
  • transport: Reduce slice re-allocations by reserving slice capacity. (#8797)

[exporter/elasticsearch] Encode require_data_stream in bulk action metadata (#46880)

## Summary

Move `require_data_stream` from bulk request query parameters to
per-document bulk action metadata in the Elasticsearch exporter.

## Why

Maintainer feedback requested splitting this change into a dedicated PR
and keeping it separate from broader request-splitting/retry
architecture work.

## What changed

- Set `require_data_stream` on `docappender.BulkIndexerItem` action
metadata (document level).
- Keep bulk-level `RequireDataStream` disabled to avoid query-string
encoding for this parameter.
- Preserve existing endpoint query params, but explicitly remove
`require_data_stream` from forwarded endpoint query parameters.
- Update logs/metrics/traces exporter tests to assert
`require_data_stream` in action metadata.
- Add/refresh focused tests and benchmark coverage for payload overhead.
- Update docs/changelog wording to match document-level encoding
behavior.

## Validation

- `make test` (exporter module): pass
- `make chlog-validate`: pass
- `go test -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkRequireDataStreamPayloadOverhead
-benchmem`: pass

Benchmark payload sizes:
- 10 items: 1400 -> 1670 bytes
- 100 items: 14000 -> 16700 bytes
- 1000 items: 140000 -> 167000 bytes

Overhead is consistently ~27 bytes per item.

[receiver/filelog] Fix last lines of compressed file is not correctly read (#45577)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
This PR checks if `atEOF` is true in `splitFunc` and flushes data in
case of compressed files. This does not wait for flush interval to
timout before sending data like normal files. This is because currently
gzip compressed files must be read entirely in one scan.

To be able to solve it in any other way will require us to read
compressed files in chunk - hence keeping this bug fix simple for now.
