feat(processor/schema): add internal telemetry metrics (#47638)

## Description

Adds internal telemetry metrics to the schema processor, giving
operators visibility into what the processor is doing at both the
resource and scope level.

Part of #47428

### New metrics

| Metric | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `otelcol_processor_schema_cache.hits` | Schema cache hits in
CacheableProvider |
| `otelcol_processor_schema_cache.misses` | Schema cache misses
(provider called) in CacheableProvider |
| `otelcol_processor_schema_resource.failed` | Resource translation
requests that failed |
| `otelcol_processor_schema_logs.failed` | Log scope translation
requests that failed |
| `otelcol_processor_schema_logs.skipped` | Log scopes skipped because
no schema URL was present on the scope or its resource |
| `otelcol_processor_schema_metrics.failed` | Metric scope translation
requests that failed |
| `otelcol_processor_schema_metrics.skipped` | Metric scopes skipped
because no schema URL was present on the scope or its resource |
| `otelcol_processor_schema_traces.failed` | Trace scope translation
requests that failed |
| `otelcol_processor_schema_traces.skipped` | Trace scopes skipped
because no schema URL was present on the scope or its resource |

`resource.skipped` is intentionally omitted — a resource with no schema
URL is normal operation and its child scopes are still processed using
their own schema URL.

All metrics are `development` stability and use the standard OTel
collector internal telemetry infrastructure (`mdatagen`).

### Implementation

- Metrics are defined in `metadata.yaml` and generated via `mdatagen`
- `*metadata.TelemetryBuilder` is stored directly on `schemaProcessor`
and passed through to `NewManager` and `CacheableProvider`, following
the pattern used by `tailsamplingprocessor`, `spanpruningprocessor`, and
others
- `NewCacheableProvider` now returns `*CacheableProvider` directly
instead of `Provider`, removing the need for type assertions when wiring
telemetry
- Resource-level errors are counted inline (single occurrence per call,
returns immediately)
- Scope-level skipped/failed counts are accumulated locally and flushed
in a single `.Add()` call at the end of each `process*` method,
following the batching pattern used by other processors
- Scope-level errors use `continue` to avoid dropping the rest of the
batch — only resource-level errors propagate and abort processing

## Testing

- `TestSkipCounters` — verifies all three scope-level `*.skipped`
counters (logs/metrics/traces) are incremented when no schema URL is
present on the scope or its resource
- `TestFailedCounters` — verifies `resource.failed` and each signal's
`*.failed` counter using an error-returning provider
- `TestCacheableProviderCounters` — table-driven test verifying hit/miss
counters in `CacheableProvider`
- All existing tests pass

## Checklist

- [x] `make generate` run to regenerate telemetry code
- [x] All tests pass (`go test ./...`)
- [x] Changelog entry added

#### Description

[extension/cgroupruntime] Expose refresh_interval for GOMEMLIMIT (#46772)

**Description:**
This PR exposes the `refresh_interval` configuration for `GOMEMLIMIT` in
the `cgroupruntime` extension.

Currently, the extension sets `GOMEMLIMIT` only once at startup. In
dynamic environments (such as Kubernetes with Vertical Pod Autoscalers),
the container's memory limit may change at runtime. Without a refresh
interval, the Go runtime continues to use the stale memory limit
calculated at startup.

This change leverages the `WithRefreshInterval` option from the
underlying `automemlimit` library to allow periodic updates of the
memory limit.

**Link to tracking Issue:**
Resolves #46768

**Testing:**
- Added a new unit test case `memory limit with refresh interval` in
`extension_test.go` to verify the configuration is correctly passed to
the runtime.
- Ran `make test` and `make lint` locally.

**Documentation:**

[extension/bearertokenauth] Support comments in token file (#46186)

**Description:**
This PR updates the `bearertokenauth` extension to support inline
comments in the token file. Previously, adding a comment (e.g., `token #
comment`) would cause the entire line to be interpreted as the token,
leading to authentication failures.

The file reading logic has been updated to:
1. Parse each line of the token file.
2. Strip any content following the `#` character.
3. Trim surrounding whitespace.
4. Ignore empty lines resulting from comment-only lines.

**Link to tracking Issue:**
Fixes #46100

**Testing:**
- Added a new unit test `TestBearerTokenFileWithComments` in
`bearertokenauth_test.go`.
- The test verifies that:

    - Full-line comments are ignored.
    - Authentication succeeds with the stripped token.

[exporter/opensearch] Add pipeline option for ingest pipeline support (#47228)

#### Description
Add an optional `pipeline` configuration parameter to the OpenSearch
exporter. When set, the specified ingest pipeline ID is passed to the
bulk indexer, causing all documents to be
processed by the pipeline before being indexed in OpenSearch.

#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #47227

#### Testing
Testing was done manually by passing the `pipeline` option to a running
opensearch instance. Passing the name of an ingest pipeline that does
*not* exist, returns a permanent error (as expected). Also, a permanent
error is returned, if there is no node in the cluster, that has the
`ingest` node role assigned.

```
exporters:
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: <endpoint>
      tls:
        ...
    pipeline: otel-ingest-pipeline
```

#### Documentation
```
- `pipeline` (optional): the ID of an [ingest pipeline](https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/ingest-pipelines/) to apply when indexing documents. When set, all documents sent via the bulk API will be processed by the specified pipeline before being indexed. The ingest pipeline must exist in the cluster and there must be a least one node with the `ingest` node role assigned.
```

[extension/pebble_tail_storage] Implement tail storage pebble extension (#47883)

#### Description

2nd donation PR for `pebble_tail_storage`, building on the
skeleton from #47980. Adds the actual Pebble-backed implementation of
the
`TailStorage` interface used by the tail sampling processor:

- `storage.go` — buffer per trace ID, range-scoped Take/Delete via a
custom
  Pebble comparer that splits keys on the trace-ID/sequence boundary so
  prefix bloom filters and `DeleteRange` can be used efficiently.
- `pebble.go` — Pebble DB setup (cache, memtable, level options, value
  separation format major version, custom comparer).
- Wires `Append` / `Take` / `Delete` on the extension and opens the DB
in
  `Start` / closes in `Shutdown`.
- `ErrorIfExists: true` is set on the Pebble DB intentionally —
persistence
across restarts is not yet supported while the on-disk schema is in
heavy
development. README updated with a `Limitations` section explaining this
  and instructing operators to treat the directory as ephemeral.

#### Link to tracking issue

Fixes
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47916
(the donation tracking issue)

Part of
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/42326

#### Testing

- `storage_test.go` covers Append/Take/Delete roundtrips, including
range
  semantics for multi-span traces and isolation between trace IDs.
- `TestStartErrorsIfDBExists` guards the `ErrorIfExists` behavior —
re-Start
  on the same directory returns an error rather than silently reopening.
- mdatagen lifecycle test is skipped via `tests.skip_lifecycle: true` in
`metadata.yaml` (with a comment explaining why);
`TestStartErrorsIfDBExists`
fills the gap. The `shutdown` subtest still runs and asserts `Shutdown`
  before `Start` is a no-op.
- A separate `integrationtest/` Go submodule wires the extension through
a
  `tailsamplingprocessor` pipeline end-to-end, including benchmarks; its
  heavy deps stay out of the main module.
- `goleak` ignores the Pebble `diskHealthCheckingFS` ticker via
`tests.goleak.ignore.top` — Pebble does not tear it down when `Open`
fails
(e.g. the `ErrorIfExists` path), and we don't want to reach into Pebble
  internals.

#### Documentation

- README gains a `Limitations` section flagging the
no-persistence-across-
  restarts behavior as a temporary measure.
- Chloggen entry: `.chloggen/pebbletailstorageextension-impl.yaml`.

[chore][pkg/coreinternal] Fix parseGotime overwriting time.Local with named system timezone (#48091)

#### Description

Fixes `timeutils.ParseGotime` returning a concrete system timezone
location, such as `WET` or `CET`, when callers requested `time.Local`.

The `parseGotime` contains a correction for timezone abbreviations that
have an offset of zero but are not `UTC` (e.g., `BST`, `WET`). It
reloads the zone and re-parses to get the correct offset. However, this
correction was also firing when no timezone abbreviation was present in
the input at all. In that case, the zone name with offset zero came from
the caller's default `time.Local`, not from the parsed input. The reload
then replaced the `time.Local` pointer with a named `*time.Location`
(e.g., `WET`), which is semantically the same instant but breaks callers
that compare `time.Time` values structurally.

The fix adds a guard to skip the reload when the parsed zone name
matches the zone name of the caller's default location, meaning it could
only have come from the default and not from an abbreviation in the
input string.

Ran the OTTL package tests and verified the timezone-sensitive math test
no longer fails when the local timezone resolves to `WET`.

  responses were spuriously stamped with `UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION`
  client-side, and Produce v13 / OffsetFetch v10+ / OffsetCommit v10+
  could be sent with zero TopicIDs on the wire. The Produce path now
  caps at v12 if any partition lacks a TopicID, and OffsetFetch /
OffsetCommit now pin to v9 in the same situation. Fixes

[receiver/datadog] prune stale metrics series to prevent memory leak (#45564)

#### Description

This PR addresses a memory leak issue in the `datadogreceiver`'s metrics
translator when handling high cardinality data.

**The Problem:**
The `MetricsTranslator` maintains an internal map (`lastTs`) to track
the timestamps of metric series for SetStartTimestamp(). Currently, this
map grows indefinitely because stale series (e.g., from ephemeral pods
or one-off jobs) are never removed. In high cardinality scenarios, this
leads to linear memory growth and eventual OOM.

**The Solution:**
- Implemented a `Prune()` method in `MetricsTranslator` to remove series
that have not received data for a specific duration.
- Added a new configuration parameter: `series_idle_timeout`.
- **Default: `0s` (Disabled).** This ensures backward compatibility and
prevents data loss for sparse metrics (e.g., hourly cronjobs) where the
state must be preserved.
- Users experiencing high memory usage can configure this (e.g., `60m`)
to automatically clean up stale series.
- Added a background sweeper in `receiver.go` that triggers the pruning
process periodically if the timeout is configured.

**Design Considerations:**
We chose `series_idle_timeout` as the name to strictly define the
behavior: it cleans up specific *series* based on *idle* time, distinct
from connection timeouts (confighttp).

#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #45523

#### Documentation

- Updated `receiver/datadogreceiver/README.md` to document the new
`series_idle_timeout` parameter and provide recommendations for its
usage.
- Added code comments explaining the "opt-in" nature of this fix to
protect sparse metrics.

[processor/tailsampling] Fix drop, latency, and span count policies in span ingest mode (#47476)

#### Description

This fixes a few bugs that I found when trying span ingest mode:
1. f a drop policy is present it effectively means that it is not
possible to make a positive sampling decision on span ingest as a future
span could change the decision to be dropped. This change handles that
case by ensuring that there are no pending drop policies before allowing
a positive sampling decision. In addition, it stops the evaluation loop
if there is a pending drop policy as there is no point in wasting CPU
cycles.
2. If an upper bound is specified in a latency policy it is possible for
the decision to change from Sampled to NotSampled, therefore any latency
policy with an upper bound needs to be considered stateful.
3. Same as 2 but for when max spans was set for span count.

The two classes of fixes are in two separate commits for ease of review.
I can split into separate PRs if that would be helpful, but the second
class is very simple so hopefully one PR is ok. The user behavior
(seeing traces that should have been discarded) is the same for all the
issues.

#### Testing
Unit tests added for all scenarios

#### Description

Similar to
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/44572

Switch Namespace, Node, Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, and Job
informers from full typed objects to PartialObjectMetadata via the
metadata client. These resources only need labels, annotations, UID,
name, and owner references—all available in object metadata—so fetching
full spec/status is unnecessary overhead.

Pods continue using full objects since they require spec/status fields
(pod IP, node name, containers, host network).

Release 1.81.0

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/compare/v1.80.0...v1.81.0)

### Behavior Changes

- balancer/rls: Switch gauge metrics to asynchronous emission (once per
collection cycle) to reduce telemetry noise and align with other gRPC
language implementations.
([#​8808](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8808))

### Dependencies

- Minimum supported Go version is now 1.25.
([#​8969](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8969))

### Bug Fixes

- xds: Use the leaf cluster's security config for the TLS handshake
instead of the aggregate cluster's config.
([#​8956](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8956))
- transport: Send a `RST_STREAM` when receiving an `END_STREAM` when the
stream is not already half-closed.
([#​8832](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8832))
- xds: Fix ADS resource name validation to prevent a panic.
([#​8970](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8970))

### New Features

- grpc/stats: Add support for custom labels in per-call metrics ([gRFC
A108](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/proposal/blob/master/A108-otel-custom-per-call-label.md)).
([#​9008](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9008))
- xds: Add support for Server Name Indication (SNI) and SAN validation
([gRFC
A101](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/proposal/blob/master/A101-SNI-setting-and-SNI-SAN-validation.md)).
Disabled by default. To enable, set `GRPC_EXPERIMENTAL_XDS_SNI=true`
environment variable.
([#​9016](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9016))
- xds: Add support to control which fields get propagated from ORCA
backend metric reports to LRS load reports ([gRFC
A85](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/proposal/blob/master/A85-lrs-custom-metrics-changes.md)).
Disabled by default. To enable, set
`GRPC_EXPERIMENTAL_XDS_ORCA_LRS_PROPAGATION=true`.
([#​9005](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9005))
- xds: Add metrics to track xDS client connectivity and cached resource
state ([gRFC
A78](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/proposal/blob/master/A78-grpc-metrics-wrr-pf-xds.md)).
([#​8807](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8807))
- stats/otel: Enhance `grpc.subchannel.disconnections` metric by adding
disconnection reason to the `grpc.disconnect_error` label ([gRFC
A94](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/proposal/blob/master/A94-subchannel-otel-metrics.md)).
This provides granular insights into why subchannels are closing.
([#​8973](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8973))
- mem: Add `mem.Buffer.Slice()` API to slice the buffer like a slice.
([#​8977](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8977))
  - Special Thanks: [@​ash2k](https://redirect.github.com/ash2k)

### Performance Improvements

- alts: Pool read buffers to lower memory utilization when sockets are
unreadable.
([#​8964](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8964))
- transport: Pool HTTP/2 framer read buffers to reduce idle memory
consumption. Currently limited to Linux for ALTS and non-encrypted
transports (TCP, Unix). To disable, set
`GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_HTTP_FRAMER_READ_BUFFER_POOLING=false` and report
any issues.
([#​9032](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9032))

#### Description

Some AI coding tools (notably Claude Code) inject a `Co-authored-by:`
trailer into commit messages by default. When that trailer references an
account that has not signed the CLA, EasyCLA fails and blocks the PR
from being merged. Make the existing `Assisted-by:` guidance in
`AGENTS.md` explicit about this so contributors know to disable or strip
the `Co-authored-by:` trailer before committing.

a panic (`unexpected nil stream`). If the background stream runner shut
down before the test called `mustSendAndWait`, the stream evaluated to
`nil`. This updates `mustSendAndWait` to gracefully return
`ErrStreamRestarting` instead of panicking when the stream is `nil`.

**Testing:**
Ran `make test` and `make lint` in `exporter/otelarrowexporter/`.

[exporter/kafka] Fix collector hanging indefinitely on shutdown when the Kafka broker is unreachable (#48144)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

The Kafka exporter hung indefinitely on shutdown when the broker was
unreachable. `WithTimeout` had been disabled in the factory, so
`ProduceSync` had no deadline and was blocked forever. Since the queue
must drain before `Close` is called, the collector never shuts down.

Re-enables `WithTimeout` with the configured timeout (default 5s) and
passes the per-attempt context through to `ProduceSync`. When the broker
is unreachable, it sends unblock after the timeout, the queue drains,
and `Close` is reached.

Re-enables `WithTimeout` with the configured timeout (default 5s) and
passes the per-attempt context through to `ProduceSync`. Users with slow
brokers or large batches may need to increase this (e.g., timeout: 30s).
Franz-go `ProduceRequestTimeout` is set to the same value, so
broker-side and collector-side deadlines stay aligned.

[receiver/mysql] strip leading sql comments before explain check (#46827)

Description

Fixes an issue where EXPLAIN was skipped for queries starting with SQL
comments. Some tools (e.g., DBeaver) prepend queries with comments like
/* ApplicationName=... */, which caused isQueryExplainable to miss the
actual SQL keyword.

This change strips leading block (/* ... */) and line (-- ...) comments
before checking the query keyword, allowing EXPLAIN to run correctly.

Fixes #46587.

explainable queries (SELECT, DELETE, INSERT, REPLACE, UPDATE) and non
explainable queries

Refactor heuristics for deployment and cronjob name extraction (#47431)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
The following PR attempts to improve the label extraction logic for both
deployment name and cron job name in k8s attributes processor.

Whilst this attributes do not "turn-on" the informer, they still first
attempt to use any informer data if available (In case the informer was
enabled due to some other attribute). In this instance, the informer
running cost has already been 'paid', so using it ensures getting the
correct data.

If no data could be fetched at the informer level, then the code falls
back to heuristic similar to the ones before, but slightly improved to
prevent incorrect matches.

- Deployment name relied on `pod-template-hash` label added to pods from
k8s deployments. The presence of this label guarantees that we are
dealing with a deployment (pods from a user created replica set do not
contain this label). Moreover, the deployment name can be computed by
removing the `pod-template-hash` suffix from the replicaset name.

- For the CronJob name, the regex is improved to account for the fact
that the final digits on the Job name match the unix job creating time
in minutes. Hence, we can check for 8 digits and that the pod creation
time is somewhat close to the job creation time. (Window was set to 59
minutes, but could be increased).

[processor/k8sattributes] Add watch_sync_period configuration option (#48111)

#### Description

This PR implements the configurable options for `watch_sync_period`
(resync period) `k8sattributes` processor, addressing a hardcoded TODO
inside the informer client.

By default, `watch_sync_period` is set to `5m` as previously harcoded
before, even though we recommend setting it to `0s` (disabled). In
large-scale Kubernetes clusters (e.g., 100K pods), periodically
reprocessing the informer cache every 5 minutes (previously hardcoded)
enqueues every single pod object back into the event handlers. This
causes significant CPU spikes, memory allocations, and GC churn for no
actual benefit since pod updates are already pushed immediately via
active watch events. Setting it to `0` disables this resync completely
while allowing users to set it to a custom duration (e.g., `1h`) if a
self-healing failsafe is desired.

Addresses
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48110

#### Description

Bumps `golang.org/x/net` to `v0.53.0` across all modules that pinned an
older version (`v0.51.0` / `v0.52.0`) to address
[GO-2026-4918](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4918): an infinite loop
in the HTTP/2 transport when handling a bad `SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE` in

```

  → http2.Transport.NewClientConn
```

Other modules carry the same vulnerable indirect dependency, so this PR
sweeps them all in one shot — same approach as the prior bump in #46475.

#### How it was applied

Per affected module:

```
go get golang.org/x/net@v0.53.0
go mod tidy
```

The diff is restricted to
`golang.org/x/{net,crypto,sys,sync,term,mod,tools,text}` entries — all
cascading transitive updates from x/net's own go.mod.

add include_all_containers option to dockerobserver (#48252)

#### Description

Adds a new `include_all_containers` option (default `false`) to the
dockerobserver extension. When enabled, the observer emits a port-less
endpoint for every running, non-paused container, alongside the existing
per-port endpoints. This makes containers without exposed ports
discoverable by `receiver_creator` rules matching `type == "container"
and port == 0`, allowing attaching log receivers (or any other
per-container receiver) to every container regardless of whether it
exposes ports.

The change is purely additive: with the flag off, behavior is
byte-identical to the current implementation. The new endpoint has `ID =
<containerID>`, `Target = <host>` (no port), `Port` and `AlternatePort`
of `0`, and `Transport` of unknown. To attach exactly one receiver per
container, rules should scope with `port == 0`; the README documents
this to avoid duplicate-receiver footguns when mixing with existing
port-based rules.

[receiver/oracledbreceiver] Add operational metrics (#47310)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

The Oracle DB receiver currently lacks metrics for data dictionary cache
efficiency, recycle bin usage, and overall database storage utilization.
These are common operational metrics that database administrators
monitor and are available in the AppDynamics DB agent but missing from
the OpenTelemetry receiver.

This PR adds 4 new opt-in metrics (disabled by default, stability:
development):

- `oracledb.data_dictionary_hit_ratio` — Cache hit ratio from
`v$rowcache`, expressed as a percentage
- `oracledb.recycle_bin_size` — Total size of the recycle bin in
megabytes
- `oracledb.storage.allocated` — Total allocated database storage from
`dba_data_files` in megabytes
- `oracledb.storage.used_pct` — Percentage of allocated database storage
that is used

These metrics can be enabled in the collector configuration:

```
yaml
receivers:
  oracledb:
    datasource: "oracle://user:password@host:1521/service"
    metrics:
      oracledb.data_dictionary_hit_ratio:
        enabled: true
      oracledb.recycle_bin_size:
        enabled: true
      oracledb.storage.allocated:
        enabled: true
      oracledb.storage.used_pct:
        enabled: true
```

fix(k8sattributes): restore otelcol.k8s.pod.association metric with low-cardinality pod_identifier (#48094)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
Use association source type/name instead of actual identifier values to
prevent unbounded metric time series growth.

The `otelcol.k8s.pod.association` metric was disabled in #47798 because
its `pod_identifier` attribute used actual pod values (IPs, UIDs) which
created one metric time series per distinct pod ever seen, growing
unboundedly.

This PR re-enables the metric with a proper fix: `pod_identifier` now
encodes the **association source type and name** (e.g. `"connection"`,
`"resource_attribute/k8s.pod.ip"`) rather than the actual identifier
value. Cardinality is now bounded by the number of configured
association rules.

protocol_version validation in pkg/kafka/configkafka from

feat(processor/schema): add migration mode to preserve attributes during version changes (#47906)

#### Description

This PR adds two features to the schema processor:

**1. Migration mode for safe schema version transitions**

When migrating between schema versions, attribute renames normally
hard-delete the old name. This makes it difficult to update queries,
dashboards, and alerts without a service interruption — the old
attribute names silently stop matching.

The new `migration` config section preserves both old and new attribute
names for renames between a specified version range. This gives
operators a safe migration window to update their downstream consumers
before committing to the new names.

Each migration entry specifies a `target` (must match one of the
configured targets) and a `from` version (must be in the same schema
family). Only renames between `from` and `target` are copied — earlier
renames are hard-renamed as normal, preventing an explosion of
attributes when migrating across many versions. This works for both
upgrades (`from` < target) and downgrades (`from` > target).

When both the source and target attribute already exist on an incoming
signal, neither is overwritten.

```yaml
processors:
  schema:
    targets:
      - https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.14.0
    migration:
      - target: https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.14.0
        from: https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.13.0
```

**2. Translation counter metric**

Adds `processor_schema.translated` — a counter that records every schema
translation with `from_schema_url` and `to_schema_url` attributes. This
gives operators visibility into what schema versions are flowing through
the processor.

When migration is active, the metric also includes a
`migration_from_schema_url` attribute indicating the migration boundary.
This provides a way to track migration activity and detect if migration
mode is left on too long — without mutating the underlying telemetry
data.

**3. Conflict handling improvement**

Improves conflict handling in the non-migration path: when the rename
target already exists with an identical value, no error is reported
(previously this was always an error). The schema file format spec does
not define behavior for name conflicts (see
[spec#3497](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/issues/3497)).

#### Related specifications

-
[spec#3510](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/issues/3510)
— proposes that schema transformations should preserve original
attributes. This PR implements that capability with scoped version
ranges to control cardinality.
-
[spec#3497](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/issues/3497)
— the spec doesn't define conflict behavior when a rename target already
exists. This PR treats same-value conflicts as no-ops.

#### Link to tracking issue

Fixes #47420
Part of #47428

#### Testing

**Config validation tests:**
- nil migration, empty from (error), valid from + target, invalid URL
(error), family mismatch (error), target not in targets (error),
duplicate migration target (error)

**Unit tests (AttributeChangeSet):**
- Copy mode apply: basic rename preserves both names
- Copy mode apply: both source and target exist — both preserved with
original values
- Copy mode apply: no match — unchanged
- Copy mode rollback: preserves both names
- Same-value conflict in non-copy mode: no error

**E2E tests (processor):**
- Upgrade with migration: both old and new attributes present
- Upgrade without migration: only new attribute (hard rename)
- Downgrade with migration: both old and new attributes present
- Both attributes already exist: neither overwritten

**Translation counter tests:**
- Records `from_schema_url` and `to_schema_url` after translation
- Includes `migration_from_schema_url` when migration is active

All existing tests pass.

#### Documentation

README updated with migration section including config reference table,
scoping explanation, workflow steps, and upgrade/downgrade/multi-family
examples.

Added GUIDE.md — an operators guide covering the problem (inconsistent
semconv versions), how the processor works, migration workflows,
monitoring, and operational recommendations.

feat(processor/schema): promote to alpha stability (#48307)

#### Description

Promotes the schema processor from `development` to `alpha` stability
and adds it to the `contrib` distribution.

This follows significant work to improve the processor's correctness,
reliability, and observability:

**Bug fixes:**
- Fix upgrade path silently applying no changes (#47632)
- Fix mutex held during HTTP schema fetch (#47633)
- Fix panic on malformed span_events entry (#47634)
- Fix inconsistent scope-level error handling (#47634)
- Fix context.Background() used instead of pipeline ctx (#47634)
- Fix CacheableProvider rate-limit reset (#47871)
- Fix prefetch errors silently discarded (#47871)
- Fix MetricTypeEmpty causing scope-level errors (#47872)

**Features:**
- Add internal telemetry metrics (#47638)
- Add migration mode for safe schema version transitions (#47906)
- Add storage extension support for persistent caching (#48267)
- Add operators guide (GUIDE.md)

**Spec compliance:**
The processor correctly implements the OTel schema file format v1.1
upgrade/downgrade behavior:
- Upgrades apply renames forward, downgrades apply them in reverse
- Ordering follows the spec (all section first, then signal-specific,
reversed for downgrades)

#### Link to tracking issue

Part of #47428

#### Testing

All existing tests pass. No new tests needed for this change — it only
modifies metadata and generated status files.

#### Documentation

README autogenerated section updated to reflect alpha stability and
contrib distribution.

[internal/filter/filterottl] Add NewBoolExprFor*WithPathContextNames (#48279)

## Description

I'm working on moving more components to the new OTTL syntax that can
infer context. Many components depend on filter OTTL indirectly through
filterottl. Instead of having each component drop its filterottl
dependency and manage a parser collection themselves, we want to add
support in filterottl for the new syntax.

[processor/tailsampling] Switch `rate_limiting` to a token bucket algorithm with `burst_capacity` (#48226)

#### Description

The `rate_limiting` policy has a strict `spans_per_second` limit
enforced each second. This means traces larger than `spans_per_second`
can never be ingested.
This PR changes the implementation to uses a token bucket algorithm from
https://golang.org/x/time/rate. The rate limiter has a burst capacity
which can sample a large trace at once.

This is almost identical to how the `bytes_limiting` policy works.

Note: this is a slight change in behaviour. Traces that were not sampled
by the previous implementation might be sampled now using burst
capacity. I think this is acceptable since the intention of the policy
didn't change and over time it will still sample at a`spans_per_second`
rate of spans.
If a user relied on never sampling more than `spans_per_second` each
second, they can set `burst_capacity = spans_per_second`.

#### Testing

Updated/added new tests.

#### Documentation

Updated the README.

feat(processor/drain): snapshot persistence via storage extension (#48076)

#### Description

Add snapshot persistence to the drain processor via the collector's
storage extension API. The Drain tree state is saved on shutdown (and
optionally at a periodic interval) and restored on startup, eliminating
the need for seed templates and warmup on subsequent runs.

When a shared storage backend (Redis, database) is used with
`save_interval`, periodic saves allow new instances in a scaled
deployment to inherit a trained tree from already-running instances,
avoiding the cold-start problem.

New config fields:
- `storage` — ID of a storage extension. Optional; when unset the
processor remains stateless (current behavior).
- `save_interval` — interval between periodic snapshot saves. `0s`
(default) saves on shutdown only.

Key behaviors:
- When a valid snapshot is loaded, `seed_templates`/`seed_logs` are
skipped (already baked in)
- Warmup is bypassed if the restored cluster count meets
`warmup_min_clusters`
- FNV-1a hash check avoids redundant writes when the tree hasn't changed
- Corrupt snapshots fall back to seeding gracefully

#### Example configuration

```yaml
extensions:
  file_storage:
    directory: /var/lib/otelcol/drain

receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:

processors:
  drain:
    storage: file_storage
    save_interval: 5m

exporters:
  debug:
    verbosity: detailed

service:
  extensions: [file_storage]
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [drain]
      exporters: [debug]
```

#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #48075

Follow-up to #47235 (original drain processor proposal), which listed
snapshot persistence as a deferred scope item.

#### Testing

8 new tests in `storage_test.go` covering:
- Start/shutdown without storage (stateless backward compat)
- Snapshot persist and reload round-trip
- Loaded snapshot skips seeds
- Loaded snapshot skips warmup
- Corrupt snapshot falls back to seeds
- Storage extension not found error
- Periodic save via `save_interval`
- Hash-gated write skip when tree unchanged

All existing tests updated to go through the full `Start()`/`Shutdown()`
lifecycle.

Manually tested end-to-end with `file_storage`: sent 8 log records,
verified periodic save wrote to disk, restarted collector and confirmed
snapshot loaded with `"loaded drain tree snapshot from storage,
clusters: 3"`.

#### Documentation

README updated with new `storage` and `save_interval` parameters, a new
"Snapshot persistence" section covering lifecycle, shared storage for
scaled deployments, and snapshot size estimates (~120 bytes/cluster,
under 600 KB even at 5,000 clusters). "Snapshot persistence" moved out
of the "Future extensions" section.

Feat/awslogsencoding subscription filter routing (#47976)

#### Description

This PR adds support for dispatching CloudWatch Logs subscription-filter
events to different inner encoding extensions, based on each event's
`logGroup` and/or `logStream`. A new `cloudwatch.streams` list is added
under the `cloudwatch` format. Each entry maps a `log_group_pattern`
and/or `log_stream_pattern` (or a known service `name` carrying default
patterns and payload mode) to an inner encoding extension's
`component.ID` and selects how that envelope is passed to the inner
(`message` per-event, or full `envelope` bytes).

Inner extensions are declared as dependencies via
[`extensioncapabilities.Dependent`](https://pkg.go.dev/go.opentelemetry.io/collector/extension/extensioncapabilities#Dependent),
so the collector starts them before this extension.

This is the follow-up to the previous attempt #47878 (closed). After
discussion with @axw, the routing logic was moved out of the
`awslambdareceiver` and into the encoding extension, where:

- Any push-based receiver consuming CW subscription events (Lambda
today, Firehose etc.) inherits multi-format support without
receiver-side changes.
- Inner targets can be any extension implementing `plog.Unmarshaler`
(i.e. any `encoding.LogsUnmarshalerExtension`), including third-party
encoders — not limited to the built-in `aws_logs_encoding` formats.

Routing decisions are made **per envelope**: CloudWatch payloads that
aggregate multiple envelopes from different log groups (common with
Firehose) are matched independently against the routing table.

##### Configuration example (taken from README)

```yaml
extensions:
  awslogs_encoding/vpcflow:
    format: vpcflow
  awslogs_encoding/cloudtrail:
    format: cloudtrail
  awslogs_encoding/cw_default:
    format: cloudwatch

  awslogs_encoding/cw_router:
    format: cloudwatch
    cloudwatch:
      streams:
        - name: vpcflow
          encoding: awslogs_encoding/vpcflow      # default log_stream_pattern: "eni-*", payload: envelope
        - name: cloudtrail
          encoding: awslogs_encoding/cloudtrail   # default log_stream_pattern: "*_CloudTrail_*", payload: envelope
        - name: lambda
          encoding: awslogs_encoding/cw_default   # default log_group_pattern: "/aws/lambda/*", payload: message
        - name: catchall
          log_group_pattern: "*"
          encoding: awslogs_encoding/cw_default

receivers:
  awslambda:
    cloudwatch:
      encoding: awslogs_encoding/cw_router
```

##### Default patterns and payload modes

Known service names carry built-in defaults so users do not have to know
AWS-specific naming conventions:

| `name` | Default field | Default pattern | Default `payload` |

|--------------|----------------------|----------------------------------|-------------------|
| `vpcflow` | `log_stream_pattern` | `eni-*` | `envelope` |
| `cloudtrail` | `log_stream_pattern` | `*_CloudTrail_*` | `envelope` |
| `lambda` | `log_group_pattern` | `/aws/lambda/*` | `message` |
| `waf` | `log_group_pattern` | `aws-waf-logs-*` | `message` |
| `rds` | `log_group_pattern` | `/aws/rds/instance/*/*` | `message` |
| `eks` | `log_group_pattern` | `/aws/eks/*` | `message` |
| `apigateway` | `log_group_pattern` | `API-Gateway-Execution-Logs_*` |
`message` |

For names not in this table the default `payload` is `message`.
`vpcflow` and `cloudtrail` default to `envelope` because their inner
encoders have CloudWatch-envelope-aware code paths; the others default
to `message` because their typical inner encoders expect a single record
per call.

Patterns support exact literals, `*` for a full segment, and affix
wildcards (`foo*`, `*foo`, `*foo*`). Streams are sorted at start time by
a three-level precedence rule (catch-all last → `log_group_pattern`
before `log_stream_pattern`-only → more-specific first). Declaration
order in YAML does not matter.

#### Link to tracking issue

Part of #46458. The S3 portion was completed in #47237.

#### Testing

Unit tests added at every layer: pattern matching, default application,
validation, sort precedence, route resolution against a fake host, and
per-envelope dispatch on aggregated payloads.

#### Documentation

- New **"Routing CloudWatch subscription-filter events to other
encodings"** section in the extension README.
- Changelog entry `.chloggen/awslogsencoding-cw-routing.yaml` under the
`extension/aws_logs_encoding` component.

[receiver/awscloudwatch] Add metrics receiver (#47295)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

Adds an initial implementation of a metrics receiver to the existing
awscloudwatchreceiver using the CloudWatch GetMetricData and ListMetrics
APIs. The idea came after a brief conversation on Slack with @schmikei
(code owner). The implementation aims to build on top of
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/14449,
adding a new `metrics` section to the configuration.

Metric output aims to be aligned with the [CloudWatch Metric Streams
OpenTelemetry 1.0.0
format](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-metric-streams-formats-opentelemetry-100.html)
to be consistent with the `awscloudwatchmetricstreamsencodingextension`.

Metrics can be configured in two ways:

- Explicit list: define specific metrics by namespace, metric name,
dimensions, and statistic
- Autodiscovery: use ListMetrics API to discover metrics dynamically,
with optional namespace and metric name filters

##### Metric representation

- Metric name: `amazonaws.com/{Namespace}/{MetricName}` (original
CloudWatch casing preserved)
- Resource attributes: cloud.provider = aws, cloud.region = <region>
- Data point attributes: Namespace, MetricName, Dimensions (kvlist)
- Default output type: Summary (Sum, SampleCount, Minimum, Maximum
combined into a single data point)
With explicit stats: Gauge (one data point per statistic, tagged with a
stat attribute)

*Config example*

```
receivers:
  awscloudwatch:
    region: us-east-1
    metrics:
      collection_interval: 5m
      period: 300s
      delay: 10m
      queries:
        - namespace: AWS/EC2
          metric_name: CPUUtilization
          dimensions:
            InstanceId: i-1234567890abcdef0
        - namespace: AWS/EC2
          metric_name: NetworkIn
          stats:
            - Average
            - p99
```

#### Description
**Adding a feature:** Expose new optional
`k8s.container.ephemeral_storage.usage` metric from `kubeletstats`
receiver.

Currently, the `kubeletstats` receiver maps `container.filesystem.usage`
exclusively to the container's rootfs (the container write layer). It
does not track the filesystem usage of the container's logs (standard

resource limits are calculated by summing both rootfs and logs usage.

`metadata.yaml` (disabled by default as an optional metric, consider
replacing it with current fs.usage later).
2. Adding a `fs.type` metric attribute with supported values `rootfs`
and `logs` to allow independent tracking and aggregation.
3. Updating the `kubelet` stats accumulator to scrape
`ContainerStats.Rootfs.UsedBytes` and `ContainerStats.Logs.UsedBytes`
from the Kubelet Summary API and report them under the new metric
family.

[receiver/prometheusremotewrite] replace string-based hashing with identity library (#48165)

## Description

Replace all `xxhash`-based string-concatenation hashing in the
Prometheus Remote Write receiver with `internal/exp/metrics/identity`
and FNV-based hashing, eliminating intermediate string allocations and
aligning with the hashing approach used elsewhere in the collector.

### Changes

**`metricIdentity.Hash()`**  
Previously concatenated all fields into a single string and hashed with
`xxhash`. Now uses `identity.Resource.Hash()` (which returns an
`fnv.New64a()` seeded from the resource attributes) as the base hasher,
then writes scope and metric fields as raw bytes separated by `\xff` (a
non-UTF-8 byte that cannot appear in metric or label names, preventing
boundary collisions like `"ab"+"c"` vs `"a"+"bc"`).

**`getOrCreateRM()`**  
Previously allocated a temporary `pcommon.Resource`, set job/instance
attributes on it, and called `identity.OfResource()` to hash it — one
heap allocation per time series. Now hashes the `job` and `instance`
label strings directly using `identity.Resource{}.Hash()`, avoiding the
allocation entirely while producing a cache key in the same FNV hash
space.

**`processHistogramTimeSeries()` histogram cache key**  
Same approach as `metricIdentity.Hash()` — replaces string concatenation
+ xxhash with `identity.Resource.Hash()` extended with scope and metric
fields, with `\xff` separators. Also fixes a bug where the hash returned
from `getOrCreateRM` was discarded (`_`), causing the resource-creation
guard to re-run on every histogram in the series.

**`exemplarKey.hash()`**  
Replaces `xxhash.Sum64String(strings.Join(...))` with
`identity.Resource{}.Hash()` extended with the exemplar key fields,
using the same `\xff` separator pattern.

Adds a framework to the supervisor that allows it to utilize extensions

being called twice (once when loading the config from file and again

also allows us to:

in the config
3. validate the configuration after validating if the feature-gate is
valid

iterate through it and any substructures calling an implemented

returned as one error.

[chore][pkg/ottl][processor/transformprocessor] Add tests confirming OTTL accepts relaxed metric instrument names (#48345)

**Description**

Adds dedicated unit tests demonstrating that the OTTL `metric.name` path
getter/setter and statement pipeline already accept arbitrary UTF-8
strings, including metric instrument names that are currently disallowed
by the OpenTelemetry specification's [instrument name
syntax](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/main/specification/metrics/api.md#instrument-name-syntax)
(e.g. names containing `:`, `\`, spaces, or starting with a
non-alphabetic character).

These are **test-only additions, no production code changes.** They
serve as evidence — to be linked from a forthcoming spec PR — that
relaxing the instrument-name restrictions in the spec does **not**
require any corresponding change in the OpenTelemetry Collector / OTTL.

**Background**

The Specification SIG has discussed relaxing the instrument-name
character restrictions multiple times (see issues linked below). One of
the conditions for moving forward, raised in the Spec SIG meeting, was
to confirm that relaxing names would not break OTTL transforms in the
Collector. These tests confirm that:

- `pkg/ottl/contexts/internal/ctxmetric` and
`pkg/ottl/contexts/ottlmetric` treat the `name` path as an opaque string
— Get returns and Set persists any UTF-8 input byte-identically
(including names with `:`, `\`, spaces, leading `-` / `.`, emoji, empty
string, and length > 255).
- `processor/transformprocessor` parses and executes statements such as
`set(metric.name, "with:colon") where metric.name == "old:name"`
end-to-end without error, for the same set of relaxed names.

OTTL string literals are pure UTF-8 by grammar; the only identifier
restrictions in OTTL apply to grammar tokens (function names, path
segments), not to string-literal contents — so this is exactly the
result expected from inspection of the grammar, now backed by automated
tests.

#### Description

The batch scraper emits points using the original Azure timestamp but
did
not throttle re-scrapes of the same (resourceType, compositeKey) pair,
unlike the non-batch scraper. When collection_interval was shorter than
a metric's Azure timeGrain (e.g. 10s vs PT1M), the same (labels, ts)

so a (resourceType, compositeKey) pair is not re-scraped more often than
its Azure timeGrain.

[receiver/saphana] Enable re-aggregation feature (#48364)

- Set `reaggregation_enabled: true` in `metadata.yaml`
- Mark attributes whose removal still yields meaningful aggregations as
`recommended`
- Mark `database`, `product`, `service_memory_used_type`, and `system`
as `required` for now because aggregating across them doesn't provide
any meaningful results:
- **product**: used in saphana.license.expiration.time,
saphana.license.limit, saphana.license.peak. SAP HANA licenses are
per-product (e.g., "memory", "cpu", "user-count"). The limit/peak values
for different products use different units of measurement, a memory
license is in bytes, a CPU license is in cores, a user license is a
count. Summing or averaging across products mixes these units into a
meaningless number.
- **system**: same three license metrics plus saphana.uptime. A system
is a SAP HANA system identifier. License values are scoped per system,
so summing licenses across systems double-counts entitlements. For
uptime, summing uptimes across systems is meaningless (you'd get
something like "12 system-hours"; not a real duration).
- **database**: used in saphana.uptime. Uptime is per-database. Summing
uptimes across databases doesn't represent any real time interval;
averaging is also misleading because individual database uptimes are
  independent.
- **service_memory_used_type**: used in saphana.service.memory.used with
values logical and physical. These are two views of the same underlying
memory: physical = actual RAM used by the process, logical = memory the
process believes it has allocated. They are not disjoint partitions —
they overlap. Summing them double-counts the same bytes.
- Regenerate metadata package and update `config_test.go` for the new
per-metric config types

feat(processor/schema): add storage extension support for persistent schema caching (#48267)

#### Description

Schema files fetched over HTTP are now optionally persisted to a storage
extension. On subsequent startups, schemas are loaded from storage
without requiring network access.

A new `StorageProvider` wraps the HTTP provider as a read-through cache:
1. Check persistent storage for a cached schema
2. On miss, delegate to the HTTP provider
3. Persist the fetched schema to storage (best-effort)

This gives operators:
- **Faster cold starts** — schemas available immediately without HTTP
fetches
- **Offline operation** — the collector can translate schemas without
internet access after the initial fetch
- **Reduced load on schema servers** — fewer HTTP requests to the
servers hosting the schema files

```yaml
    directory: /var/lib/otelcol/schema_cache

processors:
  schema:
    targets:
      - https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.26.0
    storage: file_storage/schemas

service:
  extensions: [file_storage/schemas]
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [schema]
```

[chore] experiment with scoping build-and-test to only changed files (#48320)

#### Description

- related to
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/27807

This PR adds a new experimental workflow that is a copy of
`build-and-test.yaml` with several performance improvements.

- `detect-scope` — labels each PR `scoped` / `full` / `skip` from
changed files; everything below gates on this.
- Scoped lint, integration, and unit tests — `make
for-affected-components` instead of the 16-group matrices on typical
PRs.
- Scoped cross-compile — per-arch `go build ./...` on affected modules
instead of rebuilding `otelcontribcol`. `cmd/otelcontribcol/` changes
force `mode=full`.
- PR unittest matrix drops `stable` Go. Stable still runs on main.
- `exp-checks` split into 6 parallel matrix shards (`codegen`,
`porto-and-gci`, `go-mod-hygiene`, `small-generators`,
`schemas-and-templates`, `read-only-checks`) so file-modifying codegen
targets get isolated working trees.

**Wall time on a 1-file scoped PR: ~30m → ~8m.**

| Job | Full | Scoped |
|---|---|---|
| lint | ~17m | ~4m |
| unit tests | ~14m | ~4m |
| integration | ~10m | ~3m |
| cross-compile / arch | ~10m | ~3m |
| checks | ~12m | ~7m |

**Tried and rejected:** `~/.cache/go-build` cache on cross-compile —
evicted from GitHub's 10 GB-per-repo cache budget before it could warm
up.

Because scoped checks is riskier, I'd like to add this workflow as a
separate workflow and let it run next to the real `build-and-test` and
then do some comparisons/checks to ensure it wasn't missing stuff.

Example run:
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/actions/runs/25815208184?pr=48320

[exporter/loadbalancingexporter] Add owner_account support to AWS Cloud Map resolver (#47895)

Adding owner_account to AWS Cloud Map resolver

#### Description

Adds `owner_account` configuration option to the AWS Cloud Map resolver,
enabling cross-account namespace discovery via [AWS RAM shared
namespaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloud-map/latest/dg/sharing-namespaces.html).

The `DiscoverInstances`
[API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloud-map/latest/api/API_DiscoverInstances.html)
accepts an `OwnerAccount` parameter for querying instances in a
namespace shared from another AWS account, but the load balancing
exporter's Cloud Map integration never set it. When omitted, behavior is
unchanged.

#### Link to tracking issue

#### Testing

Added `TestCloudMapResolutionWithOwnerAccount` with a mock that asserts
the `OwnerAccount` field is correctly propagated to the
`DiscoverInstances` API call. All existing tests continue to pass.

Validated end-to-end by building a custom collector from this branch and
deploying it as an ECS sidecar. Without `owner_account`, the resolver
returns `NamespaceNotFound` for a cross-account RAM-shared namespace.
With `owner_account` set, the resolver successfully discovers instances.

#### Documentation

The new `owner_account` field is documented via the `mapstructure` tag
on the config struct. Changelog entry added as this is user-facing.

[scraper/zookeeper] fix float parsing for zk_avg_latency on ZK 3.7+ (#47407)

Zookeeper 3.7+ reports `zk_avg_latency` as a float (e.g. `0.0989`),
which causes `strconv.ParseInt` to fail silently, dropping the
`zookeeper.latency.avg` metric entirely.

Fall back to `strconv.ParseFloat` when `ParseInt` fails, truncating the
result to `int64` to match the existing metric schema.

Fixes #47320

This patch release contains two narrow bug fixes and one small feature.
Deps are also bumped so that you are force-pinned to a
klauspost/compress
version that has a stack-splitting bugfix that sometimes affected
franz-go.

- `PurgeTopicsFromConsuming` now correctly persists deleted topics if
  you also had specific topics paused. Previously, when a topic had
  partition-level pauses, unpausing the topic itself (while keeping
  specific partitions paused) was bugged and the topic was stuck in
an "all paused" state (thanks
[@​gorakdev](https://redirect.github.com/gorakdev)!).

- `PollFetches` no longer surfaces a spurious `UNSTABLE_OFFSET_COMMIT`
  fetch error when an OffsetFetch retry is canceled mid-wait by a
  rebalance or client close. Observed flaking `TestTxnEtl/sticky/848`
  on KIP-848 consumer groups under transactional load.

- The MSK IAM SASL mechanism now honors `AWS_REGION` when the broker
  hostname does not match the standard MSK URL format, allowing
  connections through custom DNS names (e.g. private link endpoints)
(thanks
[@​janmoritzmeyer0210](https://redirect.github.com/janmoritzmeyer0210)!).

#### Description

Extracts the core basic auth primitives from `basicauthextension` into a
new `extension/internal/basicauth` package so they can be reused by a
standalone AWS Secrets Manager auth extension (see #48277, #48406)
without duplicating logic or pulling the AWS SDK into
basicauthextension.

The new internal package provides:
- `Authenticate()` — server-side header extraction, parsing, and
credential validation
- `CredentialProvider` interface — abstraction for username/password
sourcing
- `NewRoundTripper()` — HTTP transport with basic auth injection
- `NewPerRPCCredentials()` — gRPC per-RPC credentials with basic auth

The existing `basicauthextension` is updated to delegate to the internal
package. No user-facing behavior changes.

Related to #48277

credentials

[processor/cardinalityguardian] PR-2: Add core enforcement logic and inline spatial reaggregation (#48254)

#### Description

This is the second PR for the donation of the **Cardinality Guardian
Processor**, building upon the initial component PR.

This PR implements the core engine and logic of the processor,
introducing:
- **Core Processing Engine (`processor.go`)**: High-performance
256-shard `RWMutex` architecture wrapping AxiomHQ's HyperLogLog sketch
for sub-millisecond identity tracking.
- **Enforcement Modes (`config.go`)**: Added support for the three
primary enforcement actions when cardinality exceeds limits:
1. `tag_only`: Non-destructive metric auditing via
`otel.metric.overflow: true`.
2. `overflow_attribute`: Hard attribute value replacement to collapse
rogue identities.
  3. `strip_and_reaggregate`: Complete attribute stripping.
- **Spatial Reaggregation (`reaggregation.go`)**: Custom inline logic to
safely merge structural collisions created by the
`strip_and_reaggregate` mode (summing `Delta Sums` and tracking the most
recent `Gauge` values).
- **Background Rotation**: Memory-safe epoch rotation timers to
gracefully roll over HyperLogLog sketches.

#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #47368

#### Testing
- Ported the exhaustive test suite (`processor_test.go` and
`reaggregation_test.go`), ensuring massive structural parity and
edge-case coverage.
- Added fuzz testing (`processor_fuzz_test.go`) to ensure stability
under heavy, malformed attribute loads.
- Validated that the component passes all strict `golangci-lint`
requirements (including `forbidigo`, `revive`, and Go 1.22+ syntax
updates).
- Performed local integration testing by compiling the component into
`otelcontribcol` and firing live OTLP traffic via `telemetrygen`,
confirming that all 3 enforcement modes function perfectly.

#### Documentation
- Substantially updated the `README.md` to officially document the
`enforcement_mode` options.
- Added architectural documentation detailing how inline spatial
reaggregation behaves for different metric types.
- Generated the official `feat_cardinality-guardian-pr2.yaml` changelog
entry.

fix(receiver/httpcheck): update metrics to use nanosecond precision. (#47718)

Fixes #47257

Previously, getDurations() used integer division (ns /
int64(time.Millisecond))
which truncated any phase duration under 1ms to 0. On fast local/Docker
networks,
all five phase timings (DNS, TCP connect, TLS handshake, request write,
response
read) are typically sub-millisecond, causing the metrics to always
report 0.

Fix by changing the five affected timing metrics to value_type: double
in
metadata.yaml and using float64 division in getDurations(), so e.g. a
500µs
DNS lookup is correctly reported as 0.5ms instead of 0ms.

##### 🚀 New components 🚀

- `extension/mcp`: Add new MCP server extension component.
([#​48072](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48072))

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `all`: Support building with AIX
([#​47010](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47010))

- `cmd/opampsupervisor`: Add support for declarative
`telemetry.resource` configuration while preserving legacy inline
resource attributes
([#​45116](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/45116))
`cmd/opampsupervisor` now accepts typed telemetry resource
configuration,
  including declarative resource attributes and detectors, and validates
  unsupported mixed or deprecated forms.
  Example:
  telemetry:
  resource:
  attributes:
  \- name: service.name
  value: opamp-supervisor

- `exporter/datadog`: Add Kubernetes host alias provider to datadog
exporter.
([#​47199](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47199))
In Kubernetes environments, the Datadog exporter now automatically adds
`nodeName-clusterName` as a
host alias in the host metadata payload. Both the node name and cluster
name must be discoverable for the alias to
be added; the cluster name is resolved from cloud provider metadata
(Azure, EC2, or GCP).

- `exporter/elasticsearch`: Add ability to set filter\_path in
Elasticsearch exporter via the bulk\_response\_filter\_path option.
([#​47204](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47204))

- `exporter/file`: Allow usage of append mode with zstd compression
([#​44382](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/44382))

- `exporter/kafka`: Allow record\_headers to accept multiple headers
with the same key.
([#​48092](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48092))

- `exporter/loadbalancing`: Add stable attribute routing key encoding
for traces and metrics in the loadbalancing exporter
([#​46094](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46094),
[#​46095](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46095))
Routing keys now encode attributes as `name=value|` segments, including
explicit markers for missing attributes.
Non-string attribute values are deterministically stringified and used
consistently across traces and metrics.

- `exporter/opensearch`: specify an ingest pipeline to be used before
writing documents
([#​47227](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47227))
The `pipeline` option allows to specify an existing ingest pipeline that
should process incoming documents.
  If the ingest pipeline does not exist, ingestion will fail.

- `extension/aws_logs_encoding`: Populate ECS fields from VPC Flow Logs
as log record attributes
([#​38861](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/38861))
Previously, VPC flow log fields prefixed with `ecs-` were skipped with a
warning.
They are now mapped to `aws.ecs.*` attributes on the emitted log record.

- `extension/bearertokenauth`: Update token file parsing to ignore
everything after the first whitespace, allowing for inline comments.
([#​46100](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46100))

- `extension/cgroup_runtime`: Expose refresh\_interval for GOMEMLIMIT to
support dynamic memory limits.
([#​46768](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46768))

- `extension/docker_observer`: Add `include_all_containers` option to
emit a port-less endpoint for every running container, including those
with no exposed ports.
([#​48252](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48252))
  When enabled, the observer emits a `container` endpoint with no port
information for every running container, alongside any per-port
endpoints.
This allows `receiver_creator` rules of `type == "container"` to attach
  receivers to every container regardless of whether it exposes ports.
  Defaults to `false` for backwards compatibility.

- `extension/kafkatopics_observer`: Switch to the franz-go client.
([#​48169](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48169))
This is another step towards consolidating on franz-go for all Kafka
components.
We have already switched the receiver and exporter, and they are working
well.

- `extension/mcp`: Register available tools with MCP server.
([#​48103](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48103))

- `extension/pebble_tail_storage`: Add initial implementation of the
Pebble tail storage extension.
([#​47916](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47916))

- `pkg/faro`: Emit `k6_testRunId` in the log body when
`meta.k6.testRunId` is present in the Faro payload.
([#​47935](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47935))
  Surfaces the k6 test run identifier that the Faro Web SDK already
  forwards from `window.k6.testRunId`, alongside the existing
  `k6_isK6Browser` key. The reverse (logs -> Faro) translator extracts
  it back into `Meta.K6.TestRunID` for round-trip parity.

- `pkg/pdatatest`: Introduce pmetrictest.ValidateMetrics to strictly
validate duplicate datapoint identities.
([#​48106](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48106))

- `processor/attributes`: Added support for default values in the
attributes processor.
([#​45352](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/45352))
This enhancement allows users to specify default values for attributes
in the attributes processor.
If the primary value source (e.g., environment variable, attribute, or
context value) is not available,
the default value will be used. This ensures that the pipeline doesn't
fail due to missing configuration.

- `processor/drain`: Add drain processor to k8s distribution.
([#​47235](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47235))

- `processor/k8s_attributes`: Improve deployment name extraction
heuristic when deployment\_name\_from\_replicaset is enabled
([#​44831](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/44831))
When `deployment_name_from_replicaset` is true and the ReplicaSet
informer is not used for deployment names only,
the processor derives `k8s.deployment.name` using the pod-template-hash
label and ReplicaSet naming rules.
When a ReplicaSet informer is running (for example for
`k8s.deployment.uid`), API-backed metadata takes precedence,
  independent of the `deployment_name_from_replicaset` setting.

- `processor/k8s_attributes`: Add `watch_sync_period` config option to
configure informer cache resync period.
([#​48111](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48111))
The `watch_sync_period` config option defaults to `5m` to match the
previously hardcoded behavior.

- `processor/k8s_attributes`: Use PartialObjectMetadata for non-Pod
informers
([#​47389](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47389))
Switch Namespace, Node, Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, and Job
informers
from full typed objects to PartialObjectMetadata via the metadata
client.
These resources only need labels, annotations, UID, name, and owner
references—all available
in object metadata—so fetching full spec/status is unnecessary overhead.

  Pods continue using full objects since they require spec/status
  fields (pod IP, node name, containers, host network).

- `processor/resource`: Added support for default values in the resource
processor.
([#​45352](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/45352))
This enhancement allows users to specify default values for attributes
in the resource processor.
If the primary value source (e.g., environment variable, attribute, or
context value) is not available,
the default value will be used. This ensures that the pipeline doesn't
fail due to missing configuration.

- `processor/schema`: Add internal metrics for schema translation skip
rate and cache hit/miss
([#​47638](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47638))
  Five new metrics are emitted via the collector's internal telemetry:

  - otelcol\_processor\_schema\_logs.skipped
  - otelcol\_processor\_schema\_metrics.skipped
  - otelcol\_processor\_schema\_traces.skipped
  - otelcol\_processor\_schema\_cache.hits
  - otelcol\_processor\_schema\_cache.misses

The skip counters increment when a scope has no schema URL at either the
scope
or resource level, making silent pass-throughs observable. The cache
counters
track effectiveness of the in-memory schema cache in CacheableProvider.

- `receiver/awsfirehose`: awsfirehose receiver now attempts gzip
decompression for Firehose records before decoding.
([#​46463](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46463))

- `receiver/azure_event_hub`: Expose the Prefetch option for Azure Event
Hub receiver
([#​48038](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48038))

- `receiver/couchdb`: Enables dynamic metric reaggregation in the
CouchDB receiver. This does not break existing configuration files.
([#​46351](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46351))

- `receiver/googlecloudmonitoring`: Allow overriding default endpoint
for googlecloudmonitoringreceiver
([#​47984](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47984))
Adds an endpoint property which overrides the default
monitoring.googleapis.com:443 endpoint.
This is needed when targeting non-standard universe domains (e.g. S3NS:
<https://docs.cloud.google.com/sovereign-controls-by-partners/docs/data-boundaries/france-data-boundary-s3ns>)

- `receiver/k8s_cluster`: Enable the re-aggregation feature for the
k8s\_cluster receiver
([#​46361](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46361))

- `receiver/k8s_events`: Simplified RBAC example in README to only
include required `events` resource permission.
([#​48192](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48192))
A namespace-scoped Role can also be used when the receiver is configured
with specific namespaces.

- `receiver/kafka`: Add support for custom consumer-group
partition-assignment strategies via extensions that implement
`kgo.GroupBalancer`. Set `group_rebalance_strategy` to the component ID
of a registered extension to use a custom balancer.
([#​48096](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48096))
The four built-in strategies (`range`, `roundrobin`, `sticky`,
`cooperative-sticky`) continue to work unchanged.
Any other value for `group_rebalance_strategy` is now resolved as an
extension component ID at runtime.

- `receiver/kafka`: Cache OTel metric attribute sets in broker hook
callbacks to reduce per-read allocations
([#​47395](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47395))
`OnBrokerRead` previously rebuilt attribute sets on every call. The
computed
`MeasurementOption` is now cached per (nodeID, outcome) key and evicted
on
  broker disconnect. Growth is bounded by 2 × number-of-brokers.

- `receiver/kubelet_stats`: Add optional system container metrics
(cpu.time, cpu.usage, memory.working\_set) to kubeletstats receiver.
([#​3531](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/3531))

- `receiver/memcached`: Enables dynamic metric reaggregation in the
Memcached receiver. This does not break existing configuration files.
([#​46364](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46364))

- `receiver/mysql`: Added 'mysql.query\_plan' to query sample records
collected
([#​47413](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47413))

- `receiver/mysql`: Fix the query hash generation for MySQL queries when
the query is not explainable.
([#​48059](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48059))

- `receiver/nsxt`: Enables dynamic metric reaggregation in the NSX-T
receiver. This does not break existing configuration files.
([#​46369](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46369))

- `receiver/prometheus_remote_write`: Add debug logging when dropping
histograms with invalid schema values
([#​48027](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48027))

- `receiver/sqlserver`: Adds idle blocking sessions to
`db.server.query_sample` by appending sleeping blocker rows (with
`sqlserver.command=IDLE_BLOCKER`) when blocker session IDs are missing
from active requests.
([#​47120](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47120))
Idle blocker enrichment is best-effort: a targeted secondary
idle-session query runs only for missing blocker session IDs, and
failures are logged as warnings without failing the scrape.

##### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `connector/service_graph`: Fix PR 47971 not add
WithDeprecatedTypeAlias option in NewFactory()
([#​47971](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47971))

- `exporter/elasticsearch`: Return permanent errors for non-retryable
HTTP responses to prevent unnecessary upstream retries.
([#​47870](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47870))

- `exporter/kafka`: Fix collector hanging indefinitely on shutdown when
the Kafka broker is unreachable
([#​48140](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48140))
Re-enables the exporterhelper timeout sender (previously disabled with a
zero timeout) so that each send attempt is bounded by the configured
timeout (default 5s). The per-attempt context is now passed through to
ProduceSync, allowing in-flight sends to unblock when the broker is
unreachable. FranzSyncProducer.Close also cancels the kgo client context
before calling client.Close, ensuring shutdown completes promptly.

- `extension/health_check`: Fix deadlock when the collector run context
is cancelled while the healthcheck extension is present.
([#​47591](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47591))

- `extension/healthcheckv2`: Fix deadlock when the collector run context
is cancelled while the healthcheck extension is present.
([#​47591](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47591))

- `extension/opamp`: Decorrelate `service.instance.id` and OpAMP
`instance_uid`
([#​46495](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46495))
  Previously:

- the `service.instance.id` reported in the AgentDescription was based
on the OpAMP instance UID
- the instance UID was typically set based on the `service.instance.id`
from the Collector resource attributes
- it could be overriden using the `instance_uid` configuration of the
OpAMP extension

This meant that the reported `service.instance.id` did not always match
the Collector resource attributes,
which is a problem for correlation, and that server implementations got
used to the typical case of
`service.instance.id` and `instance_uid` matching, despite there being
no guarantee of this.

  Now:

- the reported value of `service.instance.id` always matches the
Collector resource attributes
- the instance UID is either taken from the `instance_uid` configuration
or generated randomly.

This means that the two values can never be expected to match, unless
both configurations are explicitly set to the same value.
That is what the OpAMP supervisor does, which means its behavior is
unaffected.

- `extension/sumologic`: Fix variable shadowing and formatting issues in
tests.
([#​46602](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46602))

- `processor/k8s_attributes`: Fix a data race when reading the
`kube-system` namespace from the client cache to populate the
`k8s.cluster.uid` attribute.
([#​47910](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47910))
The `ClusterUID` rule in `extractPodAttributes` accessed the shared
`Namespaces`
map without acquiring the client's read lock, which could race with
writes from
the namespace informer. The access now goes through the locked
`GetNamespace`
  helper.

- `processor/k8s_attributes`: Fix container.image.tags config check
([#​47113](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47113))

- `processor/tail_sampling`: Fix sampling inconsistencies when using
`span-ingest` sampling strategy
([#​47476](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47476))
1. Drop policies were not working if the initial batch did not contain a
span matching the drop policy.
2. If max\_spans or upper\_threshold\_ms were respectively set on
span\_count or latency policies they may not have been respected.

- `receiver/awsxray`: support for fileystem sql urls
([#​47361](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47361))
  Support for parsing sql urls without a hostname.

- `receiver/datadog`: Fix infinite memory growth in metrics translator
by pruning stale streams that have not received data within the
configured series\_idle\_timeout.
([#​45523](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/45523))
Previously, high cardinality tags would cause the receiver to retain
state indefinitely, leading to OOM.

- `receiver/faro`: Emit standard receiver telemetry
([#​48070](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48070))
The receiver constructed an `ObsReport` but never invoked it, so
standard
  metrics like `otelcol_receiver_accepted_log_records`,
`otelcol_receiver_refused_log_records`,
`otelcol_receiver_accepted_spans`,
and `otelcol_receiver_refused_spans` were not emitted. The consume calls
  are now wrapped with `StartLogsOp`/`EndLogsOp` and
  `StartTracesOp`/`EndTracesOp` so the standard receiver metrics are
  reported.

- `receiver/host_metrics`: Fix duplicate rootPath prefix in filesystem
mountpoint translation
([#​47083](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47083))
  When gopsutil falls back to reading /proc/self/mountinfo, the reported
  mountpoints already contain the rootPath prefix. This caused
translateMountpoint to add it a second time, resulting in incorrect
paths
  like /hostfs/hostfs/data.

- `receiver/mysql`: Strip leading SQL comments before EXPLAIN check so
queries prefixed with block or line comments are correctly identified as
explainable.
([#​46587](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46587))
