fix(isolationforestprocessor): trees never split + contamination_rate ignored (#47115)

## Problem

The isolation forest processor assigned identical anomaly scores (~0.69)
to all spans regardless of duration. A 14,792ms slow request and a 60ms
normal request were indistinguishable. Nothing was ever flagged as an
anomaly.

Observed before this fix (last 30 spans, mixed normal/slow traffic):

  DurMs    Score    Anomaly
     60   0.6947      False
     88   0.6956      False
    109   0.6837      False
   5660   0.6881      False   <- 5s span, should be anomaly
   7063   0.6888      False   <- 7s span, should be anomaly
  14792   0.6964      False   <- 15s span, should be anomaly

  Score spread across 30 spans: 0.024
  Slow spans flagged: 0/3

## problem 1: trees never split (unreachable split condition)

In updateNodePath, the isLeaf guard short-circuited before the split
check:

  func (oif *onlineIsolationForest) updateNodePath(...) {
      node.sampleCount++

      // fired for ALL leaf nodes — every node starts with isLeaf: true
      if node.isLeaf || depth >= maxDepth {
          return  // always returned here
      }

      // UNREACHABLE: node.isLeaf was already true above
if node.left == nil && node.right == nil && node.sampleCount > 10 {
          oif.splitNode(node, sample, depth, maxDepth)
      }
  }

Every node is initialised with isLeaf: true. The guard returned
immediately on every call, so splitNode was never reached. Trees stayed
as a single root leaf node regardless of how many samples were
processed.

As a result, calculatePathLength always traversed to the same unsplit
root and returned a constant value for every sample:

  depth(0) + estimateRemainingPath(N) = constant

Since avgPathLength and expectedPathLength converged to the same value,
the scoring formula 2^(-avgPathLength / c(n)) produced ~0.69 for every
span, regardless of actual feature values (duration, etc.).

Fix: move the split check before the isLeaf early-return so nodes grow
once they accumulate more than 10 samples.

## problem 2: contamination_rate config was ignored

The adaptive threshold percentile was hardcoded to 0.9, and
ContaminationRate was never passed into the forest constructor from
processor.go:

  // hardcoded — config value was silently ignored
  thresholdIndex := int(0.9 * float64(len(sortedScores)))

With contamination_rate: 0.05 the threshold should sit at the 95th
percentile (flag top 5%), not the 90th.

Fix: add contaminationRate field to onlineIsolationForest, pass
config.ContaminationRate (and modelConfig.ContaminationRate for
multi-model mode) at all four constructor call sites in processor.go,
and derive the percentile as 1.0 - contaminationRate.

## Result after fix

  DurMs    Score    Anomaly
     36   0.7321      False
     57   0.7426      False
    115   0.7191      False
  12137   0.8854       True   <- correctly flagged
  13629   0.8976       True   <- correctly flagged
  14520   0.8977       True   <- correctly flagged

  Normal spans (36-158ms):  score 0.719-0.746  ->  False
  Slow spans  (12-14s):     score 0.885-0.898  ->  True

Score spread increased from 0.024 to ~0.17. All slow spans correctly
flagged; no normal spans incorrectly flagged. Verified end-to-end via
Tempo API and TraceQL: { span.anomaly_is_anomaly = true }

### Description

Fixes an issue where `obfuscateXMLPlan` discarded the entire SQL Server

[receiver/postgresql] Fix EXPLAIN parameter count for repeated/literal placeholders (#50067)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
`explainQuery` determines how many nulls to bind for `EXPLAIN EXECUTE`
by regex-matching `$N` against the raw query text and counting matches.
This overcounts whenever a placeholder repeats (`WHERE a = $1 OR b = $1`
has one real parameter, the regex finds two) or when `$N`-looking text
appears inside a string literal (`WHERE msg = '$123'` has
zero real parameters, the regex finds one). Both cases make `EXECUTE`
fail with "wrong number of parameters", so `EXPLAIN` never runs for
those queries.

This change:
- Replaces the regex-based count in `explainQuery` with a lookup against
`pg_prepared_statements.parameter_types`, read after `PREPARE` succeeds
- Adds `ConnWrapper` to `internal/sqlquery` so `PREPARE`, the
parameter-count lookup, `EXPLAIN EXECUTE`, and `DEALLOCATE` all run on
one dedicated connection instead of the pool, since `PREPARE` is
session-scoped and the count lookup needs a second round trip
- Adds the empty-result guard to `explainQuery` that other `EXPLAIN`
paths in the file already had

The dedicated connection is required because reading
`pg_prepared_statements` back is a separate call from `PREPARE`, and
without pinning both to the same connection, the pool could hand a later
step a different connection than the one that ran `PREPARE`.

[exporter/awscloudwatchlogs][internal/aws/cwlogs] configurable 1 MiB per-event cap + fix batch threshold conflation (#48559)

## Description

This PR does two things:

1. **Enhancement** — adds a `max_event_payload_bytes` config field on
the `awscloudwatchlogs` exporter (and an equivalent
`cwlogs.WithMaxEventPayloadBytes` pusher option) so users can opt in to
the **1 MiB** CloudWatch Logs per-event limit that the service raised to
on
[2025-04-02](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/04/amazon-cloudwatch-logs-increases-log-event-size-1-mb/).
The default stays at 256 KiB for backwards compatibility.

2. **Bug fix** — fixes a pre-existing batching inefficiency in
`internal/aws/cwlogs`. Since the original 2022 code,
`eventBatch.exceedsLimit` has compared cumulative batch bytes against
`maxEventPayloadBytes` (the **per-event** truncation cap, 256 KiB)
rather than `maxRequestPayloadBytes` (the **per-request** PutLogEvents
API limit, 1 MiB). Those are two distinct service limits — 256 KiB has
always been the per-event cap and 1 MiB has always been the per-request
cap. Using the former where the latter belonged silently capped batches
at ~25% of the available PutLogEvents request capacity for every user of
this exporter.

Both changes are required for the new config to behave as advertised,
but the bug fix stands on its own: any user with average event size
above ~25 KiB benefits from ~3-4x fewer PutLogEvents calls after this
PR, regardless of whether they set the new config field.

## Why this matters

**For the enhancement:** in production environments routing OTLP logs
through this exporter (e.g. ECS / Fargate tasks running ADOT, large .NET
/ Java request-logging middleware that captures request and response
bodies), the 256 KiB cap silently truncated events with a
`[Truncated...]` suffix. A real-world example fleet of ~350 OTel log
groups showed **49,205 truncated events in 30 days** concentrated on 22
services — every one of them now well under the 1 MiB service limit if
the cap could be lifted.

**For the bug fix:** every user of this exporter has been making roughly
3-4x more PutLogEvents calls than necessary for medium-and-larger
events, since at least 2022. That has real cost — request signing
overhead, network roundtrips, and exporter-side CPU — even though
CloudWatch Logs doesn't charge per call directly.

The bug fix is also load-bearing for the enhancement: without it, an
opted-in user with 600 KiB events would ship one event per PutLogEvents
call (because the second event would cross the 256 KiB threshold)
instead of packing toward the 1 MiB ceiling. The enhancement only
delivers its full value with the fix in place.

## Implementation notes

- **Per-event cap (enhancement):**
- New `Config.MaxEventPayloadBytes int` on the exporter. Validated to
lie in `[perEventHeaderBytes + len(truncatedSuffix) + 1, 1 MiB]`. A
value of `0` (or omitted) means "use the package default" — existing
configs are unaffected.
- New `cwlogs.WithMaxEventPayloadBytes(n int)` functional option
accepted by `NewPusher` and `NewMultiStreamPusherFactory`. Variadic
signature, so existing direct callers (notably `awsemfexporter`) keep
compiling unchanged.
- `Event.Validate` delegates to a new cap-aware sibling
`validateWithCap`. A cap value `<= 0` falls back to the package default,
preserving compatibility with existing test code that flips the package
var.
- `MaxAllowedEventPayloadBytes` (`= maxRequestPayloadBytes`, 1 MiB) and
`MinAllowedEventPayloadBytes` are exported for config validation.

- **Batch threshold (bug fix):**
- `eventBatch.exceedsLimit` now compares against
`maxRequestPayloadBytes` (1 MiB) instead of `maxEventPayloadBytes` (256
KiB).
- The AWS PutLogEvents API documents its batch-size calculation as "sum
of all event messages in UTF-8, plus 26 bytes for each log event" —
which is exactly what `byteTotal` already sums (`eventPayloadBytes()`
includes the 26-byte `perEventHeaderBytes`). The service does not count
HTTP/2 framing or the JSON request wrapper toward the 1 MiB limit, so no
envelope-overhead margin is needed.

## Test coverage

- `TestMaxEventPayloadBytesValidate` (exporter `config_test.go`): zero
allowed, 256 KiB allowed, 1 MiB allowed, sub-minimum rejected, above-1
MiB rejected.
- `TestPusher_perPusherMaxEventPayloadBytes` (cwlogs `pusher_test.go`):
per-pusher cap raising the ceiling, zero/omitted falling back to the
package default, default `Validate` matching
`validateWithCap(maxEventPayloadBytes)`, `effectiveMaxEventPayloadBytes`
resolution, **and a new subtest asserting two 400 KiB events with a 1
MiB cap share a single batch** (the regression for the per-event vs
batch cap conflation).
- `TestAddLogEventWithValidation` updated: its previous rollover
assertion was coupled to the buggy 256 KiB threshold. It now asserts the
invariant ("batch rolls once cumulative bytes cross the per-request
ceiling") rather than the specific number.

### End-to-end verification against live CloudWatch

Built a collector with this branch (via `ocb`), pointed
`awscloudwatchlogs` at a real CloudWatch log group in a sandbox account
with `max_event_payload_bytes: 1048576`, and sent five OTLP log records
via a hand-rolled gRPC client:

- 1× 200 KiB control
- 1× 600 KiB (must pass through with the new cap)
- 2× 400 KiB in a single OTLP `Export` call (batching test)
- 1× 1.1 MiB (must truncate to 1 MiB with `[Truncated...]` suffix)

**Without the bug fix** (PR as originally posted): the five events
shipped in **5 separate PutLogEvents calls** — each event got its own
batch, because the second 400 KiB event tripped the 256 KiB threshold.

**With the bug fix:** the same five events shipped in **3 PutLogEvents
calls**:

| Call | Events in batch | Total bytes | Notes |
|------|-----------------|-------------|-------|
| 1 | 2 | ~800 KiB | 200 KiB control + 600 KiB packed together |
| 2 | 2 | ~800 KiB | both 400 KiB events packed together |
| 3 | 1 | ~1 MiB | truncated 1.1 MiB event (already at batch ceiling) |

CloudWatch console confirmed all five events landed at the expected
sizes; the 1.1 MiB event ended with `[Truncated...]`; the 600 KiB event
was preserved in full.

A separate boundary test sent four 256 KiB events (sum-by-spec exactly 1
MiB) and confirmed both that the exporter does not over-fill the batch
and that the service accepts batches at the documented limit.

## Backwards compatibility

- Defaults unchanged for the per-event cap (256 KiB).
- Batch threshold fix changes behavior for all callers, but only in one
direction (batches can grow larger, up to the actual service limit). No
caller could have been depending on the prior 256 KiB batch ceiling
without also depending on the 256 KiB per-event cap, which is unchanged.
- Config: new optional field; absent or zero gives identical behavior.
- API: `NewPusher` and `NewMultiStreamPusherFactory` gain variadic
`PusherOption` parameters. Existing callers (`awsemfexporter` and any
external direct callers) keep compiling.

## Out of scope

- This PR does not change the package default per-event cap. A separate
discussion about whether the default should be bumped to 1 MiB now that
the service supports it can happen after this PR lands.
- This PR does not change how the EMF exporter sizes events.

## Linked motivation

- [AWS announcement,
2025-04-02](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/04/amazon-cloudwatch-logs-increases-log-event-size-1-mb/)
— service-side limit raised to 1 MiB.
- Quotas page:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/cloudwatch_limits_cwl.html
(search "Event size").

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

The `draft_if_multiple_prs` job seems never successfully drafted a PR.
It fails at `gh pr ready --undo`, which issues the GraphQL mutation
`convertPullRequestToDraft`.

That mutation returns `Resource not accessible by integration` because
the otelbot token is minted with only `permission-pull-requests: write`.
The PR draft-state mutations additionally require `contents: write`.

Because the step runs under `set -euo pipefail`, the failed call aborts
it before the explanatory comment is posted, so the PR is neither
converted to draft nor commented on.

existed for the Alibaba ECS, OpenStack Nova, and Tencent CVM detectors,

[processor/k8s_attributes] Fix memory leak and incorrect deletion for custom association identifiers (#49760)

#### Changes

**Memory leak for custom association identifiers**
When a pod update removes a label/annotation used as an association
source, the stale cache entry was never evicted, the fix generalises the
existing `container.id` stale cleanup to cover all identifier types

**Active - stale - active incorrect deletion**
When an identifier disappears and reappears for the same pod before the
grace period expires, the pending delete was never cancelled, causing
the active association to be incorrectly removed;`addOrUpdatePod` now
calls `cancelDeleteRequests` to remove matching pending deletes when an
identifier is re-activated

###
[`v0.158.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v01580)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/compare/v0.157.0...v0.158.0)

##### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `all`: Update Cosign usage to work with v3
([#​1570](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1570))
The Cosign v3 upgrade introduced a change in signing workflow. Previous
two files
were required to map the outputs (certificate and signature), now only
one file is required.
  The new file is a bundle that contains both outputs in JSON format.
This change has been done following the guidance from
<https://goreleaser.com/blog/cosign-v3/>.
With this change, anyone who wants to verify the signature of the
artifacts produced by the
release will need to use Cosign V3 and point to the new bundle file or
download the bundle and
  unpack it to get the certificate and signature files.

- `all`: Use split checksum for all binaries and distros
([#​1582](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1582))
The previous attempt at splitting the checksum file for AIX releases was
not successful.
The problem lies on the fac that `.runtime.GOOS` will always be the
runtime of the compiled
goreleaser binary ("linux" in this case). The only way to split the
checksum file per target
is what's implement here, but it ends up giving one checksum file per
produced artifact.

##### 🚀 New components 🚀

- `icmpcheckreceiver`: Add icmpcheckreceiver to the contrib distribution
([#​1577](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1577))

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `all`: Add new binaries for aix/ppc64
([#​1424](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1424))

##### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `all`: Skip Docker build and publish in AIX release job.
([#​1580](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1580))
The release for Contrib on AIX runs in its own job, where it doesn't
build
Docker images. The `continue --merge` phase of goreleaser runs all
publishers
by default, including the Docker manifests one. This will fail for AIX
as
  the images aren't built.

</details>

#### Description

An easy win on `Document.sort`:

<details>
<summary>Benchmark used.</summary>

```go
// BenchmarkDocumentSort measures the sorting hotspot used by Document.Serialize.
// Each document is cloned with the timer stopped because sorting mutates it.
func BenchmarkDocumentSort(b *testing.B) {
	cases := []struct {
		name       string
		fieldCount int
	}{
		{
			name:       "fields_20",
			fieldCount: 20,
		},
		{
			name:       "fields_40",
			fieldCount: 40,
		},
		{
			name:       "fields_80",
			fieldCount: 80,
		},
	}

	for _, tc := range cases {
		b.Run(tc.name, func(b *testing.B) {
			base := newSortBenchmarkDocument(tc.fieldCount)
			b.ReportAllocs()

			for b.Loop() {
				b.StopTimer()
				doc := base.Clone()
				b.StartTimer()
				doc.sort()
			}
		})
	}
}

func newSortBenchmarkDocument(fieldCount int) Document {
	var doc Document
	for i := range fieldCount {
		// Use a deterministic non-sorted insertion order, matching documents
		// assembled from resource and data point attributes.
		fieldID := (i * 37) % fieldCount
		doc.AddString(fmt.Sprintf("metric.%03d", fieldID), "value")
	}
	return doc
}
```

###
[`v9.22.0`](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/releases/tag/v9.22.0):
9.22.0

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/compare/v9.21.0...v9.22.0)

This is a minor release introducing two flagship (experimental) features
— **client-side caching** and **automatic pipelining** — alongside
support for Redis 8.10, new commands, and a large batch of stability and
parser-robustness fixes. It consolidates everything shipped in
9.22.0-beta.1, so the notes below cover the full 9.21.0 → 9.22.0
upgrade.

⚠️ Two changes to be aware of when upgrading from 9.21.0:

- **Default configuration values changed**
([#​3918](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3918)):
read/write timeouts, retry backoff, cluster state reload interval, and
TCP keep-alive defaults are now aligned with the cross-SDK configuration
proposal (see the highlight below). Explicitly configured values are
unaffected.
- **`WaitAOF` return type corrected**
([#​3888](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3888)):
`WaitAOF` now returns `*IntSliceCmd`, matching the two-integer reply of
`WAITAOF` (previously `*IntCmd`, which failed to parse the reply at
runtime). Code referencing the old return type needs a one-line update.

#### 🚀 Highlights

##### Client-Side Caching (Experimental)

The standalone `Client` gains server-assisted client-side caching built
on RESP3 `CLIENT TRACKING`. Enable it by setting `ClientSideCacheConfig`
in `Options` (or supply your own cache via `ClientSideCache` — e.g. to
share one cache across clients). Cacheable read results are served from
a local in-process cache and invalidated automatically when the server
reports a change, cutting round trips for read-heavy workloads.

The invalidation architecture is selected by `ClientSideCacheStrategy`;
the default (and currently only) strategy is
`CSCStrategySharedTracking`: one shared cache, every pool connection
runs plain `CLIENT TRACKING ON`, and a background drainer applies
buffered invalidations — portable (no BCAST) and consistent with the
other Redis client libraries. Requirements and guardrails: RESP3
(`Protocol: 3`), standalone client, DB 0 only; commands that would
change the connection identity (`SELECT`, `AUTH`, ...) are rejected
while caching is enabled, and CSC is disabled when a credentials
provider is set (fixed `Username`/`Password` work and are namespaced).
See the README's [client-side caching
section](README.md#client-side-caching) and the runnable
[example](example/client-side-caching).

**Experimental:** the API may change in a minor release.

([#​3941](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3941))
by [@​ofekshenawa](https://redirect.github.com/ofekshenawa)

##### Automatic Pipelining (Experimental)

`AutoPipeliner` is a background batcher that coalesces commands from
many concurrent goroutines into Redis pipelines, multiplying throughput
without any manual pipeline management. It comes in two faces, available
on `Client` and `ClusterClient` (and configurable via
`Options.AutoPipelineOptions` / `UniversalOptions.AutoPipelineOptions`):

- **`AutoPipeline()`** — the blocking face: a drop-in `Cmdable` where
each call blocks until executed, exactly like a plain client, while
concurrent callers' commands batch together under the hood (measured
locally over loopback: \~1M+ SET/sec vs \~100k unpipelined; indicative,
not a guarantee). Per-goroutine command order is preserved.
- **`AsyncAutoPipeline()`** — the deferred face: command calls return
immediately and every typed result accessor (`Val`/`Result`/`Err`/...)
blocks until the command has executed. Submit a window of commands, then
read the results, to keep pipelines deep (\~2–3M SET/sec locally;
indicative).

`AutoPipelineOptions` controls batching: `MaxBatchSize` (soft target,
default 200; the blocking face's preset uses 300), `MaxBatchBytes`
(approximate payload cap so huge values flush as several bounded
writes), `MaxFlushDelay` with optional `AdaptiveDelay` (delay scales
down as the queue fills), and `MaxConcurrentBatches` (default 1 = a
single ordered batch stream; raising it requires `Unordered: true`, so
ordering is never lost by accident — `Validate()` rejects the
combination otherwise). A usage tour and throughput comparison live in
[`example/autopipeline`](example/autopipeline).

**Experimental:** the API may change in a future release — pin your
go-redis version if you adopt it.

([#​3942](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3942))
by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov), with help
from [@​cxljs](https://redirect.github.com/cxljs)

##### Redis 8.10 Support

This release adds support for **Redis 8.10**. The README's
supported-versions list now includes Redis 8.10, and CI runs the full
suite against the `redislabs/client-libs-test:8.10.0` image by default
([#​3920](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3920),
[#​3940](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3940)).

Coverage for the new commands and options that ship with Redis 8.10:

- **`HIMPORT`**
([#​3919](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3919)) —
bulk hash import via server-side fieldsets, exposed as `HImportPrepare`,
`HImportSet`, `HImportDiscard`, and `HImportDiscardAll`. Fieldsets are
session state scoped to a single physical connection, which does not mix
well with connection pooling — so the client keeps a versioned fieldset
registry and lazily replays the `PREPARE` on whichever pooled connection
executes a `SET` that needs it, at most once per connection, with no
extra round trip (the `PREPARE` is injected into the same write as the
`SET`).
- **`LMOVEM` / `BLMOVEM`**
([#​3913](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3913)) —
move multiple elements between lists in one call.
- **`SUNIONCARD` / `SDIFFCARD`**
([#​3897](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3897)) —
cardinality of set union/difference without materializing the result.
- **`XREAD` / `XREADGROUP` `MAXCOUNT` and `MAXSIZE`**
([#​3898](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3898)) —
bound how much data a stream read returns.
- **`TS.READ`**
([#​3896](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3896)),
**`TS.QUERYLABELS`**
([#​3926](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3926)),
**`TS.NRANGE` / `TS.NREVRANGE`**
([#​3870](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3870))
with multiple aggregators per key
([#​3937](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3937)),
and **`EXCLUDEEMPTY`** on `TS.MRANGE` / `TS.MREVRANGE`
([#​3912](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3912)) —
new time-series query surface.
- **`FT.ALIASLIST`**
([#​3925](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3925)),
**`COLLECT` reducer for `FT.AGGREGATE`**
([#​3886](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3886)),

##### Cross-SDK Aligned Defaults

Default configuration values now follow the cross-SDK configuration
proposal shared by all Redis client libraries
([#​3918](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3918)):

| Setting | Old default | New default |
| ------------------------------ | ----------- |
--------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ReadTimeout` / `WriteTimeout` | 3s | 5s |
| Retry backoff (min/max) | 8ms / 512ms | 10ms / 1s |
| Cluster state reload interval | 10s | 60s |
| TCP keep-alive | 5min period | 30s idle / 5s interval / 3 probes
(`net.KeepAliveConfig`) |

Applications that set these values explicitly are unaffected;
applications relying on the old defaults inherit the new ones.

##### Data-Race and Parser Hardening Sweep

A systematic audit fixed data races across the client — hooks
(`AddHook`,
[#​3868](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3868)),
`Ring.SetAddrs`
([#​3862](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3862)),
cluster node slices
([#​3861](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3861)),
pub/sub reconnect
([#​3906](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3906)),
maintenance notifications
([#​3894](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3894),
[#​3872](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3872)),
pool handoff
([#​3876](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3876)),
and `redisotel`
([#​3881](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3881)) —
and hardened the RESP parsers against malformed or unexpected replies:
over-reads on nil replies
([#​3874](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3874)),
integer overflow when skipping map/attribute bodies
([#​3877](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3877)),
unhashable RESP3 map keys
([#​3873](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3873)),
odd-length flat replies
([#​3900](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3900)),
mismatched declared array lengths
([#​3907](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3907)),
unexpected extra reply frames
([#​3884](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3884)),
and nil elements in numeric/bool slice replies
([#​3922](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3922)).

##### PubSub `Receive` Hang Fix

`PeekPushNotificationName` blocked until 36 bytes were buffered, so a
short subscribe confirmation (channel name of six or fewer characters)
on an otherwise idle connection hung `PubSub.Receive` forever — a
regression introduced in 9.20.1 by
[#​3842](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3842).
The peek now parses whatever is already buffered and only waits for one
more byte when the frame prefix is valid but incomplete. Fixes
[#​3935](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/issues/3935).

([#​3936](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3936))
by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)

##### Correct Cluster Transaction Retries

The cluster transaction pipeline treated a `MULTI`...`EXEC` block as
independently retryable commands, which could scatter a transaction
across nodes or send malformed transactions on retry. Redirects
(`MOVED`/`ASK`/`TRYAGAIN`) and aborts are now handled at the
whole-transaction level, matching Redis transaction semantics: the
transaction is re-routed and retried as a unit, never partially
([#​3909](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3909))
by [@​cxljs](https://redirect.github.com/cxljs).

##### Credential Redaction in Command Tracing

`rediscmd.AppendCmd` — used by `redisotel` and `rediscensus` to render
commands into span attributes — now redacts credential arguments as
`<redacted>`: `AUTH`, `HELLO ... AUTH`, `CONFIG SET` of `requirepass` /
`masterauth` / TLS key passphrases, `ACL SETUSER` password rules, and
`MIGRATE ... AUTH`/`AUTH2`. The client sends `HELLO ... AUTH` on every
handshake and `AUTH` on every streaming-credentials rotation through the
regular hook chain, so tracing hooks previously captured credentials
even when the application never issued an auth command itself
([#​3939](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3939))
by [@​saddamr3e](https://redirect.github.com/saddamr3e).

[receiver/datadog] Preserve RATE metric type during OTLP translation (#50195)

#### Description

Implements the fix described in #50120 by preserving the original
Datadog RATE classification during series translation.

Datapoints translated from RATE series now include
`datadog.metric.as_type = "rate"` in both the V1 and V2 translation
paths. V3 requires no separate translation change because v3 series are
decoded into the v2 representation and passed through
`TranslateSeriesV2`.

_note_: the metric _type_ is fixed while the _magnitude_ still depends
on the alpha `InferIntervalForDeltaMetrics` gate. This is exporter-side,
and by default, the gate is off.

Filed by @rickyari, who diagnosed the root cause and verified it —
thanks! I did the E2E testing, some minor tweaks, and added the
documentation before opening this PR.

The v3 path is covered by a dedicated regression test and was also
verified end-to-end with Datadog Agent 7.81.1.

#### Link to tracking issue

Fixes #50120

#### Testing

Updated the existing V1 and V2 RATE tests to verify that
`datadog.metric.as_type = "rate"` is present on translated datapoints.

Added negative assertions for COUNT and GAUGE metrics to verify that the
attribute is not added to those types.

Added `TestTranslateSeriesV3Rate` to verify that a v3 rate series is
decoded through the v2 translation path with the attribute preserved.

Validation performed:

* `make lint` — PASS
* `make test` — PASS, 294 tests
* targeted `go test -count=1 -race` for `TestTranslateSeriesV1` ,
`TestTranslateSeriesV3Rate` and `TestTranslateSeriesV2` — PASS
* `make chlog-validate` — PASS

##### End-to-end

Built `otelcontribcol` from this branch with the `datadog` receiver
feeding a detailed `debug` exporter and exercised two paths:

* Direct V1 series intake with RATE, COUNT, and GAUGE metrics.
* Datadog Agent 7.81.1 in Docker, pointed at the collector with
`DD_DD_URL`, with a DogStatsD counter submitted through the Agent's v3
series intake path.

With the fix reverted, the RATE and COUNT metrics were both emitted as
non-monotonic delta Sums with no datapoint attribute distinguishing
them.

With the fix applied, the RATE datapoint includes:

```text
datadog.metric.as_type: Str(rate)
```

The same attribute was present on the rate generated through the Agent
7.81.1 / v3 path.

COUNT and GAUGE remained unchanged and did not receive the attribute.

#### Documentation

Added `.chloggen/fix_datadogreceiver-rate-as-type.yaml`.

Updated the receiver README's `Default Attributes` section to document
`datadog.metric.as_type` and when it is set.

[receiver/sqlserver] Obfuscate SQL with go-sqllexer obfuscate_and_normalize (#50127)

#### Description
Switch the sqlserver receiver's SQL obfuscator to the DataDog
`go-sqllexer`
engine by setting `ObfuscationMode: obfuscate_and_normalize`, and bump
`github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pkg/obfuscate` to v0.82.0. This is a
follow-on
tidy-up to #50065 / #50070.
The previous configuration used the legacy tokenizer, which fails hard
on inputs
that carry no obfuscatable content or that it cannot tokenize:
- Comment-only statements (e.g. Blue Prism
`--*INSERT`/`--*SELECT`/`--*UPDATE`
banners captured in `sys.dm_exec_sql_text`) returned `result is empty`,
which
the scraper logged at `error` on every scrape interval and emitted an
empty
  `query.text`.
- Statements containing zero-width / Unicode format characters failed
with
  `unexpected byte ...` and were dropped (the case #50065 addressed).
`obfuscate_and_normalize` handles both gracefully: comment-only input
obfuscates
to an empty string with no error, and malformed/format-character input
is
obfuscated instead of dropped. This is the same engine and mode
DataDog's own
Database Monitoring integrations use for SQL Server, so the obfuscated
output and
resulting query signatures align with DataDog DBM behaviour.
`sanitizeSQL` (Cf-character stripping, added in #50070) is intentionally
kept. It
is no longer required to avoid a hard failure, but it keeps the
obfuscated text
clean and — because the top query and query sample flows can capture
statement
text from different sources (`dm_exec_query_stats` vs `dm_exec_requests`
with a
`dm_exec_input_buffer` fallback) — it ensures a stray zero-width
character does
not cause the same statement to obfuscate to two different strings
across flows.
Note: the obfuscated `query.text` is now normalized (whitespace
collapsed,
comments/aliases removed, literals redacted). In practice this closely
matches
the previous legacy output, but the format change is a one-time change
that may
alter any downstream identifiers derived from the obfuscated query text.
The
v0.82.0 obfuscate upgrade also normalizes qualified identifiers
consistently
(e.g. `schema.table` no longer renders with a spurious space after the
dot),
which contributes to the same one-time change in obfuscated output.
#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #50210

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.

#### Description

The `draft_if_multiple_prs` job fails at `gh pr ready --undo` with
`GraphQL: Resource not accessible by integration
(convertPullRequestToDraft)`
([run](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/actions/runs/31370361182/job/93397724142))
because the otelbot token is narrowed to `permission-pull-requests:
write`, which is not sufficient for that mutation, this is why #48203
didn't help, as it swapped the token but kept the same narrowing.

My follow-up
[PR](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/50141)
added `permission-contents: write`, which the installation doesn't
grant, so token creation now fails with a 422 and the draft step is
skipped entirely, meaning every first-time contributor gets a failure
([run](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/actions/runs/31646490917/job/94281200375)).

This PR removes that and drops the narrowing so the token is minted with
the installation's existing grant, matching how `tidy-dependencies.yml`,
`prepare-release.yml` and `update-otel.yaml` already request it. This
widens the token's permissions but not its reach (still repo-scoped),
and the job has no `actions/checkout`, only a SHA-pinned action, and
passes untrusted values via `env:`, so no PR-controlled code runs with
it. The 422 also confirms the installation has no `Contents: write`, so
it can't push.

`actions/checkout`, untrusted values via `env:`, workflow body from
`main`, and is scoped to one job instead of an org app token. Trade-off:

[processor/dynamic_sampling] drain pending traces on shutdown (#50106)

#### Description

Shutdown currently discards every buffered trace without a decision, so
a rollout, restart, or config reload loses up to `trace_timeout` worth
of spans. This change makes Shutdown drain the buffer instead. Pending
traces are snapshotted in arrival order and each is decided through the

a correct `ot=th` tracestate. `decision_delay` is skipped since nothing
more will arrive, and the samplers are stopped only after the drain so
rule evaluation still works. Drained decisions are visible on the
decision-triggers counter as `trigger="shutdown"`.

Since restarting is how rules changes are applied while live reload
remains future work, this also removes the data loss previously attached
to every rules change.

Shutdown is now also idempotent (a second call is a no-op), since it
does real work worth guarding.

[processor/tailsampling] Add num_shards config for parallel event loops (#48699)

## Summary

- Add optional `num_shards` config parameter (default `1`) that creates
N independent event loops, each with its own trace storage and decision
batcher
- Traces are routed to shards deterministically by trace ID, ensuring
all spans for a given trace are processed by the same shard
- When `num_shards` is `1` (or unset), behavior is identical to the
existing single-loop implementation

### Motivation

The tail sampling processor runs a single goroutine event loop that
serializes trace ingestion and sampling decision evaluation via a
`select` statement. Under high throughput, the `workChan` (trace
ingestion) dominates the `select`, starving the ticker that drives
`samplingPolicyOnTick`. This causes traces to accumulate in memory
without being evaluated or released — manifesting as memory spikes that
don't correlate with CPU usage.

Sharding by trace ID distributes the work across independent goroutines
so that each shard's tick fires reliably relative to its ingestion rate,
keeping memory bounded.

### Design

A `shardedProcessor` wrapper creates N `tailSamplingSpanProcessor`
instances. `ConsumeTraces` groups spans by trace ID and routes each
trace to `shard[traceID % numShards]`. `NumTraces` and
`ExpectedNewTracesPerSec` are divided evenly across shards.
`SetSamplingPolicy` and `SetMaximumTraceSizeBytes` broadcast to all
shards.

## Smoke test

Built `otelcontribcol`, ran with `num_shards: 4`, sent 10 traces via
OTLP HTTP, verified all 10 were sampled and exported after
`decision_wait`, clean shutdown.

- Script: https://pastebin.com/LXtV1Jjg
- Output: https://pastebin.com/gYtCw75n

with correct per-shard `NumTraces`

`TestShardedProcessorZeroShardsFallback` — confirms `NumShards <= 1`
returns original processor
- [x] `TestShardedProcessorStartShutdown` — lifecycle works cleanly
- [x] `TestShardedProcessorDeterministicRouting` — same trace ID always
maps to same shard, distribution covers all shards

[exporter/awscloudwatchlogsexporter] resolve {PodName} placeholder via k8s.pod.name attribute (#49873)

Motivation:
Issue #46202 reports that the `{PodName}` placeholder in
`log_group_name`/`log_stream_name` does not resolve for standard EKS
pipelines. The root cause, identified in the issue thread, is that
`patternKeyToAttributeMap` only mapped `PodName` to the legacy attribute
name `pod`. The `k8sattributesprocessor` sets the semantic-convention

`map[string][]string` so each placeholder can list multiple candidate
resource attribute names, checked in order. `PodName` now checks `pod`
first (preserving existing behavior), then falls back to `k8s.pod.name`.
All other placeholders keep their single existing attribute name, just
wrapped in a one-element slice, so their behavior is unchanged.

exporter/awscloudwatchlogsexporter — all tests pass, including the new
TestReplacePatternValidPodNameFromK8sSemconv (verifies `{PodName}`
resolves from `k8s.pod.name` alone) and
TestReplacePatternPodNamePrefersLegacyPodAttribute (verifies `pod` still
wins over `k8s.pod.name` when both are present, preserving backwards
compatibility).

[receiver/oracledb] Use ObfuscateAndNormalize for stable SQL query signatures (#50230)

The Oracle top-query and query-sample collectors previously obfuscated
SQL with
`ObfuscateOnly`, which replaces literals but preserves the original
formatting.
As a result, semantically identical statements that differed only in
whitespace,
comments, punctuation spacing, or a trailing semicolon produced
different
`db.query.text` values for the same Oracle `sql_id`. Because the
obfuscated text
is used to derive an internal query signature, this caused a single
query to be
split into multiple divergent signatures/rows.
This change switches obfuscation to the go-sqllexer
`ObfuscateAndNormalize`
engine so the obfuscated `db.query.text` is normalized (whitespace
collapsed,
comments stripped, punctuation spaced, trailing semicolon removed),
yielding a
stable canonical form across formatting variants. It also:
- Adds `KeepIdentifierQuotation: true` so a quoted identifier such as
`"a b"`
  does not collide with the unquoted `a b`.
- Keeps `KeepSQLAlias`, `KeepBoolean`, and `KeepNull` behavior.
- Removes the previous two-pass comment-anonymization logic
(`collectCommentsConfig`).
Leading SQL comments are no longer emitted as a leading `?`; comment
tags are
still extracted from the raw SQL and emitted via
`db.query.comment_tags`.
- Upgrades `github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pkg/obfuscate` to v0.82.0
(and `github.com/DataDog/go-sqllexer` to v0.2.4) for consistency with
the
  recently merged SQL Server change (#50127).
Note that the obfuscator does not fold keyword/identifier case, so
statements
differing only in case are not merged; this is unchanged from the
previous
behavior and does not affect a given `sql_id` (whose raw text is fixed).
This is a one-time change to the obfuscated output format and may alter
any
downstream identifiers derived from `db.query.text`.
Note: this removes the leading-`?` comment behavior introduced in
#48510;
the original contributor has been notified.
#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #50231
#### Testing
- Updated `obfuscate_test.go` expectations to the new normalized output.
- Added a format-invariance regression test asserting that
whitespace/comment
  variants of the same statement produce an identical canonical string.
- Added a quoted-identifier collision test (`"a b"` vs `a b`) covering
  `KeepIdentifierQuotation`.
- Rewrote the comment tests (comments are now stripped, no leading `?`)
and

file for
  `TestScraper_ScrapeTopNLogs`.

[chore] [receiver/tcpcheck] Fix flaky `TestScraper_ErrorEnumCounts` test on Windows (#48878)

### Description
This PR solves a flaky test in the `tcpcheckreceiver`

The problem was that the test was configured to duplicate target
endpoints
- On Linux: due to high-resolution timestamps, the concurrent test
checks resulted in unique timestamps. `MetricsBuilder` recorded separate
cumulative data points (e.g. `1`, `2`, `3`) for the same endpoint
attribute. The test parsed these and overrode the local map value, which
ended up reflecting the final recorded value (`2` and `3`)
- On Windows: the system clock resolution is lower. This caused
concurrent scrapes to resolve to the exact same timestamp. When data
points with matching timestamps and attributes are emitted,
`MetricsBuilder` aggregated them using `AggregationStrategySum`. This
resulted in the cumulative values being summed together (e.g., `1 + 2 =
3` for `invalid_endpoint` and `1 + 2 + 3 = 6` for `connection_timeout`),
failing the assertions

I've:
- Updated the endpoints in the test to be unique (`invalid:host1`,
`invalid:host2`, `1.2.3.4:80`, `1.2.3.4:81`, `1.2.3.4:82`) so
`MetricsBuilder` will not aggregate them by timestamp since the
attributes are distinct
- Adjusted the test assertions to aggregate error counts using addition
(`+=`) instead of overwriting (`=`)

`postgresql.total_exec_time`/`postgresql.total_plan_time` the same way
("in delta milliseconds") - but the code emits seconds, not
milliseconds.

Per [OTel semantic
conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/metrics/#:~:text=When%20instruments%20are%20measuring%20durations%2C%20seconds%20(i.e.%20s)%20SHOULD%20be%20used),
durations should use seconds — so the code's behavior is correct as-is.
The actual bug is the documentation.

This change:
- Fixes `metadata.yaml` (and regenerates `documentation.md`) so
`postgresql.total_exec_time/postgresql.total_plan_time` correctly say
"in delta seconds" instead of "in delta milliseconds"
- Leaves `client.go`'s `convertMillisecondToSecond` conversion and all
tests/golden fixtures unchanged from `main` - no emitted values change

[exporter/azuremonitor] add configurable HTTP success mapping (#49399)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
The Azure Monitor exporter currently marks any HTTP span with a status
code
outside 100–399 as `Success = false` on the resulting Application
Insights
`RequestData / RemoteDependencyData`

This causes expected 4xx responses (most notably 404 for cache misses,
existence checks, optional resources, etc.) to show up as failed
requests/dependencies in Application Insights dashboards and alerts. It
also
diverges from the OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions, which state
that
4xx on server spans should not set the span status to Error.


[Spec](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/http/http-spans/#status)
for reference.


This pr adds two opt-in settings to the Azure Monitor exporter:
- `non_error_http_status_codes` (list of HTTP status codes treated as
Success on both server and client HTTP spans) and
- `align_http_server_request_success_with_otel_spec` (when true, 4xx
responses on HTTP server spans are treated as Success, matching the
OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions). Defaults preserve the existing
exporter behaviour.

[pkg/stanza/fileconsumer] Require explicit top_n when sort_by is configured (#47445)

#### Description

Fixes #47444. Configuring `ordering_criteria.sort_by` without `top_n`
previously
defaulted silently to `top_n: 1`, which caused severe log duplication
when
multiple files matched: only the single highest-priority file was
returned per
poll, so other matching files cycled in and out of the 3-generation
tracker
window and were re-read from offset 0 on rediscovery.

This change requires `top_n` to be set explicitly when `sort_by` is
configured:

- `sort_by` configured without `top_n` → validation error at startup,
forcing
  the user to make the choice explicit.
- `top_n: 0` means "match all files".
- `top_n > 0` limits as today.
- `top_n < 0` errors.

Per @paulojmdias's review feedback, this is treated as a bug fix per
#47444's
classification rather than a gated rollout. Existing configurations that
set
`sort_by` without `top_n` must be updated to include an explicit `top_n`
value
before upgrading.

#### Implementation notes

- `matcher.OrderingCriteria.TopN` is `*int` so the matcher can
distinguish
unset from explicit `0`. All existing callers are tests in the same
module —
  updated.
- Helper `validateTopN(*OrderingCriteria)` encapsulates the validation;
called
  only when `len(SortBy) > 0`.

#### Link to tracking issue

Fixes #47444

#### Testing

- Unit tests in `matcher/matcher_test.go` cover: unset + sort_by
(error), zero +
sort_by (pass — match all), positive + sort_by (pass — limit), unset +
no
  sort_by (pass).
- `TestMtimeSortWithTopNZeroReturnsAllFiles` (matcher unit): verifies
  `MatchFiles()` returns all 4 files with `top_n: 0`.
- End-to-end regression `TestTopNZeroNoDuplication` (file_test.go): 10
concurrently-written files, `sort_by: mtime`, `top_n: 0`, 20 rounds →
210
unique tokens, 0 duplicates. Uses `assert.EventuallyWithT` instead of
fixed
  sleeps for flake resistance per @paulojmdias's review.
- `gofmt`, `golangci-lint`, and full `pkg/stanza/fileconsumer/...` suite
all
  clean.

#### Note on chloggen component

@paulojmdias's [review
comment](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/47445#discussion_r3147786640)
suggested `component: pkg/stanza/fileconsumer`. The chloggen validator
at
`.chloggen/config.yaml` does not list that value as valid, but it does
list
`pkg/fileconsumer` — which appears to be a misnamed alias for the actual
path
`pkg/stanza/fileconsumer`. Using `pkg/fileconsumer` here to satisfy the
validator while honoring the intent of the suggestion. Sister PR for
#47861
(mtime skip) makes the same choice for consistency.

that uniquely identifies the cluster. The value is surfaced from the
`cluster_uuid` field already returned by the root endpoint via
`ClusterMetadata()`. The attribute is disabled by default to preserve
backward compatibility.

[cmd/opampsupervisor] Ignore non-positive heartbeat interval from connection settings and revert it on failed reconnect (#50305)

#### Description

This picks up #48362, which the stale bot closed before anyone got to
review it. Following @douglascamata's suggestion in #48363, I've
cherry-picked @strawgate's original commits with their authorship intact
and rebased them onto current `main`.

There are two bugs in `onOpampConnectionSettings`, and they feed into
each other:

1. If an `OpAMPConnectionSettings` offer carries a non-positive
`HeartbeatIntervalSeconds`, the supervisor applies it as-is and
overwrites its current interval with zero. opamp-go won't accept a zero
interval over HTTP (`heartbeat interval for httpclient must be greater
than zero`), and over WebSocket it quietly turns heartbeats off instead.
2. If reconnecting with the new settings fails, the supervisor restores
the previous server config but not the previous heartbeat interval, so
the fallback reconnect fails for exactly the same reason. The OpAMP
client is stopped at that point and never comes back. The process stays
up and keeps logging, so nothing looks obviously broken, but it never
polls the server again.

The practical result: a server that sends an offer with only `Headers`
set — rotating a token, say, or handing out a per-agent credential at
first enrollment — takes the agent offline for good. On first enrollment
it never receives a collector config at all. Full analysis and repro
steps are in #50268.

With this change, non-positive intervals are ignored and the current
value is kept, and the previous interval is restored alongside the
previous server config when the reconnect fails.

One difference from #48362: the third fix there (the missing `return` in
`saveAndReportConfigStatus`) is dropped, since it has been fixed on
`main` in the meantime. Its e2e test and the related test adjustments go
with it. That's why one commit here is a partial cherry-pick, as noted
in its commit message.

#### Link to tracking issue

Fixes #50268

#### Testing

- Unit tests cherry-picked from #48362
(`TestSupervisor_onOpampConnectionSettings`). They cover: a zero
interval leaves the current value alone; a positive interval updates it;
nothing is updated when `ReportsHeartbeat` is disabled; and the interval
is reverted when reconnecting with the new settings fails.
- The full `cmd/opampsupervisor` suite, `make lint` and `make
chlog-validate` pass locally.
- Validated end to end on `windows/amd64` against an OpAMP server
sending Headers-only offers over HTTP, i.e. the scenario from #50268.

#### Documentation

Changelog entry added:
`.chloggen/50268-supervisor-heartbeat-interval-guard.yaml`. No other
documentation changes.

\===

Some bug fixes (mostly minor - hence the delay for the release) found by
users
and further Claude audits. I am gearing up for a 1.22 release but some
of the
features I am planning for are more complicated to review, so it may
take a bit
of time. Anyway:

- Previously, rollback from a cooperative group to an eager group was
  deliberately not supported and there was a data race condition if this
happened. It is now *technically* supported, although you will
experience
duplicate data. If you want a safe non-duplicate-causing rollback, you
need
to turn off the entire group, remove the cooperative consumer, and swap
the
  whole group to eager rebalancing.

- Fixed a `panic: close of closed channel` on an `acks=0` produce
connection
in a specific edge case (a broker connection dying before the connection
  was fully established caused the panic).

- If `EndTransaction` failed with an unconfirmed outcome (a transport
error,
exhausted retries, or `UNKNOWN_SERVER_ERROR`), the documented abort
retry
was a wire no-op and the next transaction could silently commit the
prior
"failed" transaction's records under KIP-890 part 2. The producer ID is
now
flagged for reload, which fence-aborts anything still ongoing
broker-side.

- `GroupTransactSession.End` could hang forever, ignoring its context,
if the
group had never joined (e.g. the consumed topic did not exist yet) and
the
  transaction committed no offsets.

- Previously, if a broker replied to ApiVersions with an error, we
ignored it
and you would eventually see an unclear error (usually a bare io.EOF,
since
anything that rejects ApiVersions hangs up right after replying). These
  errors are now handled correctly.

- Some niche edge case bugs that are only worth reading about if you're
super
interested were found in repeated Claude audits and were fixed (check
the PR
/ git history). This includes further KIP-848 "next gen consumer group"
fixes.

[processor/dynamic_sampling] pre-alpha hardening: coverage gaps and doc corrections (#50249)

#### Description

Hardening pass ahead of the alpha promotion, from a full review sweep of
the component. No behaviour changes; the gaps found were in test
coverage and documentation accuracy.

- Tests for the runtime OTTL evaluation-error paths (rule conditions and
`root_span_condition`), pinning the treat-as-non-match behaviour and the
`ottl_eval_errors` counter with the right rule labels. These branches
previously had zero coverage.
- Test for a single batch carrying one trace split across multiple
ResourceSpans, the normal shape behind a gateway/loadbalancing tier:
distinct resource attributes must survive into the decided trace, and
late multi-resource batches must stamp every span. Both held; now
pinned.
- End-to-end smoke tests for `ema_throughput` and `windowed_throughput`
through the processor (previously only exercised via `Validate()`).
- Config validation table entries for `ema_throughput` weight bounds,
negative `windowed_throughput` frequencies, and an invalid `match` mode.
- Doc corrections against dynsampler-go's actual behaviour: `weight: 0`
means the sampler default (0.5), `update_frequency: 0` means 1s, and
`lookback_frequency` values are floored to a multiple of
`update_frequency` rather than rejected (the comment previously claimed
"must be a multiple"). Also documented the `,` value separator inside
sampling keys.
- Consistency fix in `ConsumeTraces`: the forward-or-drop guard for
evicted and late traces now re-reads `stopped` under the lock instead of
using a snapshot from the top of the batch, matching how the
timer-arming loop already reads it. Unreachable difference under the
component lifecycle contract, but the fresh read costs nothing on the
hot path (skipped when there is nothing to forward) and removes the
inconsistency.

#### Link to tracking issue

Refs #49311

#### Testing

- Four new test functions plus validation-table entries; full module
suite with `-race`, lint clean.
- Changelog entry (bug_fix) included for the stopped-guard fix; the rest
of the PR is tests and docs.

#### Documentation

- config.go field comments and README corrections described above.

Bump github.com/cilium/ebpf from 0.16.0 to 0.22.0 in /receiver/systemdreceiver (#50335) Bumps [github.com/cilium/ebpf](https://github.com/cilium/ebpf) from 0.16.0 to 0.22.0.
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/cilium/ebpf's releases.

v0.22.0: Linux 7.1 compat, BPF tokens and vmlinux BTF caching changes

Hi everyone! Today we announce the v0.22.0 release of ebpf-go. We ship Linux 7.1 compatibility, older versions of the library will not work on 7.1 kernels and above, so please upgrade if you are targeting the latest releases of Linux. We also made a breaking change to BTF caching, please read those notes. And of course a few fixes, improvements and minor features.

Kernel 7.1 compatibility

In kernel 7.1 the BTF header was extended to introduce a new feature called BTF layout. This change caused our BTF parser to fail when parsing vmlinux for this kernel. This has been fixed in this latest release, we recommend upgrading to this latest release to avoid breakage on 7.1 and newer kernels.

See cilium/ebpf#2042 for details. Special thanks to @​Capricornus007 for making the bug report that allowed us to fix this in a timely manner.

BPF token support

Some BPF-related actions require the user to have root privileges (CAP_SYS_ADMIN). One example is loading and attaching programs that can inspect kernel memory. In some environments, you may want to permit a known good process to load such BPF programs, but you don't want to grant it CAP_SYS_ADMIN to avoid privilege escalation if that process gets compromised.

BPF tokens are a mechanism that allows a privileged process to delegate fine-grained BPF capabilities to an unprivileged process. The process of delegating is complex and typically handled by a container runtime such as LXC or a process manager like systemd. This part of the handshake is currently out of scope of ebpf-go, as the library is not in charge of process creation where this delegation takes place.

However, the consuming side is what's included in this release. ebpf-go will automatically detect when the current process is running in a namespace where a BPF token is provided, and will automatically try to obtain an use it for interacting with the BPF syscall. Unlike libbpf, this currently requires no extra configuration on behalf of the application.

See cilium/ebpf#1953 for more details.

BTF cache changes

Package btf used to cache kernel (vmlinux) BTF specs globally. This is a significant time gain when loading multiple Collections in a row. However, doing so comes at a fairly significant memory cost (~20 MiB), so users could flush this cache with btf.FlushKernelSpec. Unfortunately, the caching behaviour being opt-out means users would typically discover it while investigating memory usage, and would then have to find an appropriate time during execution to call the flush function. This was always a band-aid for something we didn't have a clear solution to.

With this update, we've removed the global cache and the btf.FlushKernelSpec function, which may slow down subsequent collection loading on busy systems. To opt back in, users can now maintain their own cache object, obtained from btf.NewCache and pass it to NewCollectionWithOptions via CollectionOptions.Cache. Typically, you would put this in a global variable in a bpf-related package in your application, or keep it around in function scope if you load multiple collections in a row.

See cilium/ebpf#1988 for more details. Thank you @​matthyx for these changes.

#### Breaking changes

The `format` package now models thrift unions as sum types
([#​558](https://redirect.github.com/parquet-go/parquet-go/pull/558)).
If you use the `format` package directly:

- `format.LogicalType` and `format.TimeUnit` no longer expose one
pointer field per union member (e.g. `LogicalType.UTF8`,
`TimeUnit.Millis`); they now hold a single `Value` field typed as the
`format.LogicalTypeValue` / `format.TimeUnitValue` interface.
- Some optional slice fields (e.g. level histograms in the column and
offset indexes) changed from plain slices to `thrift.Slice[T]`, which
distinguishes unset from empty.

Code that only uses the top-level `parquet` package API is unaffected.

Configure named limiters under policies.resources.rate\_limiters using

Agent-fed auth gets endpoint, moniker, and token from one atomic

invalid or near-expiry data, supports rotation, and uses zeroizing
token/header

[processor/dynamic_sampling] restructure sampler config around intent-based types (#50313)

#### Description

Restructures the sampler configuration ahead of the alpha promotion,
while breaking changes are still cheap. The names came from user testing
of the config, which showed the original types described mechanisms
rather than intent.

Sampler types now state intent, and the algorithm choice moves out of
the type name into an optional field:

| before | after |
| --- | --- |
| `deterministic` | `probabilistic` (matches the `probabilistic_sampler`
processor, same hash-consistent fixed fraction) |
| `ema_dynamic` | `dynamic_percentage` |
| `ema_throughput` | `dynamic_throughput` (`algorithm: ema` is the
default) |
| `windowed_throughput` | `dynamic_throughput` + `algorithm: windowed` |

Before:

```yaml
rules:
  - name: background-noise
    sampler:
      type: deterministic
      sampling_percentage: 5
  - name: default
    sampler:
      type: ema_dynamic
      goal_sampling_percentage: 10
      key_attributes: ["service.name", "http.route"]
  - name: capped-output
    sampler:
      type: windowed_throughput
      goal_throughput_per_sec: 1000
      key_attributes: ["service.name"]
```

After:

```yaml
rules:
  - name: background-noise
    sampler:
      type: probabilistic
      sampling_percentage: 5
  - name: default
    sampler:
      type: dynamic_percentage
      goal_percentage: 10
      key_attributes: ["service.name", "http.route"]
  - name: capped-output
    sampler:
      type: dynamic_throughput
      algorithm: windowed
      goal_throughput: 1000
      key_attributes: ["service.name"]
```

Goal fields rename to match, `goal_sampling_percentage` ->
`goal_percentage` and `goal_throughput_per_sec` -> `goal_throughput`. On
the `deterministic` rename - every sampler here decides
hash-consistently via the ot=th threshold against trace randomness, so
"deterministic" described a property all types share, and the OTel
ecosystem already calls this behaviour probabilistic.

The same review standardised terminology. "Events" is gone, and the docs
now state the volume model plainly - decisions are made per trace,
volume is measured in spans (matching Refinery via GetSampleRateMulti
with the trace's span count). The README gains a Refinery migration
mapping, including the GoalSampleRate 1-in-N to goal_percentage
conversion.

Validation enforces the new shape. `algorithm` is rejected on
non-dynamic types, `windowed` is rejected on `dynamic_percentage`
(dynsampler-go has no sliding-window percentage sampler yet, so the
field keeps that additive), and tuning fields are checked against the
effective algorithm so ema tuning on a windowed sampler fails at
startup.

Draft while co-owners review the design.

#### Link to tracking issue

Refs #49311

#### Testing

- Existing suite migrated to the new names, plus validation cases for
the algorithm field (rejected on non-dynamic types, windowed rejected on
percentage, unknown algorithm, cross-algorithm tuning fields).
- New `TestReadmeConfigExamples` round-trips every README config example
through confmap and `Validate()`, so documented examples can't drift
from the config surface. Promotes yaml.v3 from indirect to direct
dependency, no new module.
- Full suite with `-race`, lint, generate (no drift), chloggen validate,
and a stale-vocabulary sweep across code, tests, and docs (internal
sampler error strings aligned too).

#### Documentation

- The README's existing examples are all updated to the new names in
this diff, and the samplers section is rewritten around the four types
and the algorithm field, with the volume model and the Refinery
migration mapping. Breaking changelog entry included.
- Fixes a pre-existing broken example (a stray nested `deterministic:`
block), now caught by the README example test.

[cmd/opampsupervisor] fix: forward full effective config map to OpAMP server (#49909)

**Description:**
Fixes the OpAMP supervisor so the full effective config map (all named
config files) is forwarded to the OpAMP server, instead of only the
empty-string ("") key.

Previously the supervisor extracted only the ""-keyed file body from the
agent's EffectiveConfig message and stored it as a string. When
createEffectiveConfigMsg rebuilt the forwarded message it created a map
with only the "" key, silently dropping every other named file. A
message with no "" key was rejected entirely, which contradicts the
OpAMP spec (where the "" name is optional and only for single-file
agents).

The fix:
- Stores the complete *protobufs.EffectiveConfig from the agent instead
  of extracting a single string.
- createEffectiveConfigMsg returns the stored protobuf as-is when
  available, preserving all named config files.
- Adds a guard that skips forwarding when the config map is nil or has
  zero entries (analogous to the old guard that required a "" entry).

**Link to tracking issue:**
Fixes #49902

**Testing:**
Unit tests updated in supervisor_test.go:
- Test_handleAgentOpAMPMessage: added test for multi-key config map
  storage ("EffectiveConfig - Effective config message contains multiple
  named files") and a full round-trip test ("EffectiveConfig -
  full round-trip preserves all config map keys") that sends 3 named
  files to handleAgentOpAMPMessage, then calls createEffectiveConfigMsg
  and asserts all 3 keys survive.
- TestSupervisor_createEffectiveConfigMsg: added test ("stored effective
  config has multiple keys - preserve all") verifying all keys are
  preserved when the stored effective config has multiple files.
- Updated "EffectiveConfig - Effective config message contains an empty
  config" to assert the config is NOT forwarded (config map has zero
  entries).
All 7 packages in cmd/opampsupervisor/supervisor pass
(go test ./... -count=1).

**Documentation:**
None -- this is a bug fix with no user-facing API or configuration
change.

[receiver/windowsperfcounters] Allow wildcard queries to include aggregation instances (#50239)

#### Description

Adds support for retaining a Windows performance counter aggregation
instance when collecting instances with a wildcard.

The existing behavior remains unchanged:

- `instances: "*"` collects all instances except `_Total`.
- `instances: "_Total"` collects `_Total` individually without an
`instance` attribute.

Users can opt into the new behavior by explicitly listing the
aggregation instance alongside the wildcard:

```yaml
instances: ["*", "_Total"]
```
This collects all instances, including _Total, and preserves
instance="_Total". The receiver continues to create a single wildcard
PDH query.
The new aggregation_name object-level setting identifies counters that
use a different aggregation instance name. It defaults to _Total.
For example:
```yaml
instances: ["*", "_Global_"]
aggregation_name: "_Global_"
```
This retains _Global_ alongside the wildcard results. With only
instances: "*", the configured aggregation instance continues to be
omitted.
The implementation applies the same aggregation handling to formatted
and raw counter values.

#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #29054

#### Testing

- Added and updated tests covering:
- Existing wildcard behavior that omits _Total.
- Wildcard collection that retains _Total.
- Preservation of the aggregation instance attribute.
- Custom aggregation instance names such as _Global_.
- Standalone default and custom aggregation instances.
- Formatted and raw counter cleanup.
- Preservation of aggregation settings after query recreation.
- Configuration loading and behavior selection.
- Creation of one wildcard watcher for ["*", "_Total"].
- Receiver-level emission of _Total as an attributed datapoint.
- Validation performed:
- Native tests with race detection.
- Windows amd64 and arm64 test cross-compilation.
- Native, Windows amd64, and Windows arm64 builds.
- golangci-lint for both affected modules.
- Windows-targeted go vet.
- Module tidy verification.
- Configuration schema generation.
- API compatibility validation.
- Changelog validation.
- Git whitespace validation.
- The PDH-backed integration test was cross-compiled locally and is
expected to execute in Windows CI because the local development host is
macOS.

#### Documentation
- Updated the Windows Performance Counters receiver README with:
- The aggregation_name configuration option.
- Backward-compatible wildcard behavior.
- Examples for retaining _Total.
- Examples for custom aggregation names.
- A warning about potential double-counting when aggregate and component
instances are exported together.
- Regenerated config.schema.yaml and added a changelog entry.

[processor/dynamic_sampling] rename key_attributes to fingerprint_attributes (#50321)

#### Description

Renames the sampler `key_attributes` field to `fingerprint_attributes`.
The new name describes what the field is for - naming the attributes
that identify what kind of trace this is - rather than how it's
implemented. Semantics are unchanged, values are still collected from
resource attributes and from every span of the accumulated trace.

Before:

```yaml
sampler:
  type: dynamic_percentage
  goal_percentage: 10
  key_attributes: ["service.name", "http.route"]
```

After:

```yaml
sampler:
  type: dynamic_percentage
  goal_percentage: 10
  fingerprint_attributes: ["service.name", "http.route"]
```

The README's old "Sampling keys" section becomes "Fingerprints" and now
documents the collection model in full (per-attribute `,` joins, `•`
between attributes, `<missing>` placeholders, whole-trace collection),
plus guidance on choosing fingerprint attributes - classify traffic
(route, status code, method, service), don't identify individual
requests (user IDs, request IDs, raw URLs), which would give every trace
its own key and defeat the adaptation.

Builds on #50313 (the sampler type restructure, now merged). Scoped
fingerprint entries (resource./span./root. selectors) come separately
after this.

#### Link to tracking issue

Refs #49311

#### Testing

- Suite migrated to the new field name, including validation error
assertions.
- `TestReadmeConfigExamples` validates every renamed README example
against the real config surface.
- Full module suite with `-race`, lint, chloggen validate.

#### Documentation

- The README's existing examples are all updated to
`fingerprint_attributes` in this diff, and the Fingerprints section adds
the collection model and attribute-choice guidance. Breaking changelog
entry included.

observer work originally proposed in #48663. The split plan is

can be reused.

`internal/k8sinventory/informer `package. The k8sobjects receiver is not
wired to it yet, so there is no user-visible behavior change_.**
3. Follow-up — migrate the k8sobjects receiver to use the new observer.

##### What this PR adds:
* `FactoryRegistry`: reuses informers for the same `(namespace,
labelSelector, fieldSelector)` scope and GVR, so multiple observers can
share one informer and one `List+Watch` connection.

* `Observer`: implements the existing `k8sinventory.Observer` interface
using a factory from the registry. It supports both modes:

* Pull mode: waits for the initial cache sync, then emits `store.List()`
snapshots on the configured interval. It does not call the API on every
tick.
* Watch mode: registers a `ResourceEventHandler`, converts informer
callbacks to `apiWatch.Event`, applies the `Exclude` filter, and saves
`resourceVersion` checkpoints through the shared checkpoint package,
with periodic flushes and a final flush on stop.

[pkg/stanza/fileconsumer] Skip files unchanged by path+mtime since the previous poll (#48039)

#### Description

~~Adds the opt-in `filelog.skipUnchangedPathByMtime` feature gate
(alpha).~~ This PR now adds a new boolean config option
`skip_unmodified_files`, defaulting to off. When set to `true`, files
whose stat mtime matches the `LastObservedMtime` of an already-tracked
reader (in `previousPollFiles` or any `knownFiles` generation) are
skipped entirely for the current poll: no open, no fingerprint, no read.
The matched metadata is promoted into the freshest `knownFiles`
generation so it ages on the same schedule as if it had been processed.

This was originally feature gated. However, after discussion with
stakeholders it was decided to implement it as an opt-in configuration
option instead.

#### Motivation

Quoting @braydonk on #47444 (the discussion that spawned #47861):

> Something that could work would be not to change the fingerprint
identities,
> but instead to maintain a light cache of the paths we saw last poll
and their
> mtimes at that poll, then next poll paths are compared to the cache of
mtimes
> by path that we saw last poll.

For deployments with many matching files (e.g. per-host syslog outputs
where
most files are idle most of the time), every poll currently re-opens
every
file just to recompute its fingerprint and conclude "no new data." This
wastes
IO at scale. The skip path turns those checks into a single `stat` per
file.

#### Design notes

- **Reader-lifetime metadata, not a parallel cache.** `LastObservedPath`
and
`LastObservedMtime` live on `reader.Metadata`, so the mtime tracking
ages on
the same lifecycle as the reader itself (knownFiles generations +
archive).
An earlier draft used a per-poll cache; that was rejected because a
cache
  that expires before the reader does would cause re-reads.
- **`os.Stat`, not `os.Lstat`.** Symlinks resolve to the same target
file
  `os.Open` would otherwise read; an in-code comment documents this.
- **Internal archive intentionally not consulted.** The fileconsumer's
internal `archive` package (the persistent metadata store for readers
that
have aged out of the active `knownFiles` window — unrelated to
file-format
archives like gzip) is queried by fingerprint, not path. Path+mtime
lookup
  there would conflate path-based identity with fingerprint-based
resume-identity: an archived pre-rotation file and a current
post-rotation
file at the same path could share an mtime, and treating them as
identical
would silently skip new content. Path+mtime skip is therefore scoped to
the
  active generation window only.

#### Link to tracking issue

Refs #47861

#### Testing

- Unit tests in `internal/tracker/tracker_test.go` cover the helper
`TryReuseByPathMtime` across 6 scenarios: hit in `previousPollFiles`,
hit
  in earlier `knownFiles` generations, mtime mismatch, path mismatch, no
  candidates, and empty path.
- End-to-end `TestSkipUnmodifiedFiles` in `file_test.go`: sets
`skip_unmodified_files: true`, creates files, polls once, then verifies
subsequent polls do not re-read files whose mtimes haven't changed.
- `gofmt`, `golangci-lint`, and full `pkg/stanza/fileconsumer/...` suite
all
  clean.

#### Note on chloggen component

The actual path is `pkg/stanza/fileconsumer`, but that value is not in
the
chloggen validator's allowed list at `.chloggen/config.yaml`. The
closest
valid entry is `pkg/fileconsumer`, which appears to be a misnamed alias
for
the actual path. Using that to satisfy the validator. Sister PR #47445
makes
the same choice based on @paulojmdias's review feedback there.

[processor/dynamic_sampling] require scoped selectors for fingerprint attributes (#50352)

#### Description

Requires `fingerprint_attributes` entries to be scoped attribute
selectors, so each entry says where its value is read from.

Before:

```yaml
fingerprint_attributes: ["service.name", "http.route"]
```

After:

```yaml
fingerprint_attributes:
  - resource.attributes["service.name"]
  - span.attributes["http.route"]
```

| Scope | Reads from |
| --- | --- |
| `resource.` | each resource's attributes |
| `scope.` | each instrumentation scope's attributes |
| `span.` | every span's attributes |
| `root.` | the spans matching the configured `root_span_condition` |
| `any.` | the union of resource, instrumentation scope, and span
attributes |

The `resource.`/`scope.`/`span.` prefixes match OTTL's span-context path
names, so conditions and fingerprint entries share one spelling. Entries
are selectors, not OTTL expressions - fingerprints are built from the
whole trace while OTTL evaluates one span at a time, which is why
`root.` and `any.` can exist here but not in OTTL.

Each selector collects every distinct value it matches, so there's no
first-match or precedence order to remember. Bare names are rejected
with an error that shows the scoped form. I went with rejection rather
than a default scope. A span default would silently turn resource
attributes like `service.name` into `<missing>` keys, and an `any.`
default quietly opts users into scanning every span. If the requirement
turns out to be annoying we can relax it later without breaking anyone,
but whatever default we pick now gets frozen at alpha.

#### Link to tracking issue

Refs #49311

#### Testing

- Selector parser table, per-scope extraction tests (root-matcher
behaviour, any-scope union), and an end-to-end processor test for the
root-selector wiring.
- Per-scope benchmarks across trace sizes with a span-miss variant.
`resource.`/`scope.` are flat (~47ns). The walking scopes on a
10,000-span trace cost 25-32us per entry when lookups miss or skip and
~155us when the key hits every span. There are no allocations on the
extraction path, and the root matcher (which reuses the `IsRootSpan()`
fast path) is only built for rules with `root.` entries.
- `TestReadmeConfigExamples` plus the full module suite with `-race`,
lint, chloggen validate.

#### Documentation

- The README's Fingerprints section now documents the selector grammar,
the scope table, union semantics, and extraction cost, with all examples
updated. It also recommends qualifying every OTTL path so conditions and
selectors read the same, and corrects a wrong claim that OTTL requires
qualification (unqualified paths are valid and resolve to the span
context). Breaking changelog entry included, with bare-name migration
guidance.

[processor/dynamic_sampling] add record_fingerprint attribute recording (#50353)

#### Description

Adds `record_fingerprint` (default `none`), which stamps the matched
rule's fingerprint on every span of a kept trace under
`otelcol.processor.dynamic_sampling.fingerprint`, the same pattern as
the rule-name attribute. Late-arriving spans get the same value via the
decision cache, so a trace's spans never disagree.

```yaml
dynamic_sampling:
  record_fingerprint: hash   # none (default) | value | hash
```

`value` records the raw fingerprint. `hash` records the first 8 bytes of
its SHA-256 as 16 hex characters, so the size is fixed and the same key
always produces the same token across instances and restarts. A span's
token can be verified by recomputing from the raw fingerprint, `echo -n
'<fingerprint>' | sha256sum | cut -c1-16`. The goal is obfuscation and
size control, not privacy. No unsalted hash protects guessable values
from enumeration, and the docs say so. I picked SHA-256 over a faster
non-cryptographic hash because the cost lands once per decision and it
holds up for high-entropy values.

Rules whose sampler has no `fingerprint_attributes` (`always_sample`,
`probabilistic`) never produce the attribute, nor do
probabilistic-eviction decisions.

Also adds a `fingerprint_duration` histogram (microseconds,
rule-labelled, recorded once per decision around the extraction) so an
expensive fingerprint, eg a wide `any.` scope on large traces, is
attributable at runtime. The metric description is explicit that it's a
relative signal, absolute values depend on host and load.

Was stacked on #50352 (scoped selectors), which has merged, so the diff
is now scoped to this change.

#### Link to tracking issue

Refs #49311

#### Testing

- Tests per mode (off by default, raw value, deterministic hash matching
the documented recompute recipe), late-span consistency, and the
no-fingerprint sampler case.
- Decide-path benchmarks across modes. Enabling costs one attribute
write per span (~20-30% on decide, +1 alloc/span). Value and hash are
indistinguishable, the SHA runs once per decision.
- A metric test pins the histogram's rule attribute; full module suite
with `-race`, lint, generate, chloggen validate.

#### Documentation

- README metrics table row for the new histogram, an output-attributes
table row, plus a "Recording the fingerprint" section with the recompute
recipe, the enumeration caveat, and the decision-cache size note for
value mode. Changelog entry (enhancement) included.
