[chore] Free Go caches during scoped-test on Windows to avoid disk exhaustion (#51130)

#### Description
This PR frees Go caches during scoped-test on Windows to avoid disk
exhaustion.

`for-affected-components` builds and tests the whole affected set, which
is close to the entire repo when a broadly-imported module changes. On
the Windows runners `GOCACHE`, `GOMODCACHE` and the build temp dir all
live on C: (~14 GiB free), so the accumulating build cache eventually
fills C: and a compile fails with "not enough space on the disk" while
writing to `$WORK`.

This PR adds an opt-in `FREE_DISK_THRESHOLD_MIB` that makes
`for-affected-components` run `go clean -cache -testcache` between
components once free space drops below the threshold, and enables it
(4096 MiB) only on the Windows scoped-test runners. Free space is
measured on `/` (matching `check-disk-space.sh`), which under Git Bash
resolves to C:, the drive that fills and the one `go clean` reclaims,
rather than the D: drive the repo is checked out on. It is empty by
default, so local and Linux runs are unaffected.

#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #51122

[exporter/doris] fix schema creation on Doris 4.x and add a trace summary view (#51265)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

This PR fixes three problems that leave the Doris exporter without a
usable schema on Doris 4.x, and adds a materialized view for trace-list
queries.


**Fixes**

- Materialized views were never created. Their output columns had the
same names as the base table columns, which Doris rejects with
`Duplicate column name`. The error was only logged at warn level, so
deployments silently ran with no views at all — for traces, logs and
metrics alike. Every view now aliases its output columns.
- Views were created immediately after `CREATE TABLE`, while the table's
dynamic partitions were still being created in the background. The
exporter now polls `SHOW PARTITIONS` first and skips view creation with
a warning if they do not appear within 60s.
- The trace service graph job was named `<database>:<job>`, which Doris
does not accept, so the job was never created and `<traces>_graph`
stayed empty. It now uses `<database>.<job>`.

**Traces schema**

The traces table gains an `is_root TINYINT` column (1 for spans without
a parent, computed by the exporter) with an inverted index, and a
`<traces>_summary` materialized view that aggregates each trace by
`trace_id` and day: start and end time, span count, error count,
earliest root span, max span duration.

Note that the view is not a free speedup: Doris only rewrites a query to
it when the query groups by `trace_id, date_trunc(timestamp, 'day')`, so
a client has to shape its SQL accordingly to benefit. On a 33M-span
table, a trace-list query written in that shape takes 1.3s versus 8.1s
for the equivalent query against the base table.

`<traces>_summary` is created in addition to the existing
`<traces>_services` view, not as a replacement. Doris refuses to create
a second synchronous view while the first is still building, so the two
are created one after the other.

Existing tables are not altered. The new column and view only apply to
tables created with `create_schema: true`. Table key, bucketing,
partitioning, column types, the remaining inverted indexes and the
default timezone are unchanged, and the logs and metrics tables are
untouched apart from the view alias fix.

#### Description

Use high cardinality attributes as `fingerprint_attributes` can d
egrades goal accuracy directly. An adaptive sampler can never drop a
key's rate below 1 (it must always keep at least one instance of any key
it's tracking), so as the number of distinct keys grows, more o
f them sit at that rate-1 floor with only a handful of eve
nts each, and the sampler can't discard enough traffic acr
oss the keyspace to hit the configured `goal_percentage`/`
goal_throughput`. Keeping the key space small is what make
s the adaptive samplers effective.
Setting a default value for max_key config in samplers that support this
option.

#### Link to tracking issue

cause unstable sampling results.

[receiver/postgresql] Add postgresql.backend.connection.start to query samples (#50771)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
- `postgresql.query_start` is the only timestamp query samples currently
carry, and it changes on every query the backend runs, so it can't
represent how long the underlying connection has been open.
- Adds `postgresql.backend.connection.start` (RFC3339 string) sourced
from `pg_stat_activity.backend_start`, to `db.server.query_sample`.
- Follows the same pattern already used for
`postgresql.blocking.start_time` / `postgresql.blocking.wait_duration`
elsewhere in the same event: an RFC3339 timestamp paired with a derived
whole-seconds duration.
#### Why
- A query sample currently tells you what a backend is doing right now
and since when, but not how old the connection itself is - there's no
way to identify a long-running or idle connection from the emitted
attributes without a separate query against `pg_stat_activity`.

[receiver/oracledb] Add a db.server.query_plan event for the execution plan (#51121)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

Execution plans embedded in `db.server.top_query` can be large payloads:
a plan is JSON holding one entry per plan step, so it dwarfs the small
numeric and identifier attributes carried alongside it. When several
land in one batch the combined size can exceed transport/buffer limits,
dropping the whole batch and losing the lightweight query statistics
along with the oversized plan.

`db.server.query_plan` is disabled by default, so default output is
unchanged. When it is enabled the plan is reported on the new event,
joined back via `oracledb.sql_id + oracledb.child_number` and
`oracledb.plan_hash_value`, and `db.server.top_query` reports
`oracledb.query_plan` as an empty string. The event is sourced from top
query collection, so it does nothing unless db.server.top_query is
enabled too.

[chore][receiver/kafkametrics] Share a single franz-go admin client across all scrapers (#48785)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

Each enabled scraper previously created its own franz-go client,
resulting in a separate connection pool, metadata cache, and
SASL/ApiVersions handshake per scraper. Since Franz-go caches cluster
metadata per client instance, this duplicates the (potentially large)
metadata that has to be fetched and held in memory on every scrape. The
scrapers now share a single client that is created lazily on the first
scrape and closed once all scrapers have shut down, reducing connections
to the cluster and memory usage.

[chore][internal/k8sinventory] Migrate watch Observer to WatchFuncWithContext (#51184)

#### Description
This PR replaces the deprecated `cache.ListWatch.WatchFunc` with
`WatchFuncWithContext`. The watch package already threads a cancelable
context through `doWatch` to `NewRetryWatcherWithContext`, but
`watchFunc` closed over the outer `ctx` instead of receiving it per
call.

`watchFunc` now takes a `context.Context` parameter and is set via
`WatchFuncWithContext` so the per-call context is used, and the
`//nolint:staticcheck` suppression is dropped.

#### Upgrade notes

The binary format does not change. v0.3.0 decodes sketches that v0.1.0
to v0.2.6 encoded, and v0.2.6 decodes sketches that v0.3.0 encodes.

##### Code changes for callers

- Match errors with `errors.Is`. Do not compare errors with `==` or by
their text.
- When you append an encoded sketch to a larger buffer, frame it.

##### Behavior changes

- `UnmarshalBinary`, `MarshalBinary`, `AppendBinary`, and `Merge` wrap
the errors that they return. `err == ErrorTooShort` is always false.
- `Merge` wraps `ErrorPrecisionMismatch` when the precisions differ. The
error message includes both precisions.
- `UnmarshalBinary` rejects trailing bytes with `ErrorInvalidData`. It
also rejects unknown versions, invalid precisions, out-of-range
registers, and malformed sparse lists.
- If `UnmarshalBinary` returns an error, the receiver does not change.
The sketch that it decodes does not share memory with the input buffer.
- `Insert` and `InsertHash` on a zero-value `Sketch` give it precision
14 and the sparse representation, the same as `New`. In v0.2.6, they
panicked.
- `Merge` into a zero-value `Sketch` copies the other sketch, and
`Estimate` on a zero-value `Sketch` returns 0. In v0.2.6, both panicked.
- `Merge` with a zero-value argument does nothing. In v0.2.6, it
returned an error.
- `MarshalBinary` and `AppendBinary` on a zero-value `Sketch` return an
error that wraps `ErrorInvalidPrecision`. In v0.2.6, they returned an
8-byte header with precision 0.
- `Estimate` converts a sparse sketch to dense when its sparse list
grows past the register count. In v0.2.6, calls to `Estimate` between
small batches of inserts let the sparse list grow without limit.
- A sketch that v0.2.6 saved with such an oversized sparse list can give
a different estimate after v0.3.0 decodes it. In tests, the difference
was 1.1% or less.

##### Additions

- `Sketch.Reset` clears a sketch and keeps its representation and
allocated storage.
- `ErrorInvalidVersion`, `ErrorInvalidPrecision`, `ErrorInvalidData`,
and `ErrorPrecisionMismatch` are sentinel errors to match with
`errors.Is`.

### Release Notes

<summary>twmb/franz-go (github.com/twmb/franz-go/pkg/kmsg)</summary>

###
[`v1.14.0`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v1140)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/compare/v1.13.1...v1.14.0)

\===

This release contains a few new APIs, one behavior change, and one minor
bugfix.

#### Bug fixes

Previously, `HookBrokerRead` and `HookBrokerE2E` could not be used at
the same
time. This has been fixed.

#### Behavior changes

`PauseFetch{Topics,Partitions}` now causes the client to drop all
buffered
fetches and kill all in-flight fetch requests. Importantly, this also
means
that once you pause, it is no longer possible for what you paused to be
returned while polling. Previously, the client made no attempt to clear
internal buffers / in flight requests, meaning you could receive paused
data
for a while.

Seed brokers now show up in logs as `seed_###` rather than `seed ###`
(an
underscore has been added).

#### Features

- `kgo.Offset` now has an `EpochOffset` getter function that allows
access
to the actual epoch and offset that are inside the opaque `Offset` type.
- `AddConsumePartitions` allows adding individual partitions to consume,
and
the new counterpart `RemoveConsumePartitions` allows removing individual
partitions from being consumed. Removing is different from purging,
please
  see the docs.
- `KeepRetryableFetchErrors` bubbles up retryable errors to the end user
that
  are encountered while fetching. By default, these errors are stripped.
- kversion now supports Kafka 3.5
- kversion now supports version guessing against KRaft by default
- `kgo.DialTLS` now exists to even more easily opt into TLS.
- `kgo.Client.Opts` now exists to return the original options that were
used
  to configure the client, making initializing new clients easier.
- `kgo.NodeName` returns a string form of a broker node name.
Internally, seed
brokers use math.MinInt32 for node IDs, which shows up as massively
negative
numbers in logs sometimes. `NodeName` can help convert that to
`seed_<#>`.

#### Relevant commits

- [`c3b083b`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/c3b083b)
**improvement** kgo: do not returned paused topics/partitions after
pausing
- [`e224e90`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/e224e90)
**bugfix** kgo: allow HookBrokerRead and HookBrokerE2E to both be called
- [`875761a`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/875761a)
**feature** kgo Offset: add EpochOffset getter field
- [`c5d0fc5`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/c5d0fc5)
kgo: add a debug log for stripping retryable errors from fetches
- [`b45d663`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/b45d663)
kgo: add more context to opportunistic metadata loads while fetching
- [`9dae366`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/9dae366)
kgo: allow retries on dial timeouts
- [`00e4e76`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/00e4e76)
kgo: tolerate buggy v1 group member metadata
- [`34c8b3d`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/34c8b3d)
**feature** kgo: add AddConsumePartitions and RemoveConsumePartitions
- [`b5cafba`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/b5cafba)
sasl: validate non-empty user/pass/token
- [`76d2e71`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/76d2e71)
**feature** kgo: add KeepRetryableFetchErrors
- [`0df3ec0`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/0df3ec0)
kgo: fix new niche CI problem against Kafka 3.5
- [`8ff1d0d`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/8ff1d0d)
**feature** pkg/kversion: attempt to guess KRaft by default as well
- [`e92f5d9`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/e92f5d9)
**feature** pkg/kversion: detect v3.5
- [`f1b923e`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/f1b923e)
**feature** kgo: add DialTLS option
- [`9667967`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/9667967)
**feature** kgo.Client: add Opts to return the original opts, to allow
seeding new clients
- [`8e14928`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/commit/8e14928)
**feature** kgo: add NodeName for easy user formatting of internal seed
node IDs

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk
(github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk)</summary>

###
[`v1.8.0`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/releases/tag/v1.8.0)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/compare/v1.7.0...v1.8.0)

***This release is equivalent to v1.8.0-pre.2. Thank you to those who
tested the pre-release.***

In this release we introduce several fixes and improvements on top of
[v1.7.0](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/releases/tag/v1.7.0).
It adds no new protocol revision: the supported set is unchanged, and
`2026-07-28` remains the newest version the SDK negotiates.

The bulk of the work is hardening the transports against resource
exhaustion, closing session leaks, deadlocks and teardown hangs found by
users running the new protocol at scale, and giving servers explicit
control over which protocol versions they advertise.

Two behavior changes are guarded by new `MCPGODEBUG` flags; see the
section below.

#### Hardening against resource exhaustion

Every decoding path that buffers incoming input is now bounded. JSON
payloads are rejected past 1000 levels of nesting, before the parser
recurses. Both SSE readers cap the bytes buffered for a single event via
`MaxEventSize` on `SSEClientTransport` and `StreamableClientTransport`,
and the stdio transport caps a single JSON-RPC frame via
`StdioTransport.MaxLineLength`.

On the OAuth side, dynamic client registration responses are bounded to
1 MB, and the discovery code now validates metadata documents rather
than trusting them.

- internal/json: json nesting depth check by
[@​yarolegovich](https://redirect.github.com/yarolegovich)
([#​1200](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1200))
- mcp: add an sse event size cap by
[@​yarolegovich](https://redirect.github.com/yarolegovich)
([#​1205](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1205))
- mcp: add a max request body size of the old transport by
[@​yarolegovich](https://redirect.github.com/yarolegovich)
([#​1224](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1224))
- oauthex: bound dcr read to 1mb by
[@​yarolegovich](https://redirect.github.com/yarolegovich)
([#​1206](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1206))
- oauthex: oauth discovery checks by
[@​yarolegovich](https://redirect.github.com/yarolegovich)
([#​1220](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1220))

#### Restricting the protocol versions a server supports

`ServerOptions.SupportedProtocolVersions` lets a server narrow the set
of versions it advertises and negotiates. The list can only narrow,
never widen; naming a version the SDK does not implement panics at
construction.
Relatedly, a stateful streamable handler receiving a `2026-07-28`
request now returns that same JSON-RPC error instead of a plain-text
400, so the client can renegotiate down instead of losing the
connection.

- mcp: allow restricting the protocol versions a server supports by
[@​guglielmo-san](https://redirect.github.com/guglielmo-san)
([#​1199](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1199))
- mcp: return json-rpc error on stateful server serving
protocolVersion20260728 requests by
[@​guglielmo-san](https://redirect.github.com/guglielmo-san)
([#​1143](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1143))
- mcp: limit SSE discover supportedVersions to SSE-defined revisions by
[@​arimu1](https://redirect.github.com/arimu1)
([#​1121](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1121))
- mcp: prefer the negotiated protocol version over the request context
by [@​gwyszynski-sa](https://redirect.github.com/gwyszynski-sa)
([#​1163](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1163))
- mcp: export ClientSessionOptions.ProtocolVersion by
[@​arimu1](https://redirect.github.com/arimu1)
([#​1127](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1127))

#### Per-request cache control

`ServerOptions.SetCacheable` is a new hook that decides the `ttlMs` and
`cacheScope` fields of every result carrying them: `server/discover`,
the four list methods, and `resources/read`. It runs once per result,
after the handler returns, with the values that handler produced, so it
can set a policy globally while still letting an individual handler
override it. Anything left unset falls back to the protocol default of
`public`.

- mcp: allow per request Cacheable customization by
[@​guglielmo-san](https://redirect.github.com/guglielmo-san)
([#​1203](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1203))

#### Behavior changes guarded by MCPGODEBUG

Two new escape-hatch flags restore the previous behavior of the changes
above. Both will be removed in **v1.9.0**.

- **`plaintextstatefulrejection=1`** — restore the plain-text
`http.Error` 400 body a stateful `StreamableHTTPHandler` previously
returned for a request carrying per-request metadata. The default is now
a JSON-RPC `-32022 CodeUnsupportedProtocolVersion` error with an
`UnsupportedProtocolVersionData` payload advertising the legacy versions
the server supports. Introduced by
[#​1143](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1143).
- **`blockingcancelnotify=1`** — restore the previous behavior where a
cancelled call waits synchronously for `notifications/cancelled` to be
delivered (up to 5s) before returning, joining any delivery error into
the caller's error. The default now retires the call immediately and
sends the notification asynchronously. Introduced by
[#​1151](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1151).

Options below were removed, according to plan:

- `seterroroverwrite`
- `enableoriginverification`
- `disablecontenttypecheck`
- `disablelocalhostprotection`

##### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `all`: Remove the deprecated mezmo exporter.
([#​49953](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49953))
  Use the OTLP/HTTP exporter to send logs directly to Mezmo instead. See
  <https://docs.mezmo.com/telemetry-pipelines/otel-collector> and
<https://docs.mezmo.com/telemetry-pipelines/open-telemetry-source> for
migration guidance.

- `cmd/opampsupervisor`: Deprecate the `reports_remote_config`
capability config option. The `accepts_remote_config` option now enables
both the AcceptsRemoteConfig and ReportsRemoteConfig OpAMP capabilities.
([#​49763](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49763))
`reports_remote_config` is still accepted but has no effect. The
supervisor logs an error at startup when it is set to `true`.
Configurations with `accepts_remote_config: true` and
`reports_remote_config: false` now report remote config status.
  The option will fail startup in v0.163.0 and be removed in v0.165.0.

- `extension/azure_encoding`: Promote
extension.azureencoding.DontEmitV0LogConventions and
extension.azureencoding.EmitV1LogConventions feature gates to Beta
([#​50885](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50885))
The gates are now enabled by default, so Azure log records emit the v1
semconv attribute exception.message instead of the deprecated v1.39.0
attribute error.message. Disable both gates to restore the previous
behavior.

- `extension/google_cloud_logentry_encoding`: Promote
extension.encoding.googlecloudlogentryencoding.DontEmitV0RPCConventions
feature gate to Beta
([#​50879](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50879))
The gate is now enabled by default, so the audit log parser no longer
emits the deprecated semconv v1.38.0 attributes rpc.jsonrpc.error\_code
and rpc.jsonrpc.error\_message. It can be disabled to restore the
previous behavior.

- `pkg/coreinternal`: Promote
internal.coreinternal.goldendataset.DontEmitV0MessagingConventions and
internal.coreinternal.goldendataset.EmitV1MessagingConventions feature
gates to Beta
([#​45077](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/45077))
  Both feature gates should be promoted together as per RFC.
goldendataset now generates spans with messaging.destination.name
(semconv v1.40.0) by default,
and no longer generates the deprecated messaging.destination (semconv
v1.16.0) and
  messaging.destination.kind (semconv v1.19.0) attributes.

- `pkg/faro`: Promote
`pkg.translator.faro.EmitV1DeploymentEnvironmentConventions` and
`pkg.translator.faro.DontEmitV0DeploymentEnvironmentConventions` feature
gates to beta.
([#​45074](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/45074))
Make faroreceiver emit deployment.environment.name instead of
deployment.environment resource attribute by default.

- `pkg/kafka/configkafka`: Reject configurations that set both
`auth.sasl` and `auth.kerberos`.
([#​50748](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50748))

- `pkg/ottl`: Promote the `ottl.PanicDuplicateName` feature gate to
stable.
([#​50873](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50873))

- `pkg/ottl`: Remove the deprecated `Base64Decode` converter. Use the
`Decode` converter with the `base64` encoding instead.
([#​50875](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50875))

- `pkg/ottl`: Promote the `ottl.set.allowNil` feature gate to beta,
enabling it by default.
([#​49741](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49741))
When enabled, the `set` function passes `nil` values directly to the
target instead of treating them as a no-op.

- `processor/k8s_attributes`: Promote logs, metrics, and traces signals
from beta to stable.
([#​49152](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49152))
Promote the following feature gates from alpha to beta (enabled by
default):
- `processor.k8sattributes.EmitV1K8sConventions`: emits stable semconv
attribute names (e.g. `k8s.pod.label.*` singular form).
- `processor.k8sattributes.DontEmitV0K8sConventions`: disables legacy
semconv attribute names (e.g. `k8s.pod.labels.*` plural form).
Users relying on the legacy names should disable these gates or migrate
to the stable names.
It is advised that dual emission is used for the migration period. This
can be achieved through the feature gates:

`--feature-gates=-processor.k8sattributes.DontEmitV0K8sConventions,processor.k8sattributes.EmitV1K8sConventions`.
More information can be found at the respective documentation
[section](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/processor/k8sattributesprocessor/README.md#semantic-conventions-compatibility).

- `processor/signing`: Include the log record body in the signed payload
whatever its type. Previously only a string body was signed, so a record
with a structured body and a record with no body produced identical
canonical bytes and shared a signature.
([#​50911](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50911))
The body is now routed through the same `valueToInterface` conversion as
attributes, which handles every `pcommon.Value` type, enforces the
existing
nesting depth cap, and preserves the UTF-8 validation that previously
guarded
the string-only path. An unset body is still omitted rather than encoded
as
  null, so records without a body are unaffected.

This changes the canonical form for any record carrying a non-string
body, so
signatures produced by earlier versions over such records will not
reproduce.

Two new failure modes follow from the body no longer being discarded: a
record
whose structured body pushes the canonical payload past the 2 MiB limit,
or
whose body nests deeper than 128 levels, now fails to sign where it
previously
  signed with the body silently omitted.

- `receiver/kubelet_stats`: Promote the
`receiver.kubeletstats.cpuUsageScrapeBased` feature gate to beta
(enabled by default).
([#​49477](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49477))
`container.cpu.usage`, `k8s.pod.cpu.usage` and `k8s.node.cpu.usage` (and
the cpu utilization
metrics derived from them) are now calculated as the rate of the
corresponding `*.cpu.time`
counter between consecutive scrapes, instead of being read from the
kubelet's `UsageNanoCores`
value. As a result these metrics are not reported on the first scrape
after startup.
  To restore the previous behavior, run the collector with
  `--feature-gates=-receiver.kubeletstats.cpuUsageScrapeBased`.

- `receiver/sqlserver`: Remove `server.address` and `server.port` from
`db.server.top_query` log record attributes

([#​50384](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50384))
Remove `server.address` and `server.port` from `db.server.top_query` log
record attributes as they duplicate the resource-level attributes and
cause inconsistency when overridden via a processor. Both attributes are
now enabled by default at the resource level. The
`receiver.sqlserver.RemoveServerResourceAttribute` feature gate has been
removed.

##### 🚀 New components 🚀

- `extension/sd_notify`: Prepare the initial implementation for
`sd_notify` extension.
([#​49607](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49607))
- `processor/rolling_span_latency`: Add rollingspanlatencyprocessor.
([#​50260](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50260))
- `processor/signing`: Add `signingprocessor` implementation — computes
RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical hash and signs each log record, storing the
base64-encoded signature as `audit.integrity.value` and setting
`audit.integrity.algorithm` and `audit.integrity.certificate` as
resource attributes. Supports RS256, RS512, ES256, EdDSA, and
HMAC-SHA256.
([#​50079](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50079),
[#​50080](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50080))
Key material can be loaded from a file or environment variables (PR 2a),
with Kubernetes Secret and OpenBao support to follow.

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `exporter/datadog`: The `container.image.tags` attribute is now mapped
to the `image_tag` attribute
([#​50864](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50864))
The Datadog exporter and connector already recognize the deprecated
`container.image.tag` resource attribute
  and map it to the Datadog `image_tag` container tag.
  They now also recognize the newer `container.image.tags` convention.
For now, only the first element of the array attribute will be
extracted.

- `extension/opamp`: Add an opt-in `reports_raw_config` setting to
additionally report the raw, unexpanded configuration alongside the
effective configuration
([#​44341](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/44341))
  When `reports_raw_config` is enabled (default: false, and requires the
  `reports_effective_config` capability), the extension reports the raw
configuration as authored, before environment variable and other
provider
references are expanded, under the `raw` key of the effective config
map. The
fully expanded effective configuration is unchanged and remains under
the
`""` (empty) key. This is disabled by default because raw configuration
files
may contain secrets written directly into them. Values sourced from
provider
references such as `${env:TOKEN}` retain their unexpanded form in the
raw
configuration, so they are not exposed, and fields using types meant for
opaque information (such as `configopaque.String`, commonly used for
password
fields) are redacted; consult your components' documentation or source
to
  verify which fields are automatically redacted.

- `internal/healthcheck`: Migrate to NotifyConfigSnapshot
([#​50924](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50924))

- `pkg/fileconsumer`: Move filelog.mtimeSortType featuregate to beta
([#​46635](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46635))

- `pkg/ottl`: Promote the `ottl.contexts.enableOTelColContext` feature
gate to stable.
([#​46437](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46437))
The `otelcol` context is now always available and the feature gate can
no longer be disabled.

- `pkg/ottl`: Allow `Concat` to accept slice values produced by paths
and converter expressions.
([#​27821](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/27821),
[#​38690](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/38690))

- `pkg/pdatatest`: Add a `double_value/precision<n>` operator to
`pmetricassert`, comparing double datapoint values rounded to n decimal
places
([#​48441](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48441))
Mirrors `pmetrictest`'s `IgnoreMetricFloatPrecision` for assertion
snapshots.
`n` must be between 0 and 15, and the operator cannot be combined with
an
  exact `double_value` on the same datapoint.

- `pkg/semconvtest`: Pin the default Weaver image version instead of
floating on the latest tag
([#​50915](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50915))
  Use WithVersion to select a different version, including latest.

- `pkg/stanza`: Add optional server authenticator support to the
`tcp_input` operator via a new `auth` configuration block.
([#​49339](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49339))
When `auth.authenticator` references a server auth extension, the
`tcp_input` operator authenticates each
accepted connection before reading logs, closing the connection if
authentication fails. The connection's
remote address is exposed to the authenticator through the `client.Info`
in the context. This is also
available to receivers built on the operator, such as `tcplogreceiver`
and `syslogreceiver`.

- `processor/resource_detection`: Populate `host.type` on GKE in the
`gcp` detector via the Compute API when the `host.type` resource
attribute is enabled.
([#​50662](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50662))
The machine type is not available from the GKE metadata server, so
fetching it requires
a Compute API call and the `compute.instances.get` permission (covered
by `roles/compute.viewer`).
If the permission is missing, the attribute is skipped and the failure
is logged. Disable the
  `host.type` resource attribute to avoid the API call.

- `receiver/faro`: Adopt the confighttp server defaults instead of zero
values.
([#​49316](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49316))

- `receiver/k8s_cluster`: Add the `k8s.statefulset.pod.available` metric
reporting the number of available pods
(StatefulSetStatus.availableReplicas) per stateful set.
([#​50345](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50345))

- `receiver/mongodb`: Add db.system.version resource attribute
([#​50710](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50710))
The mongodbreceiver now exposes the MongoDB version as a resource
attribute (db.system.version).
This follows the pattern used by mysqlreceiver and is disabled by
default.
The version is already fetched during connection initialization and is
now included in resource attributes.

- `receiver/mysql`: Add InnoDB redo log lsn and checkpoint-age metrics
to the mysqlreceiver.
([#​50650](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50650))

- `receiver/mysql`: Add MySQL health, query execution time, and active
session count metrics.
([#​50726](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50726))

- `receiver/mysql`: Add disabled-by-default InnoDB history list and
active transaction metrics.
([#​50380](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50380))

- `receiver/mysql`: Add support for AWS IAM authentication
([#​49044](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49044))

- `receiver/oracledb`: Add the `db.server.top_procedure` event,
reporting aggregated stored procedure performance metrics.
([#​50796](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50796))
Derived from `V$SQL` grouped by `PROGRAM_ID` and joined to
`DBA_PROCEDURES`, with deltas computed
across scrapes. Disabled by default; configure via the new
`top_procedure_collection` block
(`max_procedure_sample_count`, `top_procedure_count`,
`collection_interval`). Rows are fetched up to
`max_procedure_sample_count` and ranked in the collector by elapsed-time
delta, so a procedure that
is hot only in the current interval can reach the report even when its
lifetime totals are modest.
Correlates with `db.server.top_query` and `db.server.query_sample`
through the `oracledb.procedure_id`
  attribute.

- `receiver/oracledb`: Add `server.address` and `server.port` resource
attributes
([#​50724](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50724))
`server.address` and `server.port` are now emitted by default, so that
the monitored instance's network
location is available without extra configuration. When the receiver
connects over loopback (for example
`localhost` or `127.0.0.1`), `server.address` reports the host name of
the machine running the collector
rather than `localhost`, since the monitored instance is co-located with
the collector. This matches how
`service.instance.id` already resolves its host, and both attributes now
share one resolution path.
  `host.name` is unchanged.

A target whose port is absent or unparseable now resolves
`service.instance.id` to `host:1521/service`
instead of `unknown:1521/service`. Connection strings with no parseable
host at all, such as TNS
descriptors, still report `unknown:1521/service` and omit
`server.address`, since the instance's
  location cannot be determined.

To stop emitting the server attributes, disable them via
`resource_attributes.server.address.enabled: false`
  and `resource_attributes.server.port.enabled: false`.

- `receiver/postgresql`: Report non-relation locks in the
`postgresql.database.locks` metric
([#​49733](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49733))
Locks with a `lock_type` of `transactionid`, `virtualxid`, `object` or
`advisory` were dropped and are
now reported with an empty `relation`. Those on a transaction ID belong
to no database, so they carry
  an empty `db.namespace`.
This adds data points to a metric that is disabled by default. Every
backend holds one `virtualxid`
lock, so a sum over this metric grows by about the number of open
connections. Check any dashboard or
  alert that totals this metric.

- `receiver/sqlserver`: Add a new `db.server.query_plan` event that
carries `sqlserver.query_plan` on its own record, so an oversized
execution plan no longer risks dropping the lightweight query statistics
alongside it.
([#​50629](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50629))
`db.server.query_plan` is disabled by default, and while it is disabled
`db.server.top_query`
keeps carrying `sqlserver.query_plan` exactly as before. Enabling it
moves the plan off
`db.server.top_query` and onto the new event, joined back via
`sqlserver.query_hash` +
`sqlserver.query_plan_hash`. It is collected as part of top query
collection, so it does nothing
  unless `db.server.top_query` is also enabled.

- `receiver/sqlserver`: Report a loopback target as the collector's host
name in the `server.address` resource attribute.
([#​49885](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49885))
When the receiver connects over loopback (for example `server:
localhost` or `server: 127.0.0.1`),
`server.address` now reports the host name of the machine running the
collector rather than `localhost`.
A loopback target is only reachable when the monitored instance is
co-located with the collector, so the
collector host's name identifies the instance, whereas `localhost` would
be shared by every monitored host.

This matches how `service.instance.id` already resolves its host, and
the two now share one resolution
path, so they cannot disagree. `host.name` and `service.instance.id` are
otherwise unchanged, including
  the `host\instance` form used for a named instance.

- `receiver/sqlserver`: Add the `db.server.top_procedure` event,
reporting aggregated stored procedure statistics.

###
[`v1.22.0`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v1220)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/compare/v1.21.7...v1.22.0)

\===

This release supports Kafka 4.3 and 4.4, has a few new APIs, and has a
few
big internal improvements. In particular, I recommend checking out the
new
`StreamingCompression` option, as well as evaluating if you'd like to
use
`RackAwarePartitioning`. There are some behavior changes that you should
read
about below. The "next gen" rebalancer is now usable via the new
`ServerSideBalancer` option. It's had a few releases to shake out bugs
internally (via integration tests and LLM audits), but if you do
experience a
bug, please open an issue straightaway.

Some minor bug fixes (that were never reported) were found during the
implementation that are not worth mentioning.

kfake has also been significantly extended and I recommend checking out
the
new APIs, in particular:

- A new Fault type to make it easier to inject errors without Control
functions
- Group introspection cluster APIs
- BlackholeProduce and SyntheticFetch APIs for benchmarking / play
testing

My `kcl` CLI has been *significantly* expanded as well and is worth
checking
out. It supports essentially everything you can do with a cluster, and
now
allows you to run a full broker locally via `kcl fake` (in memory or a
dumb
disk backed localhost broker) - as well as setup the fake broker with
fault
injection. I've been running LLM audits and extensions to `kcl` in
particular
to try to shape it up to a "finalized" CLI shape. If you use it and have
ideas
for improvements, please open an issue.

#### Behavior changes

- **Rack aware group partition assignment (KIP-881) now requires
`BalanceRacks`.**
v1.21.0 enabled group balancers to assign partitions based on the rack
that
members were in if you used the range or sticky/cooperative-sticky
balancers.
Well, `Rack` is also used to opt into preferred read replica assignment
when fetching by the broker itself. These two decisions conflict with
each
other. Now, `BalanceRacks()` is required to opt into group balancers
using
the rack while balancing. The client warns when balancing if
`BalanceRacks`
  is on and the brokers have preferred read replicas enabled.

- **`ConsumeResetOffset` defaults to `RewindOffset(time.Minute)`**
rather
than `NewOffset().AtStart()`. **Setting only `ConsumeStartOffset` no
longer
sets `ConsumeResetOffset`**. I introduced `ConsumeStartOffset` a while
back
because it was really weird IMO to use a reset offset for both how a
consumer
starts *and* for how it recovers in the event of data loss or falling
behind.
They were bidirectional since introduction, but since start is newer and
much
less commonly used and you often don't want to recover from the start,
I've
removed the start -> reset mapping when you only set the start. I
recommend
reading the docs on both options for an updated understanding of when
and
how they apply. As well, I've introduced `RewindOffset(d)` which is
*only*
relevant to the reset offset (rewind by `d` duration from the last
consumed
offset on data loss we cannot exactly recover from) and
`LookbackOffset(d)`
  which is relevant to both options but more useful for the start offset
(start consuming `d` before the newest record; before Kafka 3.0 it is
`d`
before the current time). If a committed offset has fallen below the log
start, the first fetch answers `OFFSET_OUT_OF_RANGE` and the reset
offset
decides where to resume. Before, a start offset of `AtEnd` was copied
into
  the reset offset, so the consumer skipped to the end. Now, with the
  defaults, it resumes at the log start.
  **`ConsumeResetOffset`'s new default is `RewindOffset(time.Minute)`**.

- **Topic recreation is now a hard failure.** The client always
produces to and consumes from the first instance of a topic. If you
delete
and recreate a topic, the client refuses the new version: buffered
records
fail with `UNKNOWN_TOPIC_ID`, fetches stop, offsets from the old topic
cannot
be committed to the new one, and transactions on the old topic fail.
This
needs a broker that reports topic IDs (Kafka 2.8+). Previously, some
things
  in the client continued to accidentally work, and the behavior was
unreliable and usually not good. If you want your application to stay
alive
  across topic recreations, you can `PurgeTopicsFromClient` and, for
consumers, `AddConsumeTopics`. More details about topic recreation are
now in
  a new section in the README.

- **`MaxDecompressBatchBytes` now blocks decompression if a batch would
  decompress too large (default 1GiB)**. Fetches when consuming can only
specify to the broker "give me X bytes of batches", but they cannot
control
how large those batches decompress into. A hostile or buggy batch could
OOM
your program. Now, a batch over the limit causes the partition to enter
  a fatal state and return `ErrDecompressTooLarge` once from polling.
The application can recover by manually skipping the batch with
`SetOffsets`
(with the fields in the error; see the docs), or by restarting the
client
with a higher limit. This option does not apply to custom decompressors,
  but, custom decompressors can still return `ErrMaxDecompress` to stop
the partition. This option is also closely related to streaming
compression,
  which is described below.

#### Improvements

- **gzip now uses klauspost/compress** (same format). Its default level
is
1.7x faster than stdlib's with a slightly better ratio; klauspost's
default
maps to its level 5 where stdlib's mapped to 6, and level for level it
is
1.1x to 1.2x faster. `WithLevel(n)` now selects klauspost's level `n`,
so
  the bytes a given level produces differ from before.

- **The sticky balancers are now exactly optimal** on balance, then rack
placement (with `BalanceRacks`), then stickiness. Balancing was already
load optimal but had some very niche edge cases where maximal stickiness
  was not preserved, especially if balancing used racks. Rack placement
  outranks stickiness: turning `BalanceRacks` on in a running group
reassigns, at its next rebalance, every partition held by a member in a
  different zone from the partition's leader.

- Sticky balancing is much faster, most of all on rejoins and on groups
whose
members subscribe to different topics. Against v1.21.7: a rejoin of 100
members over 1600 topics of 100 partitions goes from 351ms to 24ms; a
regex
shaped group of 500 members over 20,000 topics from 176ms and 810MB to
12ms
and 9MB; 2001 members over 500 topics of 2000 partitions with one narrow
  subscriber from 3.4s to 0.3s. Fresh uniform balances are unchanged.

#### Features

##### Streaming compression

`StreamingCompression` is an opt-in producer option that compresses a
partition's backlog of batches together, bounded by their *compressed*
size.
By default a batch is cut at `ProducerBatchMaxBytes` measured on
uncompressed
records. Streaming compression will help reduce traffic to the broker
and
increase how effective compression actually is (by pulling more data in
at
once). A custom compressor makes this option a no-op.

The client is implemented such that each compression codec's worst case
overhead is tracked internally, which should avoid a compressed batch
ever
exceeding `ProducerBatchMaxBytes`. If this ever does happen, the client
discards the merge, logs a warning, disables streaming compression for
the
client going forward (records are still compressed batch by batch), and
asks
you to file an issue.

The client has a new option `MaxDecompressBatchBytes` to bound both (a)
how
much the producer can stuff into a merged batch (i.e. how much it will
decompress into), and (b) the maximum size a consumer will decompress a
batch
to; the consumer never decompresses past the bound (preventing a zip
bomb).
The default is 1GiB.

##### Rack aware producer partitioning (KIP-1123)

`RackAwarePartitioning` sends unkeyed records to partitions whose leader
is in
the client's `Rack` (which must also be set), falling back to all
partitions
when no leader is. Keyed records are never affected. Unlike the Java
client,
this works with any partitioner, since the eligible-broker filtering
happens
before your partitioner is consulted. Note that this option skews which
partitions receive records if your producers are not spread across racks
in
proportion to partition leaders.

##### ServerSideBalancer (KIP-848)

`ServerSideBalancer` opts into KIP-848 "next-gen" consumer groups, where
the
broker's group coordinator assigns partitions rather than the client.
This
requires Kafka 4.0+ and either a range or sticky / cooperative-sticky
balancer. This replaces the hidden `opt_in_kafka_next_gen_balancer_beta`
context key from v1.19.0; the key still works in this release and is
removed
in the next. The default remains the classic protocol, matching the Java
client. I still think the classic client side balancers are better (and
this
client's implementation is way faster than the Java client), but if you
want
to use server side balancing, it is strongly recommended to only use it
if
your cluster is Kafka 4.3+. Before 4.3 (before KIP-1251), an offset
commit
that races with a heartbeat epoch bump can fail with
`STALE_MEMBER_EPOCH`,
which the client cannot detect nor handle.

##### BalanceInfo for custom balancers

A balancer that implements `GroupMemberBalancerInfo` receives a
`BalanceInfo`
before balancing: the group, generation, leader member ID, and lazily
built
topic and broker metadata. `ConsumerBalancer` implements it, so
balancers
built on `NewConsumerBalancer` can call `Info()`. This allows, for
example, a
balancer that assigns every partition to the leader with the other
members as
hot standbys. Thanks
[@​michaelwilner](https://redirect.github.com/michaelwilner)!

###
[`v1.21.7`](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v1217)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/compare/v1.21.6...v1.21.7)

\===

A handful of bug fixes and improvements found by users and while working
on
v1.22. Rather than enumerating the relevant commits, you can check the
git log
between v1.21.6 and this release - there are many minor commits. As
well, kfake
has been improved significantly and has more API surface to aid in
writing
tests.

- A rare, very niche panic while producing has been fixed. Thanks
[@​PumpkinDemo](https://redirect.github.com/PumpkinDemo) for the
report, see
[#​1385](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/issues/1385)
for more details.

- If retention deleted the segment a consumer was reading, the
OffsetOutOfRange reset listed by the last consumed timestamp and could
skip
surviving records, or jump to the log end and skip everything. The reset
  now resumes at the log start when below it.

- Improved KIP-951 handling (the broker returning where a partition
should move
with the produce response if the partition changed leadership).
Previously, a
broker could return NotLeaderForPartition *and* hint the leader the
client
  was already using, at the same or an older epoch. These hints are now
  ignored and the client backs off, rather than spinning. Thanks
[@​3AceShowHand](https://redirect.github.com/3AceShowHand) for the
report and
  [@​jjj-n](https://redirect.github.com/jjj-n) for a fix, see
  [#​1412](https://redirect.github.com/twmb/franz-go/issues/1412).

- Rack aware balancers ignored rack for any topic the group leader did
not
itself consume. A client now loads the rack for *all* partitions in the
  group, even if the leader does not consume some of the topics.

- The metadata cache has been improved (there were a few cases where it
was
  emptied erroneously).

- Regex consuming now consistently never matches internal topics such as
`__consumer_offsets`. As well, the regex log no longer reports an
excluded
topic as both added and skipped (thanks
[@​lahsivjar](https://redirect.github.com/lahsivjar)).

- Decompression allocates less (thanks
[@​scunningham](https://redirect.github.com/scunningham)).
If you use pools, slices are now reliably returned if decompression
errors.

- The client now starts at a random seed broker rather than always the
first, so many clients starting at once no longer all hit the same seed.
  Thanks [@​chailuecha](https://redirect.github.com/chailuecha)!

- A producer that receives RequestTimedOut or
NotEnoughReplicasAfterAppend now
retries after the produce backoff rather than waiting for a metadata
refresh.

- A few other minor improvements and bug fixes.

[exporter/prometheus] Remove every stale series in a metric (#51289)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

When a scrape drops several series of the same metric at once, the
accumulator removes only one of them. The rest keep being served until
`metric_expiration` elapses, so `/metrics` reports label sets the source
stopped publishing, alongside the ones that replaced them.

Example:

before:
```
g{node="a",status="active"} 1
g{node="a",status="blocked"} 0
g{node="a",status="failed"} 0
g{node="a",status="failure_ignored"} 0
g{node="a",status="orphaned"} 0
```
after:
```
g{node="b",status="active"} 1
```
... the same five statuses on node b

**Expected**: `/metrics` serves the five `node="b"` series.

**Actual**: it serves the five `node="b"` series and four of the five
`node="a"` ones, for five minutes. Exactly one of the dropped series is
removed, and which one varies between runs.

My case is `ha_cluster_pacemaker_resources` from ha_cluster_exporter,
whose `node` and `role` labels both change when a cluster migrates a VM.
For up to five minutes the collector then reports the VM as running on
the node it left and as running on the node it arrived at, and my reader
trusting the exposition picks one of the two.
I had no problem as long as my reader was polling the exporter directly
and it started getting weird when I use the collector in between.

(with go 1.26) but passes with the fix.
The full `exporter/prometheusexporter` suite still passes.

samplers are surfaced today. Without those internal metrics, it's hard
to diagnose adaptive_throughput and adaptive_percentage sampler
performance.

`GetMetrics()` function. This PR expose those metrics as part of the
processor metrics

percentage, EMA throughput, windowed throughput). Confirms each
implements MetricsProvider, checks the expected map keys come back after

[receiver/prometheus] optimize scrape transaction performance (#51133)

#### Description

Part 1 of breaking down the Prometheus receiver scrape transaction
optimizations into smaller PRs (per
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/51133#issuecomment-5781544878).

This PR focuses on **changing pointer values to value types and
pre-allocating slices**, along with adding the `BenchmarkScrapePayload`
benchmark suite:

1. **Value-type `resourceKey` (`internal/transaction.go`)**: Return and
pass `resourceKey` (`struct{ job, instance string }`) by value in
`getJobAndInstance`, `initTransaction`, and `prepareLabels` instead of
allocating `*resourceKey` pointers on the heap for every scraped sample.
2. **Value-type `scrape.MetricMetadata` (`internal/metadata.go`,
`internal/metricfamily.go`, `internal/transaction.go`)**: Return value
structs instead of heap-allocated `*scrape.MetricMetadata` pointers in
`internalMetricMetadata` and `metadataForMetric`, and reuse a singleton
`emptyMetadataStoreInstance` when target metadata is disabled.
3. **Contiguous `[]dataPoint` slice pre-allocated to typical capacity
(`internal/metricfamily.go`, `internal/metricfamily_test.go`)**: Change
`metricGroup.complexValue` from `[]*dataPoint` to `[]dataPoint`,
pre-allocate slices to typical bucket/quantile counts
(`make([]dataPoint, 0, 8)` for histograms, `make([]dataPoint, 0, 4)` for
summaries), and sort points in-place via `slices.SortFunc`.
4. **Direct `pdata` slice writes with `EnsureCapacity`
(`internal/metricfamily.go`)**: Populate explicit bounds
(`ExplicitBounds()`) and bucket counts (`BucketCounts()`) directly into
`pdata` via `EnsureCapacity` + `Append` / `FromRaw` without allocating
intermediate `[]float64` / `[]uint64` slices, pre-allocate
`DataPoints()` / `QuantileValues()` capacities, and append directly via
`metrics.AppendEmpty()` in `appendMetric`.

[cmd/opampsupervisor] Preserve reported health across OpAMP client replacement (#51015)

#### Description

`startOpAMPClient` publishes `ComponentHealth{Healthy: false}` on every
client it creates. That's correct for the initial client, but
`onOpampConnectionSettings` reuses it to build the replacement client
after an accepted offer, silently overwriting the health of an
already-running, healthy Collector. Nothing corrects it afterward — the
Collector doesn't restate health, and the opamp extension only emits on
change — so the false report stands until the Collector process
restarts. Full failure mode and fleet impact are in #51009.

Affects only deployments with `accepts_opamp_connection_settings: true`
(default `false`) whose server sends offers.

**Fix:** a new `lastReportedHealth` field, written by
`Supervisor.SetHealth`, tracks what we last told the server. New clients
publish that instead of resetting to unhealthy. With nothing reported
yet (initial client), we still publish unhealthy — startup behavior is
unchanged. Whether that first publish should say "unknown" instead is
left to a separate issue per #51009.

`lastHealthFromClient` is deliberately not the source: it holds
agent-reported health only, clears on new config, and feeds
config-apply-timeout logic — after a process exit it can still say
"healthy," which would mask the exact failure this PR is fixing.

Side effect: the no-config and shutdown paths now go through `SetHealth`
too (previously called `s.opampClient.SetHealth` directly), so they
can't go stale and now also update the `supervisor.agent.health_status`
metric. Noted in the changelog.

**Scope:** this stops client replacement from destroying known health.
It does not let a fresh Supervisor learn the health of an
already-running Collector — there's no mechanism for that (Supervisor
never sends `ReportFullState`), which was question 1 in #51009 and is
explicitly out of scope here.

#### Link to tracking issue

Fixes #51009

#### Testing

`TestSupervisor_healthSurvivesOpAMPClientReplacement` (new):
- healthy agent survives a client replacement
- a newer Supervisor-detected failure isn't overwritten by an older
agent-reported healthy (also seeds `lastHealthFromClient`, so it can't
pass vacuously)
- retained health is copied — later mutation can't reach the replacement
client
- no health yet → still starts unhealthy
- each replacement seeds from the most recent report, not the first
- health survives a failed replacement and its rollback — when the new
client can't be created, `onOpampConnectionSettings` retries
`startOpAMPClient` with the old settings, and both attempts must seed

`TestSupervisorOpAMPConnectionSettings` now asserts the health the *new*
server receives after the offer. Fails on `main`, passes with this
change; no existing assertion removed. `initialServer` gained an
`OnMessage` to observe health — it returns the same empty
`ServerToAgent` opamp-go's `defaultOnMessage` returns for a nil
callback, so traffic is unchanged.

`cmd/opampsupervisor` unit suite and e2e pass, `-race` included.

#### Documentation

None — no config or user-facing behavior changes. Changelog covers the
fix and the metric change.

**Breaking changes**: OTel mode now needs ES 9.6.0+; users on older
clusters need mapping.allowed_modes: [ecs].

The PR supports ingesting with OpenTelemetry profiles through the `otel`
mapping mode (default), using the datastreams OTel schema. New changes
for the profiles otel mode:

- No symbolization is supported at the moment, unsymbolized queues not
needed.

`otelserializer/serializeprofiles/model.go`: the new OTel profiling
serializer. Index names get the .otel-default suffix, documents use OTel
field names (resource.attributes.*, @timestamp), no ecs.version, no
symbolization queue.
- `transform.go` is not new logic:
otelserializer/serializeprofiles/transform.go is the ECS one minus
EcsVersion/ProjectID/sym-queue, plus @timestamp on
stacktraces/stackframes.

everything identical between the two modes moved to internal/serializer/

feat(adaptivetailsampling): add explicit root-scoped fingerprint selectors (#51306)

#### Description

Adds explicit root-scoped fingerprint selectors so a fingerprint can
read the root span's resource, scope or span attributes specifically.
`root.` becomes a position prefix that composes with the existing
origins, giving `root.resource.attributes[...]`,
`root.scope.attributes[...]`, `root.span.attributes[...]` and
`root.any.attributes[...]`. `root.any.` is the root-span union,
mirroring the top-level `any.`.

Bare `root.attributes[...]` is dropped in favour of naming the origin.
It currently reads the root span's span attributes only, so
`root.attributes["service.name"]` returns `<missing>` for the
resource-level service that people actually want. Requiring the origin
turns that into a parse error pointing at
`root.resource.attributes[...]` rather than an unitended wrong match.

This is a breaking change for existing `root.` selectors, which is
acceptable at development stability.

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
This PR fixes a flaky test that broke its consume loop on the first
non-short token. Because the short and long files are read by separate
goroutines racing for an unbuffered sink, a long-file token can arrive
first, so the loop could break having never observed the short file's
token. The short reader may not have reached its EOF/`delete()` yet, and
the 100ms `EventuallyWithT` assertion then relied on that goroutine
being scheduled in time, which fails under CI scheduling jitter.

A reader deletes its file synchronously before emitting the file's final
batch of tokens, so observing the short file's token guarantees the
short file is already deleted. This PR consumes until both the short
line and at least one long line are observed, then asserts deletion
deterministically.

[receiver/kafka]: stop processing a fetched batch on revocation or shutdown (#50836)

#### Description

Two independent things cancel a partition context: a rebalance revoking
the partition, and receiver shutdown. In both cases the receiver kept
walking the rest of the already-fetched batch. Each remaining record was
marked, then failed on the dead context and lost() commits those marks.
A marked-and-committed record is never redelivered, so the rest of the
batch is gone even though nothing processed it.
The loop now stops at the cancellation. Unprocessed records stay
unmarked and are redelivered: to the partition's next owner after a
revocation, or on the next run of the same consumer group after a
shutdown. That redelivery is what keeps the receiver at-least-once.

Two further changes:
- The interrupted record is no longer marked under
message_marking.on_error: true. A cancelled partition context means the
record was cut short, not that the pipeline refused it, so the on-error
config no longer applies and marking it would commit a record nothing
processed. This is a separate leak from the one above.
- Shutdown behaviour changes: records fetched but not delivered at
shutdown are redelivered on the next run instead of being committed.
That is why TestConsumerShutdownConsuming changed, the assertions now
count only what was actually delivered.

Fixes

[receiver/awss3] add support for day-partitioned time-slices (#51038)

#### Description
The awss3receiver currently supports partition naming formats only
including minutes or hours (i.e.
my-partition/2026/09/15/1200/some_blob). The default use-case for
accessing s3 buckets is covered by this, but some off-meta setups may
not partition by hour or minute resolution at the partition-level (i.e.
my-partition/2026/09/15/1200_some_blob or even
my-partition/2026/09/15/some_blob).

This uses the existing function for finding the timestep and just
expands its resolution to support day-level granularity if minutes and
hours are missing from the partition format (i.e.
my-partition/%Y/%m/%d). Behavior prior to this would return "no time
step found for partition format ..." if adding a minute or hour did not
increase the partition format. This adds a third step (literally third,
as it's tried last) which adds 24 hours in attempt to move the partition
format.

Prior behavior for seeking the timestep for a partition-format without
hours or minutes was...
Partition format: my-partition/%Y/%m/%d
Example start time: my-partition/2026/09/15
... determineTimestep() adds 1 minute to see if start time has changed
... determineTimestep() adds 1 hour to see if start time has changed
... nothing has changed start time, no step can be provided, err out

The new behavior simply adds one try to the flow:
... determineTimestep() adds 1 minute to see if start time has changed
... determineTimestep() adds 1 hour to see if start time has changed
... determineTimestep() adds 24 hours to see if start time has changed
... start time has changed (for our example) with a step of 24 hours,
return that timestep

#### Link to tracking issue
No issue exists for this

#### Testing
The prior testcase in Test_determineTimestep tested certain partition
formats against the returned timestep from the function. Originally it
held three cases, one for testing the minute step, one for testing the
hour step, and one for testing failures to find steps. A new case was
added after the hour step to test for day steps, with the expected
returned timestep for a partition format of "year=%Y/month=%m/day=%d" as
24 hours. Because this partition format was the partition format used
for the failure test case (which will now succeed), the failure test's
partition format was moved down in resolution to "year=%Y/month=%m"
which should not result in a timestep and instead return an error.

#### Documentation
The existing documentation still adequately describes the behavior of
the receiver. This simply enables further control using the existing
levers in place.

[processor/delta_to_cumulative] Fix exponential histogram bucket limit rounding (#50923)

#### Description

Delta-to-cumulative aggregation can produce exponential histograms with
161 or 162 buckets despite its 160-bucket limit. `Limit()` truncates
both bucket-range endpoints toward zero, so its predicted size can be
smaller than the result of `Collapse()` and `Merge()`.

For example, the range `[1, 321)` contains 320 buckets. The current
calculation predicts 160 buckets after one downscale step, but the
actual result spans indices 0 through 160 and needs 161 buckets. Ranges
crossing index zero can exceed the limit by two buckets.

This change rounds the lower index down and the exclusive upper index
up, including negative indices. It makes scale selection match the
existing bucket-merging algorithm. Observation counts are preserved, and
the tests check that ranges which fit do not receive unnecessary
downscaling.

I encountered this while using the Collector for AWS Lambda in a
production workload handling billions of requests, where oversized
histograms were rejected by AWS. The regression tests use small
synthetic inputs to isolate the defect; they do not replay the rejected
production payloads. The faulty calculation was present in v0.151.0 and
is still present on the main branch used for this PR.

#### Link to tracking issue

No separate issue. This PR includes regression tests that reproduce the
defect.

#### Testing

Eight regression cases exercise `Limit()`, `Downscale()`, and `Merge()`
together. They cover positive and negative offsets, a range crossing
zero, repeated downscaling, and ranges that fit the limit. They also
check that both observations remain in the merged histogram.

- Before the fix, five of the eight cases fail: four produce 161 buckets
and one produces 162. The three control cases pass.
- After the fix, all eight cases pass.
- `make test` in `processor/deltatocumulativeprocessor`: all 115
component tests pass with the race detector enabled.
- `make lint` in the same directory: passes.

#### Documentation

Added a changelog entry and a code comment explaining the rounding
rules. No configuration or public API changes.

#### Description

breakdown (split from #51133):

scraped series do not carry exemplars (and `Summary` metrics never

and `addHistogramDatapoint` allows `Append` to attach exemplars directly
via `curMF.addExemplar(seriesRef, exemplar)`.

[chore][receiver/prometheus] avoid scope map and label filter allocations when series have no scope labels (#51443)

#### Description

Part 3 of the Prometheus receiver scrape transaction optimization
breakdown
(https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/51133#issuecomment-5781544878).

Most Prometheus scrape series do not carry `otel_scope_*` labels.
Previously, every scraped sample:
1. Allocated a `pcommon.NewMap()` and computed `xhash.MapHash(attrs)` in
`getScopeID` even when no `otel_scope_*` attribute labels were present.
2. Scanned all series labels a second time in
`getSortedNotUsefulLabelsForSeries` (and allocated a `seen` map when
scope labels were present) to compute the series reference hash.

This PR:
- Updates `getScopeID` to check `strings.HasPrefix(lbl.Name,
prometheus.ScopeLabelPrefix)` first, lazily allocate `attrs =
pcommon.NewMap()` and compute `xhash.MapHash(attrs)` only when extra
`otel_scope_*` attribute labels exist, and return `hasScopeLabels`.
- Passes `getSortedNotUsefulLabels(mtype)` directly to
`ls.HashWithoutLabels` in `getSeriesRef` when `!hasScopeLabels`,
avoiding a redundant second pass over `ls`.
- Removes the redundant `seen` map allocation in
`getSortedNotUsefulLabelsForSeries` since `labels.Labels` is already
sorted/deduplicated and `base` contains no `otel_scope_*` labels.

[exporter/loadbalancing] Add randomness (ot=rv) routing key (#49666)

#### Description

Adds a `randomness` routing key to the loadbalancing exporter that
routes spans by the OpenTelemetry randomness value - the explicit
`ot=rv` from the span's W3C tracestate when present or a randomness
value derived from the trace ID per the sampling specification.

Implementation notes:

- The existing single-pass `consumeTracesByID` path is generalised to
`consumeTracesPerSpan`, taking an identifier function; `traceID` routing
behaviour is unchanged.
- The backend is resolved once per trace ID within a batch, so
tracestate parsing and ring hashing are amortised across a trace's
spans.
- Spans whose tracestate is present but unparseable fall back to trace
ID randomness and are counted in a new optional
`otelcol_loadbalancer_randomness_tracestate_unparseable` counter (only
produced when the key is in use, following the kafkaexporter
optional-metric pattern).
- `randomness` is traces-only; the logs and metrics exporters reject it
at startup as an unsupported key.

#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #49660

#### Testing

- Added unit tests for the identifier extraction
- Integration-style test asserting two traces with different trace IDs
but a shared `rv` land on the same backend while an rv-less trace routes
by its own trace ID randomness
- Existing traceID-routing tests (multiple trace IDs, consumeWG leak on
resolve error) now exercise the generalised per-span path

#### Documentation

- README: `randomness` is added to the routing table with a full
description under `routing_key`
- New optional metric documented via mdatagen (`documentation.md`
regenerated)

[receiver/mysql] Add a db.server.query_plan event for the execution plan (#51335)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

The `db.server.top_query` and `db.server.query_sample` events currently
carry the statement's execution plan directly in their`
mysql.query_plan` attribute. Because these plans are output from EXPLAIN
FORMAT=json (containing per-table access details, costs, used columns,
and conditions), they grow with join count/subquery depth and can
dominate the record size.

When a combined record exceeds downstream buffer or transport limits,
both the metrics and execution plans are lost. Furthermore, operators
cannot shed execution plans while keeping statistics without employing
complex transform processors.
This PR adds a single `db.server.query_plan `event (disabled by default)
to hold execution plans separately.

[chore] tailsampling: Improve processor benchmarks (#51538)

#### Description
`BenchmarkProcessorThroughput` generated a new batch inside the timed
loop, so about half of all allocated bytes came from the benchmark
itself, and its spans had no attributes, which understated the per-span
copy cost that dominates ingest in real traffic. It also only covered
one shard.

The intent is a reliable baseline for any future performance work, so
each change can show its effect with `benchstat`.

Each producer now builds one realistic batch (resources with k8s
attributes, several scopes, span attributes, mixed trace sizes, errors)
and only rewrites its trace IDs per iteration. This is safe because
`ConsumeTraces` copies its input before returning.

It runs with `num_shards` 1 / 4 to better measure the sharded path, and
reports `sampled-spans/op` and `consume-calls/op` to measure how much
reaches the next consumer and how often it is called.

Last, adds `BenchmarkProcessorMemory`, which reports the heap retained
per trace and per span while traces wait for a decision. This is what

[receiver/mongodb] Fix replica set secondary connections never being established (#50653)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

The MongoDB receiver never uses a replica set secondary. Two call sites
type-assert a nested BSON
document to `bson.M`, which the Go driver does not produce.

The driver's default registry maps a BSON embedded document to `bson.D`
(`RegisterTypeMapEntry(TypeEmbeddedDocument, tD)`). `RunCommand` decodes
only the **top level** into
`bson.M`; every document nested inside it decodes as `bson.D`. Both
assertions therefore always
fail, and both fail silently.

**1. `findSecondaryHosts` (`scraper.go`) discovers no secondaries.**

```go
for _, member := range members {
	m, ok := member.(bson.M)
	if !ok {
		continue    // always taken
	}
	...
}
```

The loop `continue`s on every member and the function returns `(nil,
nil)`, so nothing is logged and
`start()` reads the empty result as "this deployment has no
secondaries". `secondaryClients` stays
empty for the receiver's lifetime, and `scrapeLogs` collects
`db.server.query_sample` events from
the scraped instance only.

**A second instance of the same mistake is deliberately left alone.**
`recordOperationsRepl`
(`metrics.go`) does `status["opcountersRepl"].(bson.M)` for the same
reason and fails the same way.
It stays dead after this change, so `mongodb.operation.repl.count`
continues to read the scraped
instance exactly as it does today. It is not repaired here because
repairing it correctly is a
redesign, not a bug fix — see the follow-ups below. The accepted cost is
that `recordOperationsRepl`
now issues one `serverStatus` per secondary per scrape whose result is
discarded.

Both sites were introduced by the same commit, `2605e8cb885` (#37517) —
one mistaken model of the
driver's decode shape, two call sites. A scan of every nested-BSON type
assertion in the receiver's
non-test code finds no third instance: the rest target `bson.A` on
arrays, which is correct, or check
both container types (`dig` / `digBsonD`).

**The fix.** Site 1 reads the member fields through the receiver's
existing `getValue[T]` helper,
which resolves `bson.M`, `bson.D`, and `map[string]any` — the same
helper the `$currentOp` handling
already uses. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: only members in state
`SECONDARY` are returned, and a
member without a name is still skipped.

**Hardening the path this makes live.** Populating `secondaryClients`
for the first time also makes
`Config.ClientOptions(secondary=true)` reachable, and it returned before
two settings the primary
path applies:

- **TLS.** Secondary clients would have connected in plaintext, so on a
TLS-required deployment the
  fix would have been silently inert.
- **An operation timeout.** The secondary branch set only
`SetConnectTimeout`. A secondary that
connects but stops responding would stall the scrape indefinitely,
because `scraperhelper`'s
`Timeout` defaults to `0` — the scrape context carries no deadline.
`SetTimeout` bounds a single
operation and, per the driver's contract, defers to an operation context
deadline when one exists,
  so a configured scrape timeout still wins.

The members-format error a few lines above site 1 reports `expected type
primitive.A`. `primitive.A`
is a v1 driver type that no longer exists after the v2 migration, so the
message is corrected here.

No configuration change is required, and no metric or attribute is
added, removed, or renamed.

**Known follow-ups, deliberately out of scope.** Making discovery work
surfaces pre-existing limits
in the discovery feature itself. None is a regression from this change,
and each is better reviewed on
its own:

- `recordOperationsRepl`'s furthest-ahead-secondary selection has the
same `bson.M` assertion and has
never executed. Simply repairing the assertion would emit incorrect
telemetry: the data point is
emitted under the *scraped instance's* resource, so another member's
counters would carry the wrong
`server.address`; and `mongodb.operation.repl.count` is `sum` /
`cumulative` / `monotonic: true`
over a per-process counter, so a source host that changes between
scrapes would make the series
decrease. Doing it properly means emitting per-secondary series under
each secondary's own resource,
the way `scrapeLogsFromClient` already emits query samples. That is a
design change and needs its
  own issue.
- Secondaries are discovered once in `start()` and never refreshed, so a
failover or membership change
  is not picked up until the collector restarts.
- All three scraper instances (metrics, query-sample logs, top-query)
run discovery, but only the
  query-sample scraper reads `secondaryClients`.
- The primary client sets `SetConnectTimeout` but not `SetTimeout`, so
the stall bounded here for
secondaries is still possible on the primary. Unchanged from `main`, but
asymmetric.
- On `mongodb+srv` with `tls.insecure`, the secondary branch may not
preserve the scheme's implied TLS.

[receiver/postgresql] Add a db.server.query_plan event for the execution plan (#51302)

<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
Execution plans embedded in `db.server.top_query` can be large payloads:
`postgresql.query_plan` holds the full `EXPLAIN` output for the query,
so it can dwarf the small numeric and identifier attributes carried
alongside it. When several land in one batch the combined size can
exceed transport/buffer limits, dropping the whole batch and losing the
lightweight query statistics along with the oversized plan.

`db.server.query_plan` is disabled by default, so default output is
unchanged. When it is enabled, the plan is reported on the new event,
joined back to its query via `postgresql.queryid` and `db.namespace`
(queryid alone is not a safe join key - `pg_stat_statements` scopes it
per-database via `dbid`, so two databases can share a `queryid` for
structurally identical queries), and `db.server.top_query` reports
`postgresql.query_plan` removed from the record rather than empty. The
event is sourced from the same top query collection, so it does nothing
unless `db.server.top_query` is enabled too, and enabling it without
`db.server.top_query` is a configuration error.

[receiver/vcenter] Add proxy_url for per-receiver proxy configuration (#51191)

#### Description

`vcenterreceiver` can only be proxied through the process-wide
`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables, because govmomi's SOAP
client inherits its proxy from `http.DefaultTransport`. That means one
proxy per collector process, so several vCenters that each sit behind
their own proxy cannot be scraped from one collector.

This adds a `proxy_url` field so each receiver instance can use its own
proxy. It accepts `http`, `https`, `socks5` and `socks5h` URLs. When
unset, nothing changes: the environment variables still apply.
